Within-group task contrasts (parametric memory load linear contrasts and task vs baseline) are reported for a healthy adult sample (n=12). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and does not trigger any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (Go/No-go), which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain activation maps (cluster-thresholded %AUC maps and between-/within-group voxelwise comparisons), and also reports within-group contrasts (inhibition trials versus baseline and within-group Time1 vs Time2 comparisons). Partial slice coverage (19 sagittal slices) is acceptable under the review rules because analyses are voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted. Results are presented as cluster locations/BA and statistical comparisons. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive control / cognitive flexibility). It reports a group-level, voxelwise within-group contrast (task switch vs task repetition) across 16 healthy participants, with thresholded z-maps and cluster significance testing; results are presented in figures and a table of activation foci (coordinates). Although slice coverage was limited (seven slices), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, which meets the partial-brain allowance. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses and outcomes. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (provided content includes title, abstract, and metadata but not full article methods/results/discussion). Based on the abstract, the study is an fMRI task-based investigation of selective letter generation contrasted with an alphabetical recitation control, indicating a within-group task contrast. The task falls within executive function domains (verbal working memory, response selection/inhibition). The abstract reports "significant and extensive foci of activation" across multiple cerebral regions, which implies voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked activation results are reported in the article text. No evidence in the provided content suggests ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical status. Therefore, the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. Because the full text is incomplete, confidence is moderate. Full text should be obtained to verify voxelwise analytic details and confirm whole-brain coverage and group-level statistical maps.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly tests cognitive control processes in a social-evaluative paradigm. It reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (inconsistent vs. consistent actions) and group-level voxelwise ANOVAs, along with ROI analyses and stereotactic coordinates. Although slice coverage was limited (17 contiguous slices), analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-only, satisfying the partial-brain allowance. Participants were healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET activation study of planning (Tower of London), an executive function domain. It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (categorical task-minus-rest and correlational analyses with task complexity) for both Parkinson's patients and controls, with whole-brain coverage and tables/figures of coordinates. Within-group task contrasts are reported (task vs rest; complexity covariate), and results are presented in text, tables and figures. Participants include a clinical sample and controls. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that manipulates executive demand (two-back vs one-back; source vs item memory) and explicitly investigates executive control. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (conjunctions, thresholded maps and coordinates) and within-group high-vs-low load contrasts. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Stroop task (inhibition), an established executive function paradigm. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (incongruent > congruent and incongruent > control) with whole-brain cluster-corrected results and peak coordinates in tables. Participants (n=9) and methods are described in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion), and whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported, satisfying the review’s requirements. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go), which falls squarely within executive function (inhibition). Methods report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM99 analyses and thresholded SPM maps with tables of significant clusters/coordinates. Multiple within-group contrasts are reported (go vs visual control, go/no-go vs visual control, go/no-go vs go), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy volunteers (acceptable per I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The provided full text is incomplete (only references and citation metadata are present). Title indicates a PET study of sustained attention (vigilance), so I5 (PET task-based study) and I6 (task within executive domain: vigilance) appear satisfied. However core article content (methods, results, group-level voxelwise analyses) is missing, so I cannot verify I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps) or I8 (within-group task contrast). No exclusion criteria from the list are clearly met based on the available content, but because essential information to confirm required inclusion criteria is absent, the study must be excluded pending complete full text.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) — an executive function domain. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM96 group map showing main effect of load), provides coordinates/tables and figures of activation, and reports within-group task contrasts (main effect of load and contrasts across 0B/1B/2B/3B and correlation of activation with performance). It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes within-group contrasts for a participant group. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (task switching using Stroop/reverse-Stroop), reporting group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses of within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; Stroop, RS-Early, RS-Late) with whole-brain coverage and tables/figures of results. The methods, results, and discussion are complete in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for an executive-function task activation meta-analysis and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical).

The abstract describes an fMRI study using a parametric spatial n-back (working memory) task with group-level analyses reporting load-sensitive and load-insensitive activations in dorsolateral prefrontal, parietal cortex, and anterior cingulate. This meets the review objective and clearly satisfies: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory domain), I8 (within-group task contrast / parametric load effects), and I9 (healthy volunteer participant group). The abstract also describes voxelwise spatially-resolved activity consistent with whole-brain analysis, supporting I7. However, only title/abstract/metadata were provided here (full text not available), so I cannot fully verify exact analytic details (e.g., explicit statement of voxelwise group-level statistical maps, coordinate tables or figures). Recommend retrieval of the full article for final verification. Full text is incomplete in this submission.

This is an event-related fMRI study of executive control processes (Go/No-go inhibition, oddball target detection, response selection). It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects ANOVAs and whole-brain exploratory analyses (conjunction, disjunction) with coordinate tables and figures, and presents within-group task contrasts (low- vs high-frequency events; error vs correct). The full article (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. Therefore it meets all stated inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title and abstract-level information). While the abstract confirms this is an fMRI study of working memory in schizophrenia (meeting I5, I6), reports within-group task effects (I8), includes clinical participants (I9), and reports results in text/figures (I10), I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. All inclusion criteria must be verified; because I7 cannot be established and the full article (methods/results) is not available, the study cannot be confirmed as eligible. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) apply based on available information.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (n-back tasks) in children and adults with FASD and controls. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain (partial coverage with 21 slices) SPM analyses including group-level one-sample t test maps and within-group subtraction contrasts (Blank minus Simple; One-back minus Simple). Results are presented as group activation maps and tables of regions/Z-scores. These elements satisfy: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I7 (group-level voxelwise maps; partial-brain acquisition still qualifies), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant groups), and I10 (results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The provided full text appears to be only an abstract/summary (fulltext_incomplete=true) so key methodological details cannot be confirmed. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI study confirmed), I6 (task involves go/no-go/inhibition component consistent with executive function), I9 (participant group acceptable). Could not confirm crucial inclusion criteria: I7 (no clear statement that group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked maps are reported), I8 (no clear within-group task contrast reported — the abstract emphasizes between-group comparisons), I10 (uncertain whether whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) can be definitively applied from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify voxelwise within-group activations required for inclusion, so I exclude pending access to complete article.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (black faces vs baseline/white faces) and reports coordinates (satisfies I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the in-scanner task was a spatial location detection task (press left/right) while viewing faces, not an established executive function task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study probes executive-control brain regions indirectly (correlating face-evoked activity with a separate, out-of-scanner Stroop inhibitory task), but it does not assess executive function using a task-based paradigm in the scanner. Therefore it fails I5 and I6 and must be excluded. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]) ; Inclusion criteria met: I7, I8, I9, I10 ; Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5, I6.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (task switching) that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses. The paper performs voxelwise regressions of pretrial BOLD predicting RT and paired t tests contrasting switch versus repeat coefficients across subjects, fulfilling a within-group task contrast. Methods, results, and figures/tables present whole-brain statistical maps and ROI/ICA follow-ups; participant sample is a within-group healthy adult cohort. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures described) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation that includes the Go/No-go paradigm (response inhibition), which falls squarely within established executive function domains (inhibition). Analyses were performed voxelwise at the group level using SPM2 random-effects second-level models, and within-group task contrasts are reported (No-go vs Go; Loss vs No-loss; Aversive vs Neutral). Whole-brain results are presented (thresholding, clusters, tables/figures), and tables/figures of coordinates are described. Participants are healthy volunteers (acceptable). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (e.g., WM > control; spatial > object), within-group task contrasts, and voxelwise significance thresholds with cluster correction. Results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. It therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and is empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). (a) Exclusion criteria met: none ([]). (b) Inclusion criteria clearly met from abstract: I5 (task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/Stroop), I6 (task falls within inhibition/executive function domain). (c) Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed due to incomplete full text: I7 (cannot verify presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis or reported voxelwise maps), I8 (cannot confirm a within-group task contrast is reported in a group-level voxelwise analysis), I10 (cannot confirm whether whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/figures/tables). Because core methods/results are missing, I cannot verify required voxelwise within-group analyses; therefore the study is excluded pending retrieval of the full text.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group contrasts (2-back > 0-back) for both patients and controls, and performs whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (non-parametric SnPM) with coordinates and tables/figures of activation peaks. Results are reported at group level across the whole brain. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

This is an empirical fMRI study of planning (Tower of London), reporting voxelwise, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (task vs rest and load levels) with coordinates/tables and within-group contrasts for males and females. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function imaging (planning) and provides whole-brain, within-group statistical maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm (Montreal Card-Sorting Task) that probes executive functions (planning and cognitive flexibility/set-shifting). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with multiple task contrasts (e.g., retrieval with shift vs control; retrieval with shift vs retrieval without shift), provides voxel coordinates/peaks and thresholded statistical maps, and includes healthy adult participants. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the provided full text is complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition using the stop-signal task (an established inhibition executive-function paradigm). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (whole-brain contrasts and tables/figures) including within-group task contrasts (stop > go; stop success > stop error), and provides voxel coordinates and corrected results. Participants are healthy adult males; analyses include whole-brain and ROI/SVC but are not limited to ROI-only. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). From the abstract, the study is an fMRI task-based investigation of working memory, so it appears to meet I5 (fMRI task study) and I6 (working memory domain). However, the full article (methods, results, group-level voxelwise maps, and specific contrasts) is not available in the supplied content, so I cannot verify I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), or I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures). Because these required inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are known to be met based on the available content.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of the Stroop color-word interference task (inhibition/cognitive control), which clearly falls within executive function/inhibition. The study reports voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (pixel-by-pixel t-tests, correlation analyses, and group composite t-tests) contrasting incongruent versus congruent trials (a within-group task contrast). Although acquisition used a limited number of slices, the analysis is voxelwise (not ROI-restricted), and partial-brain coverage is acceptable per criteria. Results are reported in text, figures, and tables (coordinates and composite maps). Participants are healthy adults and at least one within-group contrast is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded under E6: this is a computational/modeling paper that does not report original human fMRI/PET task-based empirical data or group-level voxelwise activation maps. The article describes an integrate-and-fire network model reproducing single-neuron and fMRI-like signals for working memory tasks, but provides no within-group task contrasts or whole-brain statistical maps from participants. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (addresses working memory domain). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no original fMRI/PET task-based study reported), I7 (no group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I9 (no participant group analyses reported), I10 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Full text appears incomplete (abstract/summary only).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly manipulates and measures executive resources (planning/decision-making and working memory) during sentence disambiguation. It meets I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive/cognitive-control processes), I6 (tasks tap established executive domains: working memory and planning/decision-making), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise SPM group-level analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., less-consistent vs more-consistent; with-WM vs without-WM), I9 (within-group contrasts on a healthy adult sample reported), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and appendices. Thus the study should be included.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), which falls squarely within executive function (inhibition). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials; one-sample t test across 24 subjects) with whole-brain analyses and thresholded statistical maps and coordinate tables/figures. Additional between-group (short vs long SSRT) voxelwise analyses and ROI correlations are also reported. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable), and results are reported as tables/figures with coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory with distraction and reports within-group contrasts, but analyses are ROI-based within individual anatomies without any group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise group analyses. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (only ROI analyses reported, no voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrasts comparing distraction conditions), I9 (acceptable participant group). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete.

Full text is incomplete: only title and abstract provided (no methods, results, or full analyses), so essential methodological details cannot be verified. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study) and I6 (tasks within executive domains: working memory and attention/vigilance). Inclusion criteria not verifiable / not met from provided content: I7 (cannot confirm existence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I8 (cannot confirm that a within-group task contrast is reported as a voxelwise analysis), I10 (cannot confirm format/extent of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on available text. Because core article content (methods/results/discussion) is missing, the study is excluded pending a complete full text to confirm I7 and I8. Fulltext_incomplete=true.

Exclusion: E6. This article is a non-empirical commentary/review summarizing Furey et al. and other PET/fMRI studies; it does not present original human neuroimaging data, methods, or voxelwise group-level activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: none (no original task-based fMRI/PET results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an empirical fMRI/PET study reporting original data), I6 (although working memory is discussed, the paper does not present task-based data), I7 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported in this article), I9 (no within-group activation contrasts provided for any participant group in this paper), I10 (no primary whole-brain results reported in tables/figures as original data). Full text appears complete for a commentary (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the stop-signal paradigm to probe response inhibition (an executive function). The manuscript includes full introduction, methods, results, and discussion. It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., StopInhibit vs Go; Go vs null) with group-level mixed-effects analyses and cluster correction; coordinate tables and maps are described. Tasks clearly fall within the inhibition domain. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/No-Go), which is an established executive-function domain (inhibition). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and contrasts are reported (No-Go vs Oddball within placebo and drug conditions; placebo vs THC/CBD), with tables of coordinates and cluster-level inference. At least one within-group task contrast is provided. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI Stroop task study assessing response inhibition (an executive function) with voxelwise group-level analyses and within-group task contrasts reported. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise statistical mapping (time-course p-maps, group and within-group contrasts) and provides results in figures/tables for both pathological gamblers and healthy controls. Partial slice coverage is present but voxelwise analyses were conducted, which meets the meta-analysis allowance for partial-brain acquisitions. Core article sections (methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of a numerical Stroop task that probes interference control/inhibition (an executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (SPM2; random-effects second-level analyses) with activation tables/coordinates and baseline and conjunction contrasts. Within-group task contrasts (activation blocks minus rest; simple contrasts per group used for masking) are reported, satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Partial-brain acquisition (24 axial slices) is permissible per criteria because voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise activation maps and a 3×3 ANOVA (group × memory load) with clusterwise inference, as well as within-group task contrasts (each memory load vs baseline) and group-specific activation maps and tables/figures. Participant groups include patients, unaffected relatives, and healthy controls. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This article is a methods/protocol paper that describes the counting Stroop task and how to implement it in fMRI/PET studies, but it does not present original empirical, group-level voxelwise neuroimaging results. Inclusion met: I6 (task falls within executive function/cognitive control - inhibition/interference). Inclusion not met: I5 (paper is not an empirical fMRI/PET study reporting original activation data), I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps are reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast/results are reported). Exclusion applied: E6 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete as a protocol, but it does not provide the necessary empirical activation maps/within-group contrasts required for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Stroop task (a cognitive control/inhibition executive function task) with task-based contrasts. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects GLM analyses and t-tests, thresholded and corrected for cluster size, and provides within-group task contrasts (controls and relatives) with coordinates/tables and figures showing whole-brain activations (e.g., ACC, DLPFC). Partial-slice differences are reported but analyses are voxelwise across acquired slices. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based N-back working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports within-group voxelwise analyses (2-back > 0-back) at the group level, including whole-brain second-level one-sample t-tests and multiple-regression voxelwise maps, with coordinates and tables/figures. Results include whole-brain activation maps (Table 2, Figs. 1–3) and voxelwise statistical results (including small-volume correction applied post hoc). Participants are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion, and provides voxelwise task activation contrasts appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using the color–word Stroop task (an inhibition/cognitive-control executive function task). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (e.g., incongruent > congruent; congruent+incongruent > neutral) with whole-brain thresholding and tables/figures of activations. Although acquisition had limited slice coverage (13 slices), analyses are voxelwise and reported across the imaged volume, satisfying the partial-brain allowance. Within-group task contrasts are reported for the sample of healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps (1-back>0-back, 2-back>0-back, 0-back>rest) and provides coordinates and cluster statistics. At least one within-group task contrast is reported for each participant group (healthy, schizophrenia violent and non-violent, APD), meeting the requirement for task-evoked voxelwise maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and is eligible for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (thought/image suppression), which maps onto executive function/inhibition domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects; contrasts reported such as suppressing>free-thinking, erasing>free-thinking, imagining>free-thinking) with tables/figures of activations and coordinate reporting. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study (10 healthy adults) using Stroop and Simon interference tasks that probe cognitive control/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise (pixel-wise) within-group contrasts of incongruent vs congruent trials, with whole-volume voxelwise maps, Talairach coordinates, time-course and ROI-averaged data. Although slice coverage was limited (10 axial slices), analyses were voxelwise and thus meet partial-brain allowance. The full text includes introduction, detailed methods, results, figures/tables, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, nor non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study satisfies I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Abstract describes an empirical task-based fMRI study of the Color–Word Matching Stroop (an inhibition/executive control task) with a reported within-group contrast (incongruent vs neutral) showing activations in frontoparietal regions and discussion of ACC findings. This meets criteria for fMRI task activation (I5), an executive function domain (inhibition; I6), a within-group contrast (I8), participant group reporting (I9), and the abstract reports whole-brain activation patterns consistent with voxelwise analysis (I7) and acceptable report format (I10). However, only the abstract/metadata are provided here — the full methods/results are not available to verify voxelwise group-level maps or coordinate tables, so I flag the full text as incomplete and assign moderate confidence.

This is an empirical PET and fMRI study using task-based paradigms that include working memory (2-back) and episodic memory tasks. Group-level, voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM/ANCOVA) and within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back, encoding/retrieval vs baseline). Participant groups (young and old healthy volunteers) are acceptable. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function imaging and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM99) at the group level (random-effects ANOVAs) and provides statistical maps and coordinate tables. Individual subject contrast images (one-sample t tests) were created (i.e., within-subject 2-back vs 0-back contrasts) and entered into group analyses, and results are reported for groups (siblings and controls). Thus the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts were computed as subject-level contrasts), I9 (participant groups reported, including clinical-family risk and controls), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore INCLUDE.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (set switching) using a pure switching task in 20 healthy adults. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group-level whole-brain analyses contrasting switch vs repeat trials, with cluster- and voxel-level permutation testing and tables/coordinates and figures. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (cognitive flexibility), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group maps), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Inclusion justified for meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates motor planning and self-initiation, which map onto executive domains of planning and initiation. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM results, thresholding, ROI whole-midbrain analyses) and within-group task contrasts (e.g., planning internally initiated vs rest; internally vs externally initiated). Participants are a healthy adult sample and results include voxelwise statistical maps and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs fixation), group-level t maps averaged across participants, voxelwise t tests, and tables/figures with coordinates — satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based EF activations and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (SART) probing executive functions (response inhibition and sustained attention/vigilance). The full text reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise t-tests with cluster thresholds, Talairach normalization, coordinates in tables/figures) and within-group contrasts (Random vs. Fixed SART; event-related correct inhibitions and error maps, and tonic block activations vs rest). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinates. Therefore the paper satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation mapping and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study directly probing response inhibition (an executive function) using within-group voxelwise contrasts (nogo vs saccade and task vs fixation). The design includes whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects statistical maps and tables of significant clusters (partial-brain coverage but voxelwise analyses are reported). Within-group contrasts (nogo> saccade; localizers vs fixation) are reported at the group level. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the study meets criteria for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts for executive function tasks (two-back working memory; WCST cognitive flexibility). Group-level statistical maps were computed, thresholded, normalized, and ROI/local maxima coordinates are reported (Table I and figures), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting. At least one within-group task contrast (task vs control) is presented for healthy adult participants. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of the Stroop color-word task, an established inhibition/executive-control paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses (incongruent vs. neutral), provides activation maps and coordinate tables, and includes full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task fMRI), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on abstract: this is an event-related fMRI go/no-go categorization task (animal detection), so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (task within executive domain: inhibition/cognitive control) and reports within-group contrasts comparing targets vs distractors, meeting I8. However, the full article (methods/results) is not provided, so I cannot confirm that a group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map was reported (I7) nor that whole-brain results/coordinates are clearly reported (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met from the available content. Because the full text is incomplete, inclusion criteria cannot be fully verified, so the study is excluded pending full-text retrieval.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based executive function paradigm (N-Back working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (within-subject, second-level ANOVA) and reports voxel coordinates and cluster results (left DLPFC) for the within-group contrast (3-back minus 1-back). Although a priori ROI and small-volume correction were used for inference, the analyses involved voxelwise statistical maps and a within-group task contrast was explicitly tested. Full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses contrasting task conditions (retrieval/manipulation vs maintenance; manipulation vs motor control), corrected for multiple comparisons, and presents whole-brain activation results. Within-group task contrasts are clearly reported and results are described in text/tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (only ROI-only, only connectivity/resting-state, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract, the study uses PET and fMRI and investigates alertness/vigilance using task paradigms, so I5 and I6 are met. However, the provided content does not allow confirmation of critical inclusion criteria: there is no available evidence in the supplied text that a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported (I7), nor clear documentation of a within-group task contrast (I8). Reporting of whole-brain results as coordinates/figures/supplement (I10) cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are directly met based on the abstract. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending full-text availability.

This study is excluded because it reports only ROI-based functional connectivity analyses (mutual information/coherence) and resting/task-related connectivity differences, without any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (connectivity/resting-state analyses without a task activation map) and E3 (only ROI/region-based analyses with no voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (working memory/N-back, an executive function task), I8 (within-group task contrast comparing N-back vs rest for MI), I9 (participant group acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported), I10 (no voxelwise coordinates/voxelwise whole-brain activation maps provided). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Given the absence of voxelwise task activation results, the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps and is therefore excluded.

This is an fMRI study of a planning task (Tower of London) in healthy adults and therefore meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (planning is an executive function) and I9 (participant group reported). However, the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise within-group task activation map. The authors performed voxelwise GLMs at the individual level and then quantified activation as suprathreshold voxel counts within manually defined VOIs and conducted between-group t-tests on VOI spatial-extent measures (ROI-based quantification). Because the main reported analyses are ROI-based spatial-extent comparisons and no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrast is provided, the study fails to meet I7 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked map) and I8 (a group-level within-group voxelwise contrast). This matches exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI-based/small-volume type analyses with no group voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude.

The study reports task-based fMRI using n-back working memory tasks (letters, shapes, locations) — clearly within executive function (working memory) and uses statistical comparisons of activation patterns between stimulus conditions. The abstract indicates group-level activation comparisons (voxelwise contrasts across stimulus types), satisfying within-group contrasts. Published empirical fMRI work (NeuroImage, 2000) likely reports whole-brain task-evoked results. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided), so I cannot verify the exact format of reported maps/tables or confirm voxelwise statistical map reporting in the full methods/results. Given the available information, inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 appear met. Marking fulltext_incomplete=true and giving moderate-high confidence.

This article is a methods/review-style paper that discusses PET/PLS/SEM examples and network analyses rather than presenting a clear original, primary whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map with explicit within-group contrasts suitable for activation meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (uses PET and addresses working memory/executive processes) and I6 (tasks fall within executive domains). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no explicit whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or coordinates are provided in the full text), I8 (within-group voxelwise task contrast not reported in a form usable for activation meta-analysis), and I10 (qualifying whole-brain results are not clearly reported as voxelwise maps or coordinates in the text). Exclusion criterion applied: E6 (non-empirical/methods-style paper without original human neuroimaging data in the form required for this meta-analysis). Given these gaps, the study cannot be included for pooling task activation coordinates/maps for executive-function activation meta-analysis.

Full text not provided (only abstract/metadata). The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of cognitive interference (Counting Stroop) and reports a within-group interference vs. neutral contrast, so it meets I5, I6, I8, and I9. However, I7 (presence of a group-level voxelwise/whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verified and I7 is unconfirmed, I exclude the study pending full-text review. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met/confirmed: I7. Full text incomplete.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study (H2(15)O) using an N-back working-memory paradigm (executive function). The full text reports voxelwise SPM99 group and within-group contrasts (2-back minus reference) for both patients and controls, with whole-brain activation maps, tables of peak coordinates, and figures. Thus it provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps and within-group task contrasts. Clinical participant group (schizophrenia) is included but that is acceptable. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and the study should be included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an incongruent color-word Stroop task (an inhibition/attentional control executive function) paired with heat pain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses and multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., distraction-specific (PD+HD)>(P+H), pain-specific (P−H), (PD−HD)), with whole-brain corrected statistical maps described in methods/results. Participants are healthy adults. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an executive-control/inhibition task (emotional counting Stroop) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (negative vs neutral; neutral vs fixation) with Talairach-transformed, voxelwise KS statistical maps and reported coordinates/p-values. Although image acquisition used limited slice coverage, the analyses were voxelwise (qualifies under partial-brain acquisition). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of analyses and outcomes. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Stroop paradigm (an inhibition/attention executive function task). The paper reports group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (SPM99 group analyses, thresholded maps, Table 2 and figures) and describes within-group contrasts (task vs rest) for both controls and TBI patients. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented and coordinates/figures are reported. Full article components (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) are present in the provided full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). From available information: meets I5 (task-based PET study of cognitive/executive processes), I6 (tasks include working memory, sustained attention/vigilance/time estimation), I8 (reports within-group contrasts, e.g., counting with no auditory stimulation vs counting while listening), and I9 (typical healthy adult sample; participant group acceptable). Cannot verify I7: the abstract reports "significantly increased relCBF in" regions but does not confirm a group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical map or provide coordinates/tables/figures; full article is needed to confirm whole-brain voxelwise analyses. Because I7 cannot be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and must be excluded pending full-text verification. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified Sternberg working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (e.g., Load 7 vs Load 3 contrast) with tables/figures of activated/deactivated clusters and ROI analyses, and at least one within-group task contrast. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (occluded target switching visual search) that reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., target switching vs non-switching) with voxel-wise FDR-corrected maps and voxel-wise analyses across the whole brain. The task manipulations probe executive domains (working memory, cognitive control/switching, response preparation/conflict). The paper includes full methods, results (voxel-wise contrasts, ROI and connectivity analyses), and discussion, and provides tables and figures describing whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Tower of London planning paradigm (an established executive-function domain: planning). Whole-brain, voxelwise preprocessing and second-level group analyses were performed and reported (SPM5; whole-brain ANOVA and paired t-tests) with tables/figures of coordinates and cluster results. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (planning vs. baseline; task-load parametric contrast), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task activation map. Participant group (MZ twins discordant for OCS) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; core content appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses executive functions (interference suppression and response inhibition) using task-based paradigms (flanker and go/no-go). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99; random effects), within-group contrasts (incongruent>neutral; no-go>neutral) for children and adults, and reports coordinates and regression results. It therefore meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The provided content is limited to title, metadata, and abstract only; the full article text (methods, detailed results, figures/tables) is not available for verification. From the abstract the study satisfies several inclusion criteria: it is a PET task-based study of executive function (WCST) (I5), the task falls within executive domains (working memory/cognitive flexibility) (I6), a within-group task contrast is described (WCST vs a sensorimotor control) (I8), and participants are a within-group (young normal) sample (I9). However, I cannot confirm that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map was reported (I7) nor that whole-brain results (e.g., coordinates) are presented (I10) because these details require the full methods/results and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on available information. Because the full text is incomplete, I am excluding the study pending review of the complete article to confirm I7 and I10.

This is an empirical fMRI Stroop study of cognitive control with within-group contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) and healthy adult participants, but the fMRI analyses were conducted within an a priori ROI mask (BAs 24/32, 8/9/46, 7/40) rather than reporting voxelwise whole-brain group maps. Methods state the analyses were confined to ROIs and significance was assessed within that mask, indicating ROI-only voxelwise results. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain (or at least non-ROI-constrained voxelwise) task-evoked group maps. Exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain results) applies, so the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control using a stop-signal paradigm (executive function: inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (thresholded z-maps, Bonferroni correction, coordinates/table), and multiple within-group contrasts (GO ONLY vs GO/STOP, parametric STOP-likelihood, correct vs incorrect STOP). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This paper is not an fMRI/PET activation study: the authors explicitly state they do not report brain-imaging data and focus on behavioral results. It therefore fails the primary inclusion requirement I5 (no task-based fMRI/PET activation data reported). Consequently it also does not provide whole-brain voxelwise maps (I7) or any within-group task activation contrast (I8/I10) required for inclusion. The task itself is an executive-function (task switching) paradigm (meets I6) and participant sampling is acceptable (meets I9), but missing neuroimaging activation results precludes inclusion. Exclusion criterion E5 applies because no within-group task activation contrast/map is reported for any group. Full text appears complete (behavioral methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory paradigm (executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise analyses (2-back > 0-back) including a whole-brain random-effects one-sample t-test with FWE-corrected voxelwise thresholds, and also provides ROI and extracted percent BOLD signal. A within-group task contrast is explicitly reported. Participants are human adults (twin sample). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Chinese-character Stroop, which probes inhibition/action-monitoring (an executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise task>control contrasts (one-sample t-tests) for both patients and controls and between-group random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM, with whole-brain activation maps reported in figures/tables. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function whole-brain voxelwise results. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and includes the required within-group contrasts. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. It includes group-level, voxelwise GLM deactivation maps (task vs baseline) in normalized whole-brain space, and reports within-group contrasts (negative response against baseline). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). The study reports within-group, voxelwise group-level (random effects) task contrasts (encoding, maintenance, retrieval) analyzed with SPM2 and presents whole-brain activation results in tables/figures (with ROI-based reporting restrictions but voxelwise analyses performed). Partial-brain coverage (inconsistent inferior cerebellum) is acknowledged but acceptable per criteria. Therefore it meets inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of planning using the Tower of London (an executive function within 'planning'). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses (ToL vs two active control conditions and parametric within-group contrasts), with coordinates and corrected statistical maps and ROI analyses. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a cognitive + emotional Stroop task (inhibition/conflict monitoring), which falls squarely within executive function/inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (P-corrected cluster < 0.05) and provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., IC vs CC; cognitive Stroop contrasts reported for the BAL condition and ATD effects). Results are reported as whole-brain tables/coordinates and discussed across task contrasts. Participants are healthy female volunteers (acceptable per I9). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (complete for screening). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study used task-based fMRI (n-back verbal working memory) in healthy adults and reports voxelwise analyses relating task activation power to reaction time, including Talairach coordinates of significant posterior parietal clusters. The paradigm falls squarely within the working memory executive domain, includes within-group task vs control contrasts (n-back vs sensorimotor control), and presents whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata present), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This is an fMRI task-based study using the Continuous Performance Task-Identical Pairs (CPT-IP), a sustained attention/vigilance task (an executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise group composite activation maps (figures and tables of coordinates) contrasting task vs control, and performs whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with cluster correction). Partial-brain slice coverage is present but voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported, satisfying the review's allowance for partial coverage. Both patient and healthy groups have within-group contrasts. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly assesses an executive function domain (working memory) and also examines visual attention. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 voxel-by-voxel repeated-measures ANOVA and contrasts such as 2-back vs 0-back and load effects), and within-group task contrasts are clearly described. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are full-brain statistical maps (cluster- and voxel-thresholding reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (reading span test) assessing executive function. The methods report group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) with voxel-level thresholds and identification of whole-brain activation areas; within-group task contrasts (Read+Memory and Recognition vs baseline) are reported for young and elderly groups. Results include tables/figures describing whole-brain activations and percent signal changes. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a digit n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise group-level activation maps (task vs baseline) and within-group contrasts across n-back loads, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses used to define ROIs and test load effects for each subject group (euthyroid, hyperthyroid, SCH, and treated SCH). Clinical participant groups are included and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not non-empirical). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that probes emotional conflict resolution—a form of response inhibition/cognitive control analogous to the Stroop—which fits executive function domains (inhibition/cognitive control). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses and provides coordinate-based activations for contrasts (e.g., incongruent>congruent, low>high conflict resolution, high>low conflict resolution). At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participant details (N=19) and full methods (stimuli, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, statistical thresholds) and results are present. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is an original empirical human neuroimaging study. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (feature binding) in young and older adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise statistical analyses (mixed ANOVA across voxels with reported clusters and Talairach coordinates), includes within-group planned contrasts showing combination > object/location for young adults (and contrasts reported for older adults), and provides whole-brain voxelwise results (partial slice coverage but voxelwise analyses). Results are reported as coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for executive-function task activations (working memory domain) with within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a go/no-go variant probing inhibition and timing (executive functions). It reports within-group one-sample t tests (control subjects) and exploratory whole-brain two-sample voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (random-effects), with task-evoked statistical maps and reported coordinates. Thus it provides voxelwise, group-level, within-group task contrasts appropriate for inclusion. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so content appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a spatial N-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The methods report voxelwise individual contrast maps (1-, 2-, 3-back vs 0-back), and group-level voxelwise t-maps (tested voxelwise against zero) used to identify working-memory ROIs; results include tables of coordinates and whole-brain thresholding. Within-group task contrasts are reported (individual and pooled group t-maps), and analyses are reported for both patient and control samples (and combined group maps). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups reported, clinical and controls), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided), so key methodological details cannot be verified. From the abstract: this is a PET task-based study of sustained attention/working memory (meets I5 and I6), and it reports task vs rest and control contrasts in a within-group sample of eight healthy volunteers (meets I8). However, the full article is not available to confirm that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical analysis was performed and reported (I7) or that whole-brain results are presented as coordinates/figures (I10). Because I7 cannot be confirmed from the available text, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back), an executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise single-subject contrasts (WM vs vigilance) and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses across the brain (thresholding, cluster correction), with figures and tables showing within-group activation maps and coordinates. Acquisition used whole-brain EPI (21 contiguous slices; partial coverage but voxelwise analyses were performed). Participant sample includes adolescents and young adults (non-psychotic first-degree relatives and controls). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (faces). This is an fMRI task-based study using an auditory verbal N-back working memory task (an executive-function domain). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM) including within-group two-back versus zero-back contrasts and separate group maps, and provides coordinates/tables/figures of activations. Methods, results, and discussion are present, enabling extraction of whole-brain task-evoked activation data. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study of executive function (modified flanker task) in 57 healthy adults that reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (INC>CON, NOGO>CON) analyzed with SPM99 random-effects models. Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps, tables of regional activations/coordinates, figures, and correlation analyses. The task targets inhibition and interference monitoring (established executive domains). Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI of executive function; appropriate executive domains; voxelwise group-level whole-brain analyses; within-group contrasts reported; results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is an empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a PET study measuring presynaptic Fdopa uptake at rest and relating uptake to separate neuropsychological tests (vigilance and Stroop). While the tasks fall within executive domains (vigilance, inhibition) and participants include clinical/control groups, the imaging data are not task-evoked activation maps. No within-group, voxelwise task contrast (task > baseline or task condition contrasts) is reported; analyses are voxelwise group comparisons of tracer uptake and correlations with behavior. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for task-based, within-group activation contrasts. Exclusion IDs met: E5. Inclusion IDs met: I6, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET activation study), I7 (no voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (no within-group task contrast). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using the AX-CPT, an executive function (context/working memory) task (meets I5,I6). The paper reports voxelwise GLM analyses and group-level ANOVAs with whole-brain cluster correction and tables of coordinates (Table 3), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise reporting (I7) and acceptable coordinate/table reporting (I10). The authors generated subject-level beta maps for task regressors (e.g., B-cue, delay) and describe task-related deflections within groups (e.g., positive deflection in controls), indicating within-group task contrasts are available/assessed (I8). Clinical and healthy participant groups are included and reported (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, and include within-group task contrasts rather than only between-group contrasts (E3–E5 not met). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a modified Stroop task (a canonical inhibitory/selective-attention executive function paradigm) with task-based voxelwise analyses. The paper reports within-group Stroop>rest activation maps for both healthy controls and unmedicated schizophrenia patients, provides whole-brain voxelwise methods (even if slice coverage was partial), and reports results in tables/figures/text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Sternberg working memory task (executive function domain: working memory). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; one-sample t-tests and random-effects ANOVA) with whole-brain FDR correction and tables/figures of activations. At least one within-group task contrast (WM vs control; and parametric load/delay contrasts) is reported. Participant sample is described (healthy adults). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/working memory with healthy adult participants. Reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99; voxelwise contrasts and peak coordinates) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., Repeat-Unexpected vs Repeat-Expected). Results are presented as voxelwise maps/coordinates and ROI analyses. Meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of semantic verbal fluency that examines effects of response pacing and overt/covert production. The task engages executive components (working memory, response inhibition, sustained attention/initiation) and the authors explicitly interpret activations in terms of cognitive control processes. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests, cluster-corrected maps) for within-group contrasts (fluency overall vs. baseline; paced vs. unpaced; covert vs. overt), satisfying within-group task contrast requirements. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable per criteria. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study using the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test to probe cognitive set-shifting (cognitive flexibility), an executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise statistical analyses (paired t-tests, replication and thresholding approaches) including pooled group-level results across seven subjects and reports coordinates and figures of significant activations in the inferior frontal sulci. Although slice coverage was partial, the analyses are voxelwise (not ROI-only) and therefore meet the meta-analysis requirement that partial-brain acquisition is acceptable when voxelwise results are reported. The paper provides methods, results, and discussion (full core content present). Hence all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (MSIT) probing cognitive control/interference (executive function). The paper reports within-group interference vs control contrasts at both individual and group levels using voxelwise t-tests and provides group-averaged activation maps and coordinate tables (whole-brain loci reported). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task type, executive domain, voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, and reporting of whole-brain results. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

The provided full text is incomplete (API error message only) and lacks the core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I cannot confirm whether the study used fMRI or PET, whether task paradigms fall within executive-function domains, whether whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported, or whether any within-group task contrasts are present. Because I cannot verify satisfaction of inclusion criteria, the study must be excluded pending a complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are identifiable from the available metadata. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / unable to assess: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

This is an fMRI task-based study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain), reporting within-group and between-group voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM99. The methods describe whole-brain acquisition and random-effects voxelwise group contrasts; results include within-group task activation maps and coordinates (tables/figures) for both patients and controls. Clinical participant groups are allowable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion, so appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI of the Tower of London planning task (an executive function) and a motor task in healthy participants. It uses whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (random-effects one-sample t-tests) implemented in SPM, thresholded at P<0.05 corrected across the whole brain. Within-group task contrasts are reported (easy and difficult TOL versus control; move versus rest), and results are described in text, figures, tables, and ROI/frequency maps. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for executive function task activations (planning). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a counting Stroop task that probes response inhibition (an executive function). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (mixed-model ANOVA, voxelwise percent-signal-change, cluster-threshold correction) and presents group-level within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent; speed×congruency interaction) with tables/figures describing activation. Correlational within-group analyses between ACC activation and HRV are reported.
