Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of executive control), I6 (inhibition domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation using a two-back verbal working memory paradigm (executive function domain). It includes within-group task contrasts for both patients and controls and describes group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses using SPM99 with whole-brain voxelwise results presented in tables and figures. The paper provides methods, results, and discussion (full text content available). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not only between-group contrasts). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of task activations across executive function domains.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an n-back paradigm (working memory) which falls within executive function domains. Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2; FDR-corrected contrasts; tables of coordinates and figures), and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., lag 2 vs lag 1, comparison vs identity, number vs letter contrasts). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is incomplete (API error message only). Unable to verify key methodological details required by inclusion criteria. I cannot confirm whether this study used fMRI or PET task-based paradigm (I5), whether tasks fall within executive function domains (I6), whether voxelwise whole-brain analyses were reported (I7), whether a within-group task contrast is reported (I8), or whether qualifying results are reported in tables/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be assessed from the provided content. Because the full text is unavailable, inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed, so the study is excluded pending retrieval of the complete article.

This is an empirical PET (H2 15O) task-based neuroimaging study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function domain: planning). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed using SPM96: a categorical within-group contrast (planning vs rest) and correlational voxelwise analyses (complexity, movement number) are reported with tables/figures of coordinates and statistical parametric maps. Participants are a within-group of healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete. Hence INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working-memory task (executive function), with within-group contrasts (2-back vs baseline) reported for controls and patients. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLMs with cluster-level correction and results shown in figures and coordinates, and behavioral covariates were used. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for task, domain, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that assessed processes requiring cognitive control/working memory: participants generated and maintained visual mental images (retrieval and maintenance) and performed judgment probes, fitting the working memory/executive domain. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and paired t-tests), voxelwise contrasts (imagery vs baseline, perception vs baseline, and perception–imagery paired contrast), cluster-thresholded statistical maps, and tables/figures with coordinates. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain activation results suitable for meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps (FEAT/FLAME Z-stat images and cluster thresholds) and provides within-group contrasts (2-back>1-back, 2-back>0-back, 1-back>0-back) for both MDD patients and healthy controls. Partial brain coverage (24 axial slices) is present but voxelwise analyses were performed, satisfying the meta-analysis’ allowance for partial-brain acquisition. Results are reported in figures, tables of coordinates and in-text descriptions. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included.

This is a PET study of motor planning (planning is an executive function) that uses task-based imaging and voxelwise parametric maps in a single subject, but it does not report any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise map). It does satisfy I5 (task-based PET), I6 (planning domain), I8 (within-task contrast at the subject level), I9 (human participant group), and I10 (voxelwise/figure-based whole-brain results reporting). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (fixed- and random-effects), within-group task contrasts (working memory vs control; subtraction images across scans), and provides peak coordinates and statistical thresholds. Participant groups are healthy adult volunteers. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task activation maps are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete for screening.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that manipulates working memory load (one-back versus two-back) and perceptual load within a task-based paradigm. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., higher activation for the two-back versus one-back task in prefrontal cortex) and whole-brain analyses with reported coordinates. The task falls within an established executive function domain (working memory). Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI studies of executive function and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a working memory task (chunking in spatial WM), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects), with FDR-corrected peaks and Talairach coordinates, and presents within-group contrasts (structured vs unstructured trials) and task-vs-baseline effects. Participant groups (healthy adults) are acceptable. Results are reported as coordinates and described in the text. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text is complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an executive-function paradigm (color-naming Stroop; inhibition/selective attention) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses using SPM2. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (one-sample t-test for controls for the motor task and task vs control contrasts used in group analyses), presents whole-brain results in tables and figures (coordinates and cluster maps), and includes complete methods and results. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. Inclusion recommended for meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This fMRI study reports task-evoked, whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses of a task that includes a clear working-memory component (mental addition/subtraction of fractions). The paper describes within-group active vs control contrasts and presents voxelwise random-effects activation maps for musicians, non-musicians, and all subjects combined (figures/tables), satisfying the requirement for a within-group, voxelwise task activation map. The task falls within an executive-function domain (working memory) per the authors’ description, and results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise analyses (not ROI-only). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the counting Stroop to probe response conflict/inhibition (an executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Stroop vs control) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected results reported in tables/figures), and provides complete methods, results, and discussion. Although slice coverage was partial (19 sagittal slices), the analysis was voxelwise and therefore qualifies under the partial-brain allowance. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a Go/No-go (inhibition) task in younger and older adults, so it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (inhibition within executive domains), I8 (a within-group task contrast was computed: activation for correct target trials vs baseline), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results described in text). However, the paper’s imaging analyses and reported results are ROI-based: functional activation values were extracted from anatomically defined basal ganglia ROIs and analyzed with ANOVAs. The manuscript does not present a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinate tables. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise analysis), and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI-based analyses with no voxelwise results). On that basis the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (spatial 2-back vs 0-back) with group-level, voxelwise analyses. The paper reports whole-brain random-effects one-sample t-tests for the main effect of task and between-genotype group contrasts, with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results are presented in tables, figures and text. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, genotyping, task, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, and statistical analysis), Results and Discussion sections. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (meets I5 and I6) that reports within-group task contrasts and group-level random-effects tests (meets I8 and I9). However, all reported analyses were performed using a priori regions-of-interest (the authors state "All the analyses reported ... were performed with ROIs") and group results are presented as ROI-based summaries rather than voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it does not provide group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps and meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses) is not met.

The study reports task-based fMRI of spatial working memory (an executive function: working memory) and explicitly describes whole-brain fMRI contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs rest, center vs rest) and within-group activation patterns for both alcoholics and controls. These features satisfy inclusion criteria for fMRI modality, executive function domain, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group contrasts. However, the provided full text is limited to the abstract and metadata; the complete article (methods/results sections, coordinate tables or voxelwise maps) is not present here, so I cannot fully verify availability of group-level statistical maps or coordinate reporting required for meta-analytic extraction. Full-text retrieval is recommended to confirm voxelwise group maps/coordinate tables and extract data for pooling.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a verbal n-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects GLM, voxel-based ANOVA, conjunctions) and provides coordinates/tables and figures of task contrasts (e.g., 2BRW>1BRW, state contrasts, conjunctions). Within-group task contrasts are reported for the healthy adult sample across load levels and sleep-deprived vs rested states. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and include within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain: working memory). Data were acquired whole-brain at 3T and analyzed voxelwise with SPM5 (group-level random-effects parametric analyses reported), with coordinates and tables given. At least one within-group task contrast (parametric linear increases with load; 0-,1-,2-back) and conjunction/disjunction group analyses are reported. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts present). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. The full text reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (contrasts 2-back > 0-back and 3-back > 0-back) and within-group task contrasts for both TBI patients and healthy controls; results are reported in text/tables and discussed. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group activation maps and coordinate reporting. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The full text reports an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses proactive motor inhibition (an executive function/inhibition task) using a task-based paradigm. It includes group-level, voxelwise second-level random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with whole-brain reporting of activations and tables of coordinates. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (e.g., mixed-block no-cue vs cued; SOA100 vs SOA500), qualifying as within-group task activation contrasts. Participants are human subjects (healthy adults). Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control (thought suppression) using task-based paradigms. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM99) contrasting suppression conditions (SUPPRESS and CLEAR) against a FREE-THOUGHT baseline and against each other, with thresholded whole-brain t-maps described in the text. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (fMRI task assessing executive/inhibitory control; tasks map to inhibition; group-level voxelwise analyses; within-group contrasts reported; healthy participant group; whole-brain results described in text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of attentional control (integrated Simon and spatial Stroop tasks), which falls squarely within executive function/cognitive control (inhibition/conflict resolution). The paper reports group-level random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain analyses and presents within-group contrasts (Simon Incongruent > Simon Congruent; Stroop Incongruent > Stroop Congruent), with tables/figures of activation and coordinates. Participants are a within-group (healthy adults) sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study of non-perceptual attentional set-shifting (cognitive flexibility), reporting group-level voxelwise SPM analyses and within-group contrasts (alternate vs rest and other contrasts). Although slice coverage was limited (12 axial slices), analyses were whole-brain voxelwise and thresholded across the brain, which meets the partial-brain allowance. Participants were healthy volunteers; results are reported in text with coordinates. All inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation studies are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI task-based study probing inhibitory control of learned motor programs (executive function domain: inhibition). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (INH vs REST; ACT vs REST) and conjunction analyses at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, permitting assessment. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human neuroimaging). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (inhibition) using a Go/Nogo paradigm (I5,I6). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group- and task-level analyses (AFNI voxel-wise t-tests, cluster correction) and provides coordinates/tables and figures (I7,I10). Within-group task contrasts are reported (Nogo–Go; Go/Cue–Go/Noncue; Cued-Nogo–Uncued-Nogo), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast (I8). Participant groups include clinical (schizophrenia) and healthy controls, which is acceptable (I9). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and the paper includes within-group activation contrasts (no E3–E5 violations). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (N-back), an established executive function domain. Methods describe voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses using SPM99 (task-versus-control contrasts, 0- vs 2-back), and results list group-level activation clusters and coordinates (patients and controls; between- and within-group contrasts and regression with symptom severity). The paper therefore provides within-group task activation maps, uses whole-brain voxelwise analyses (not ROI-only), and clearly reports task activations in text/tables. It is empirical human neuroimaging data (not connectivity- or resting-state-only). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based n-back working memory paradigm. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise SPM99 random-effects analyses (task on vs off contrasts), provides coordinates and cluster statistics, and describes within-group task contrasts for all participant groups. Although slice coverage excluded the cerebellum, analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-limited. Full article includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain executive-function activation maps.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (3T) of Stroop paradigms targeting inhibitory control (an executive function). The methods describe whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise group analyses (SPM2 random-effects ANOVA) with within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; congruent vs neutral), cluster thresholds, and coordinate tables—results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise activations and ROI analyses. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). It reports within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., Binding, Sign, Speech, 2Binding > Sign + Speech) analyzed with SPM2 and corrected maps and coordinate tables. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (with complementary EEG) that uses a Stroop paradigm to probe conflict monitoring and cognitive control. It reports group-level voxelwise task contrasts (conflict contrasts: moderate vs low, high vs low; incongruent vs congruent) with coordinates and cluster results, includes whole-brain/random-effects analyses (and ROI-based as well), and presents within-group task contrasts. The task falls squarely within executive function domains (inhibition/cognitive control). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an event-related fMRI investigation of recognition memory with instructions to feign impairment (malingering). It meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain SnPM analyses), I8 (within-group contrasts: NH vs MM and NCR vs MFA), I9 (healthy adult participant group), and I10 (results reported with coordinates/tables). However, it does not meet I6: the primary task is episodic recognition memory (visual object recognition) rather than a canonical executive-function task (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the authors discuss executive-control-related activations (e.g., DMPFC, VLPFC) arising during deceptive responding, the paradigm and contrasts are centered on memory recognition and malingering, not an established executive function domain per I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing I6.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (an established executive function). The study reports within-group task contrasts (1-, 2-, 3-back vs 0-back) and performs whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (including a 3×3 repeated-measures ANOVA and voxel/clusterwise inference with reported coordinates and cluster statistics). Results are presented for healthy controls and patient groups, with ROI trends derived from whole-brain maps. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (Montreal Card-Sorting Task) assessing set-shifting and planning in Parkinson’s patients and controls. The full text reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (single-group and inter-group), thresholding and statistical maps, and tables/figures of peak coordinates. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., retrieval with shift vs retrieval without shift) for at least one group. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain activation analyses of executive functions.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop interference task (inhibition), fitting executive-function domain. The full text reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (random-effects t tests; whole-brain maps, thresholds and clusters) and also presents within-group task contrasts (interference minus color naming) for each group. Results are reported as voxelwise activation maps, tables, and figures. DTI is additional but does not preclude inclusion. The article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full experimental details provided), so the full text is complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports voxelwise, whole-brain activation results for executive-function tasks (probabilistic reversal-learning for cognitive flexibility and Tower of London for planning). Methods describe whole-brain SPM2 voxelwise analyses and second-level (random effects) contrasts; the paper reports task>baseline activation maps (main effects) and group comparisons, with tables/figures of activations. At least one within-group/task main-effect contrast (task vs baseline across participants) is reported. Participant samples include clinical groups (problem gamblers, smokers) and healthy controls. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based EF fMRI with whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts and suitable reporting.

This empirical study reports task-based fMRI of a working-memory (Sternberg) paradigm in both healthy and schizophrenic subjects, with within-group contrasts (five-digits vs arrows baseline) and group-averaged voxelwise activation maps identified via pairwise t-tests. The task falls within the executive function domain (working memory). Although slice coverage was limited (15 slices), analyses were voxelwise rather than confined to ROIs. Results include within-group activation maps for both participant groups and detailed methods, results, and discussion, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI (SPM99) empirical study of set-shifting (Wisconsin Card Sorting Task) addressing cognitive flexibility—an executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level random-effects contrasts (1st-round vs 2nd-round shifts), provides whole-brain normalized images, statistical activation maps, and coordinate tables (Table 1, Figs. 2–4). Although small-volume correction (SVC) was applied to some frontal peaks, the analyses are voxelwise whole-brain GLMs rather than ROI-only. Participants are healthy adult humans. Thus the study meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10, and does not violate exclusion criteria (no ROI-only reporting, no connectivity-only analyses, no between-group-only contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) with within-group contrasts and group-level reporting, and the full text is available. However, the reported analyses are confined to a priori ROIs (dorsolateral and ventrolateral PFC and amygdala), with results summarized as measures within these ROIs (numbers of suprathreshold voxels within ROIs and percent-signal change). The paper does not present or describe a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (or voxelwise analysis covering the whole brain) in the text; analyses appear ROI-confined. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise task map). Consequently the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using n-back working-memory tasks (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (n-back task vs rest and pre/post-chewing paired comparisons) and group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects paired t-tests) with whole-brain results presented (figures and tables of coordinates). Participants are healthy humans. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and tables/figures, so fulltext appears complete. Hence the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Empirical fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function domain) in healthy adults. Reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (2-back>0-back and 1-back>0-back) using second-level random-effects analyses; main task effects were assessed with whole-brain FWE correction and reported in tables/figures (activation coordinates). Thus it provides a voxelwise task-evoked map (within-group contrast). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of selective attention and top–down control using Stroop and oddball tasks (executive/cognitive control domains: inhibition/attention), reporting within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Stroop-incongruency vs. Stroop-congruency; Word-oddball vs. Oddball control) analyzed with random-effects whole-brain statistics and coordinate tables/figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses an emotional Stroop task (task-based fMRI) and reports within-group task contrasts relating extraversion to AC activation and to functional connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task involves inhibition/attention component within executive function domain—emotional Stroop relates to cognitive control/inhibition), I8 (within-group task contrast: positive vs neutral words), I9 (healthy participant group within-group results reported), I10 (results reported as coordinates/figures described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map is reported—task activation results in the AC were reported using an a priori ROI mask rather than a whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Exclusion criteria applied: none (the paper reports connectivity analyses but also ROI task activation; no exclusion rule directly applies). Therefore excluded due to failure to satisfy I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task activation).

This is an fMRI study that includes a 2-back working memory task (an established executive-function domain). The paper reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back) and group-level, random-effects whole-brain statistical maps with FDR thresholding, plus tables of coordinates and figures. Whole-brain coverage was used. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo) in abstinent heroin dependents and healthy controls. The full text includes background, detailed methods (whole-brain fMRI acquisition and voxelwise preprocessing/analysis), behavioral and within-group contrasts (one-sample t-tests reported for each group) and between-group voxelwise comparisons reported with coordinates and figures. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for task domain (inhibition), imaging modality (fMRI), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and within-group task contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references.

The article reports an event-related fMRI experiment using a Stroop-like size classification task probing conflict/interference (inhibition/attentional control), with full methods, results, and discussion. It includes within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., RI–CO, SI–CO, CO–SU) analyzed with SPM2 and conjunctions; results are presented in tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations and violates no exclusion criteria. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a categorical n-back (working memory) task — an established executive function domain. The full text reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level random-effects analyses (SPM99), within-group contrasts (correct n-back > baseline) for multiple participant groups (6-, 10-year-olds and adults), and provides tables/coordinates and detailed methods/results/discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes volitional inhibition (breath holding), which maps onto the executive function domain of inhibition. The study used whole-brain BOLD fMRI with group-level, voxelwise analyses (thresholded and corrected) and reports within-group task contrasts (breath-hold vs baseline) with results presented in tables and figures. Participants were a healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a parametric n-back working memory task (an executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise random-effects SPM99 analyses (one-sample t tests for linear increase in n-back) and between-group ANOVA, with whole-brain cluster results, corrected p-values, coordinates, and tabulated imaging findings. Thus it provides voxelwise, group-level task activation maps and within-group contrasts for both patients and controls. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (modified Sternberg), an established executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (one-sample t-tests within each group and group ANOVAs) across whole-brain images, with coordinates and cluster results described. Within-group task contrasts (exponential BOLD signal decreases across retrieval blocks; task vs implicit baseline/within-group effects) are explicitly reported for both patients and controls. Partial brain coverage (24 slices) does not preclude inclusion because voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI of the Stroop (inhibition/cognitive control), meeting executive function domain criteria. The methods describe voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (one-sample within-group t-tests and between-group two-sample t-tests) using SPM99b with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent; results include coordinates and statistical maps/tables. A within-group contrast (interference vs facilitation) is explicitly reported for both patient and control groups. Participant groups include clinical (schizophrenia) and healthy controls. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a well-established executive function task (Stroop color-word interference — inhibition/cognitive control). It reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects ANOVAs including whole-brain exploratory analyses with cluster-corrected voxelwise results and Talairach/MNI coordinates, and presents within-group condition contrasts (incongruent vs congruent). Participant sample and reporting (coordinates, figures, methods, results, discussion) are appropriate and full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation mapping.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a parametric n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). It reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (0-,1-,2-,3-back vs rest) and presents whole-brain activation results (voxelwise statistical maps, corrected at P<0.05 and figures/tables with coordinates). Partial slice coverage is noted but voxelwise, whole-brain analyses and figures/tables are provided. Participants are healthy never-smokers (acceptable). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Figures/Tables, References).

This study reports task-based fMRI in 20 healthy adults including an n-back working memory task (an established executive function). The paper presents voxelwise, group-level activation maps (one-sample t tests and ANOVA) using SPM2 with whole-brain normalization and thresholding (p=0.05 FWE), and reports activation volumes, laterality indices, and percent signal change derived from voxelwise analyses. Within-group task contrasts (main effects of task vs baseline and n-back levels) are explicitly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function, voxelwise group maps, and within-group contrasts are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Study reports task-based fMRI investigating working memory (an executive function) with parametric manipulation of memory load and reports a linear relationship between activity and load. The abstract describes whole-brain imaging in a replication experiment and within-group task effects (load-related activation), consistent with voxelwise, group-level task contrasts. However, only the title/abstract/metadata are provided here, so the full text (methods/results/discussion) is incomplete and could not be fully verified. Inclusion is based on information in abstract indicating I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are likely satisfied; fulltext_incomplete flag set to indicate uncertainty and need to verify full article for final coding.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (executive function) in healthy older adults and aMCI patients. It reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain analyses (first- and second-level SPM2 random-effects), including within-group contrasts (‘targets’ minus baseline) and group-by-emotion interaction maps with coordinates and tables. Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps (thresholded SPMs) and peak coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is a task-based BOLD fMRI study using a Go/NoGo response-inhibition paradigm (an established executive function: inhibition). The paper reports a within-group contrast (nogo vs. go) and a group-level, voxelwise one-sample t-test for the main effect of response inhibition (thresholded whole-brain at p<.05 FWE), satisfying the requirement for a group-level voxelwise task-evoked map. Participant group (healthy adult males) is acceptable. Whole-brain results are reported with coordinates/tables and figures. Although some genotype analyses used small-volume correction, the study nonetheless provides whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports original task-based fMRI data of an executive function (inhibition/interference) paradigm (ANT variant with arrow and gaze flankers), meeting the review objective. It includes within-group, voxelwise/random-effects contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) for both neurotypical and autism groups, with whole-brain voxelwise maps and tables of coordinates reported. Analyses used SPM, random-effects voxelwise t-maps, and reported anatomical coordinates (Table 2). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses task-based paradigms probing sequencing/working memory (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain statistical maps and tables of coordinates), including within-group contrasts (REVERSE vs FORWARD and task vs baseline) and practice-related interperiod dynamics. Participants are healthy adults; results are reported in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a go/no-go inhibition paradigm (executive function). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (performed errors vs correct responses; observed errors vs observed correct responses; observed vs performed errors) at the group level, with whole-brain analyses and tables/figures of activations. Although ROI SVC analyses were used for a priori ACC hypotheses, whole-brain voxelwise results are explicitly reported (thresholds, tables, figures). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus all inclusion criteria for fMRI task activation (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract provided). The PET study reports a Stroop task performed within a day of the PET but does not clearly state that PET was acquired during the Stroop (no task-evoked PET activation described) and there is no evidence of a group-level, voxelwise within-group task activation contrast. The paper reports between-group metabolic comparisons and correlations between rCMRglc and Stroop performance. Therefore inclusion criteria met: I6 (task is an executive-function Stroop/inhibition task). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (no clear task-based PET/fMRI paradigm during imaging), I7 (no evidence of voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked maps), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I9 (within-group contrast requirement not satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (reports only between-group contrasts/correlations with no within-group task activation map). Because core article content (methods/results/discussion) is missing, fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a 2-back verbal working memory task (executive function domain). The study reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 with random-effects inference and corrected thresholds, presents coordinates and tables/figures of results, and includes within-group contrasts (auditory VWM vs auditory control; visual VWM vs visual control). The full article contains introduction, methods, results, discussion and references. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical data present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly investigates planning (an executive-function domain) using a task-based Tower of London paradigm. The paper reports within-group main effects (planning > baseline) and task-load contrasts for both OCD patients and controls, analyzed with voxelwise whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses and reported as coordinates and figures. The methods describe whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise group-level statistics, and results include within-group activation maps and task load correlations. The manuscript contains full introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete for screening purposes. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review and violates no exclusion criteria.

Abstract and metadata indicate an empirical PET rCBF study using statistical parametric mapping in healthy subjects performing executive tasks (Wisconsin Card Sorting Test and an auditory verbal shadowing task). These are established executive domains (working memory, cognitive flexibility). The methods imply voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses and the reported contrasts compare single vs dual task performance (within-group task contrasts). Results are described in text (rCBF maps), meeting reporting requirements. However, only abstract/metadata are provided here — full article (methods/results/discussion) is not included for verification, so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate pending full-text confirmation.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (digit-sorting), an established executive-function domain. The full text reports group-level random-effects hierarchical GLM and whole-brain voxelwise regressions (voxel-by-voxel analyses) with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster thresholds, and condition-related within-group contrasts (parametric effects of 3-,4-,5-digit conditions and task vs baseline). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results and coordinates are reported in-text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (face WM), which falls squarely within executive function domains. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The authors report whole-brain, voxelwise group-level mapwise analyses (random-effects t maps) with corrected thresholds and provide coordinates (Table 1) and figures of activation, satisfying whole-brain evidence. Within-group task contrasts (main effect of task vs baseline; early vs late practice contrasts) are explicitly reported. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (mental rotation), which is an executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (rotation vs. identity judgment; simultaneous vs. successive) analyzed with SPM99 and reports whole-brain thresholded activations and coordinates. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise group-level statistical maps/contrasts and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (verbal 2-back), reporting GLM-based voxelwise analyses (SPM2) and Talairach-transformed coordinates, and presenting within-group task contrasts (2-back vs 0-back/ baseline). Although the paper emphasizes SEM connectivity, it includes whole-brain, voxelwise activation analysis used to define activated regions for subsequent modeling. Participants were healthy adults and the task falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). Partial brain coverage (16 slices) is noted but voxelwise group-level analyses were performed and reported, so I7 is met. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study (Chein & Fiez, 2001) uses a delayed serial recall working memory task, which falls within established executive function domains (working memory), satisfying I5 and I6. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (voxel-wise t-tests and ANOVAs, thresholded maps, and coordinates/figures) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses despite limited slice coverage, satisfying I7 and I10. Multiple within-group contrasts (maintenance vs baseline, encoding vs baseline, retrieval vs baseline) are reported, satisfying I8. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults, satisfying I9. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based n-back working memory paradigms (3-back and 1-back) relevant to executive function. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analyses (voxelwise correlational search and cluster-level maps with coordinates) and within-group contrasts (e.g., 3-back vs 1-back; event-related amplitude analyses and load comparisons). Participant sample is healthy adults. Results are reported with coordinates, figures, and detailed methods/analyses. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts (violent vs fearful/neutral) in healthy adults, but the experimental paradigm is passive viewing of film clips, not an established executive-function/cognitive-control task. It therefore fails inclusion I6 (task within executive function domains) and consequently does not meet I5 (fMRI assessing executive function via a task-based paradigm). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group qualifies), I10 (results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I6) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The paper reports results from a working-memory task and uses fMRI-derived activation clusters (Table 1; references to fMRI activations for load 1 and load 3 vs fixation), providing group-level voxel coordinates and maps used to constrain source analysis. This satisfies the meta-analysis requirements: task-based fMRI data for an executive function domain (working memory), within-group task contrasts (load1/load3 vs fixation), whole-brain voxelwise evidence summarized as coordinates/maps, and participant group-level analyses. Although the primary focus is EEG/ERP source decomposition, fMRI activation results (group clusters/coordinates) are presented and used directly. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria appear to apply.

This fMRI study assesses working memory (Sternberg) in first-degree relatives of schizophrenia patients (meets I5 and I6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise between-group statistical maps (controls > relatives and relatives > controls) and whole-brain exploratory maps (meets I7 and I10) and includes an eligible participant sample (meets I9). However, the manuscript does not report any group-level within-group task activation contrasts (e.g., task > baseline or one-sample t-tests per group) in the results or tables—analyses were carried forward to second-level between-group t-tests only. Therefore it reports ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task activation contrast, violating exclusion criterion E5 and failing inclusion criterion I8. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study must be excluded for not providing a within-group task activation contrast.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a memory-guided saccade (MGS) task assessing spatial working memory, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (group maps transformed to Talairach space; significant voxels identified in AFNI) and contrasts isolating MGS versus VGS (MGS–VGS), indicating within-group task contrasts were computed and used to generate group maps. Although slice coverage is partial (seven axial slices), the analysis is voxelwise and therefore meets whole-brain evidence criteria per inclusion rules. Participants include a developmental/clinical high-risk sample, which is acceptable. Given these points, all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Sample size is small, but that is not an exclusion criterion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines monitoring and evaluation processes within a short-term/working memory paradigm—functions that fall within established executive domains. The study reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (condition × time ANOVA with voxelwise thresholds, Talairach transformation, and reported activations), and presents within-group task contrasts (e.g., PW > ON and other condition contrasts reported separately for young and older adults). Results are described in the main text with coordinates and region labels. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The provided full text is incomplete: it contains only an HTML skeleton with no Introduction, Methods, Results, or Discussion. Therefore I cannot verify any inclusion criteria. Specifically, I cannot confirm I5 (use of fMRI or PET task-based paradigm), I6 (task falls within established executive function domains), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis), I8 (presence of a within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups reporting within-group contrasts), or I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be confirmed from the available content. Exclusion recommendation is based on fulltext incompleteness; full assessment requires complete article text or supplemental materials.

Full text provided appears to be only title/abstract/metadata (no methods, results, or discussion), so I cannot verify key eligibility criteria. From the abstract, the study is an fMRI Stroop task examining attentional control in younger and older adults, so it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function) and I6 (task falls within executive function domain — inhibition/attentional control). However, I cannot confirm whether the paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (I7), whether at least one within-group task contrast is reported for any group (I8), whether qualifying whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I10), or whether the conditional participant-related criterion (I9) is satisfied. No exclusion criteria can be confirmed from the abstract alone. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot include the study.

Study is a PET, task-based investigation of the Stroop interference task (an inhibition executive function), reports task-evoked regional activations and appears to report within-group task contrasts in healthy subjects. These meet key inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I8, I9) and the results are described in the text/abstract (I10). However full text is not provided here (only abstract/metadata), so I cannot confirm whether group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps were reported (I7 unconfirmed). Full text is needed to verify voxelwise analyses and detailed methods/results.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The study is a PET task-based investigation of inhibition (Hayling task) and clearly meets I5, I6, I8, and I9. However, the provided content does not allow confirmation of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps (I7) or whether whole-brain results are reported as voxelwise maps/coordinates/figures (I10). Because at least one required inclusion criterion (I7) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on available information.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract: the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (working memory task), and I9 (clinical participant group: MTBI). However, I cannot verify I7 (presence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map) or I8 (reporting of at least one within-group task contrast) from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are demonstrably met. Because the full text is incomplete and key eligibility items (I7 and I8) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone, I must exclude this record pending full-text availability. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I9. Inclusion IDs not met / not verifiable: I7, I8 (and I10 cannot be confirmed).

This is an fMRI task study using a counting Stroop (inhibition/cognitive control) — an established executive function paradigm. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (number Stroop vs neutral Stroop during no-stimulation) with Talairach coordinates and maps described, satisfying a within-group task contrast. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not only between-group contrasts). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on available abstract: the study used task-based fMRI with young adults and reports within-group contrasts (rule-based vs similarity-based), so I5 (fMRI task), I8 (within-group contrast), and I9 (participant group) appear satisfied. However, I6 (task falls within specified executive function domains) cannot be confidently confirmed because the task is semantic categorization (not clearly one of the listed EF domains), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis) cannot be verified from the abstract alone, and I10 (sufficient reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are evidently met. Because the full article (methods, voxelwise analysis details, and results) is not available here, I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria; therefore I exclude the study pending full-text access.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the stop-signal task (an established inhibition/inhibitory control paradigm) with voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses and group-level random-effects within-group contrasts (e.g., post-go speeding > post-go slowing). The paper reports full methods, results (whole-brain FWE-corrected activations, tables/figures), and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based neuroimaging of executive function and provides within-group, voxelwise activation maps. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (MAT/PREP/EXEC), so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (working memory). It reports within-group contrasts and group-level ROI-based statistics (repeated-measures ANOVA on extracted betas), so I8 and I9 are met. However, the paper reports analyses focused on functionally-defined ROIs and ROI-based group statistics; it does not present a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map or voxelwise group results in the main text. Thus it fails I7 (no clear group-level voxelwise task-evoked map) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/small-volume analyses reported with no voxelwise group results). Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI (N-Back working memory) assessing executive function in healthy volunteers, with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99 random-effects) contrasting working-memory conditions vs 0-Back (within-group task contrasts). It reports activation maps and voxelwise results (with SVC for multiple comparisons) and behavioral measures across executive domains. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical human neuroimaging). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults. It reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects analyses), provides whole-brain (near whole-brain) coverage and stereotactic coordinates, and tests within-group task contrasts (main effect of task vs intertrial interval and period-specific contrasts). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (mPASAT) in moderate-severe TBI and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM96 (random effects), provides within-group task contrasts for both groups, and presents activation results in figures and tables (Talairach coordinates). The task falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based event-related fMRI study of executive function (task-switching; cognitive flexibility). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (one-sample within-group contrasts and between-group ANOVA) with tables/figures of activation (task-switch minus task-repeat) for control and OCD groups. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (cognitive flexibility), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses; partial coverage acceptable), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (clinical participant groups acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an original, task-based fMRI study of auditory verbal working memory (executive function domain). It reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (WM vs vigilance contrast) and provides whole-brain results (with corrected peaks and tables of coordinates), plus within-group task contrasts for both relatives and controls. Although imaging used limited axial slices (15 × 7 mm), the analyses were voxelwise and small-volume corrections were applied, which meets the allowance for partial-brain acquisition. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stroop interference paradigm (inhibition), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and both ROI and voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise regression maps, cluster thresholds, and tables of coordinates are reported: Tables II–III and figures). Although slice coverage was limited (6 common slices used for all subjects), voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed and reported, and partial-brain acquisition is allowed per inclusion criteria. Results are reported as voxelwise coordinates and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports original event-related fMRI data using conflict tasks (Stroop and two spatial conflict tasks) that probe executive function/inhibitory control. The abstract describes within-subject within-group contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) with reported significant activations in anterior cingulate and prefrontal cortex, suggesting voxelwise group activation maps were produced. Thus the study appears to meet inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI (I5), executive-function tasks (I6), within-group contrasts (I8), permissive participant groups (I9), and acceptable reporting formats (I10). I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis) is likely met based on description of spatial extent and peak activation locations, but cannot be fully confirmed because only the abstract is provided. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are evident. Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided), preventing definitive verification of voxelwise group maps and availability of coordinate tables or figures; inclusion is provisional pending full-text review.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts relevant to executive functions. The tasks include a working memory maintenance condition and a reasoning condition that involves manipulation/integration (executive processes). Group-level voxelwise GLM contrasts are reported (reasoning vs rest, maintenance vs rest, reasoning vs maintenance) with cluster-level inference and peak coordinates. The report includes methods, participants, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates an fMRI study of working memory with within-group task contrasts, satisfying I5 (fMRI task-based EF study), I6 (working memory task), and I8 (within-group contrast described). However, the available content does not allow verification of I7: that at least one group-level voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map was reported. Because I7 is required and cannot be confirmed from the provided text, the study must be excluded pending full-text verification. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the provided information. Recommend obtaining the complete article (methods/results/tables) to reassess inclusion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (phonological rehearsal), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses including a within-group contrast (delay period L6 vs L1) and a group analysis showing premotor (BA6) activation. The methods describe whole-brain EPI acquisition and voxelwise statistical analysis; results are reported in the text (and tables/figures), satisfying requirements for group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study uses fMRI as the testing environment and includes an executive-domain task (working memory) and appropriate participant groups, it does not report any task-evoked neuroimaging results. The full text presents behavioral analyses (A' scores, response bias) comparing laboratory vs. scanner performance but contains no group-level, voxelwise fMRI/PET activation maps or within-group task contrast maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI/PET study assessing executive function with task-based neuroimaging), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), and I8 (within-group task contrast at the imaging level) are not met. Inclusion criteria I6 (task in executive domain: working memory) and I9 (participant groups reported) are met. Full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), an established executive function domain (inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects), with within-group contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials) for men, women, and combined groups, and provides tables/figures of coordinates and results. Imaging acquisition covered the whole brain. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This article is a methods/protocol paper describing the emotional counting Stroop and how to implement it in fMRI; it does not present original group-level, voxelwise task-activation maps or within-group task contrast results in the full text provided. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task paradigm) and I6 (task maps to inhibition/cognitive control domain). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise statistical maps provided in this protocol), I8 (no within-group task contrast results reported), and I10 (no whole-brain results in tables/figures/coordinates in this article). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete (protocol with introduction, methods, anticipated results, references). Therefore exclude.

Exclusion E3 applies: the paper reports fMRI task results using a priori ROIs (ACC and lPFC) and presents percent-activation/ROI ANOVAs; no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps or coordinate tables are reported in the text. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control/conflict), I6 (task taps executive/cognitive control processes), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), and I9 (healthy participant group). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation analysis reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E3.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a Stroop color–word task (an established inhibition/cognitive-control executive function paradigm). The paper reports group-level voxelwise activation maps (group analysis, z-score maps, figures and Table of Talairach coordinates) and a within-group contrast of Stroop vs baseline/rest. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented (though with limited slice coverage, voxelwise group maps are used, which satisfies I7). Participant sample is healthy adult group (within-group contrasts reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendix). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study of visuospatial working memory (2-back), an executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (‘2-Back minus Match to Centre’) with coordinates and corrected statistics, and also ROI analyses; results are described in the text and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (visual 3-back style) in controls, MCI, and AD. The paper reports within-group stimulus-versus-rest voxelwise statistical parametric maps and group-average activation maps analyzed with AFNI, indicating whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses rather than ROI-only methods. It explicitly presents within-group contrasts (group activation maps for each group) and describes group-level voxelwise thresholding and cluster criteria. Participant groups include clinical samples (MCI, AD). Results are reported in text, figures, and tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears to include introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations and is included.

This is an empirical fMRI study (N=18) using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM, one-sample t-tests; SPM2), with within-group task contrasts (task vs rest/implicit baseline). Results are presented as activation maps and group analyses across subjects. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for pooling executive-function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using task-based n-back paradigms with within-group contrasts (0-,1-,2-back) and voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM analyses across 30 healthy adults. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses and maps are reported (including cluster- and voxel-level inference), satisfying requirements for whole-brain, within-group task contrasts. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly investigates planning (an executive function). It uses a task-based paradigm (Tower of Hanoi/GOP) with trained participants, models planning-related events, and performs group-level, voxelwise analyses (between-subject voxel-wise t tests of the ACT-R regressor) reporting whole-brain activation foci and coordinates. Within-group task effects are reported via voxelwise regression contrasts (task-related ACT-R(t) coefficient), satisfying a within-group task contrast. Partial-brain coverage is acceptable per criteria and the paper presents voxelwise maps/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Tower of London planning paradigm (an established executive-function domain: planning). The full text reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-level correction across the whole brain) and provides coordinate tables and figures. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., six- versus four-move problems; planning and movement-execution phases; correct vs. erroneous trials), satisfying within-group task contrast requirement. Participants and methods are fully described. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references, appendix).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go), which is an executive function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (Movement Nogo and Count Nogo vs baseline; direct comparisons) using SPM2, with whole-brain thresholding and tables of coordinates; thus it provides qualifying whole-brain task activation maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Delaylocation/no secondary task – baseline; Delayobject/no secondary task – baseline) and presents group-level, spatially normalized group-average statistical maps and tables. Whole-brain, event-related acquisition and analyses are described, with group-level voxelwise contrasts and thresholding. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task domain (I6), imaging modality and task-based design (I5), whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (I7), within-group task contrasts (I8), permissive participant sample (I9), and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in figures/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures, tables, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), which is an established executive function. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses using SPM2, conjunction contrasts ([3-back – 1-back] and [1-back – rest]) and within-group task contrasts (load-sensitive analyses for young, and group comparisons), with whole-brain/voxelwise results described in text and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only title/metadata/redirect notice provided). Based on title and metadata, the study appears to use fMRI and addresses maintenance/working memory (so I5 and I6 are likely satisfied). However I cannot verify critical inclusion criteria: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses) and I8 (within-group task contrasts) are not confirmable from the available information, nor can I confirm I10 (reporting of whole-brain results/coordinates).
