No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the limited content. Because the full article (methods/results) is not available to confirm whole-brain voxelwise within-group task activations, I exclude this record pending retrieval of the complete full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise task activation maps (semantic task vs control) with whole-brain coverage. Although the primary paradigm is a semantic association task, the task explicitly requires maintaining the noun in memory for later comparison and the authors discuss working memory demands as a key interpretation. Therefore the paradigm falls within the executive function domain of working memory. The paper reports within-group contrasts, whole-brain thresholded maps and cluster/peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of the Stroop task (executive control/inhibition), reporting within-group, voxelwise, random-effects group analyses (contrasts such as oddball vs baseline neutral, incongruent>neutral, incongruent-eligible>ineligible). Although acquisition used 10 slices (partial coverage), analyses were voxelwise and thresholded and peak clusters are reported, which satisfies whole-brain evidence (partial-brain acquisition allowed). The study assesses executive function domains (inhibition/attention/working memory), uses task-based fMRI, and reports appropriate within-group contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI n-back working-memory study with within-group task contrasts and whole-brain acquisition; it addresses executive function (working memory) and reports group-level ROI/VOI percentage signal-change statistics. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group results reported), I10 (results clearly described in text). However, the paper’s analyses are ROI/VOI-based: no group-level, voxelwise task-activation statistical maps (nor coordinate tables or voxelwise figures) are reported. Therefore it does not satisfy I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analysis) and meets exclusion E3 (only ROI/VOI analyses reported with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Consequently, exclude under E3; inclusion criteria met: I5,I6,I8,I9,I10; inclusion criterion not met: I7.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study of volitional saccade tasks (antisaccade and ocular motor delayed response) probing inhibition and working memory—established executive function domains. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (one-sample t maps, voxel-by-voxel BOLD contrasts versus fixation, Talairach normalization, cluster correction) and presents within-group task contrasts (task vs fixation) for participant groups (healthy, relatives, schizophrenia). Participant samples include clinical groups but within-group contrasts are reported. The full text includes background, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study with group-level, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (switch vs stay) investigating task switching, a form of cognitive flexibility (executive function). It reports whole-brain random-effects analyses with thresholded statistical maps and tables of coordinates, and includes within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults; results are presented as coordinates and figures. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory with distractors (an executive function task). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 and a random-effects second-level one-sample t-test, with sustained memory-delay contrasts (correct trials vs control) and comparisons between correct and error trials (within-group contrasts). Participant group is healthy adults. Whole-brain results are reported and activation foci coordinates are provided. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references (complete).

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (Tower of London planning), reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and within-group contrasts (TOL vs fixation) for participant groups (autism and control). Methods describe SPM99 voxelwise analyses, and results include within-group activation tables/figures. Although the sample had partial slice coverage (14 oblique slices), the study performed voxelwise analyses, which qualifies under I7. The paper also reports clinical participants but within-group contrasts are present, meeting I9. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4) since task activation maps are reported, does not report only between-group contrasts (E5), and is empirical (E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. The task is an emotion-regulation (cognitive reappraisal) paradigm rather than a canonical executive function task within the specified domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the paradigm engages cognitive control processes, it is not one of the established executive function domains listed in I6. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts such as increase>look and decrease>look), I9 (reports within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an event-related fMRI study that explicitly examines deception, conceptualized and discussed as requiring executive functions (inhibition of pre-potent truthful responses, cognitive control, task switching). The study reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (lie>truth, lie>control contrasts) using SPM across 14 healthy adults, with coordinates and thresholding described. This satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (task engages inhibition/cognitive control), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of picture naming with linguistic distractors examining language production, semantic/phonological facilitation and interference. Although it includes neural measures related to conflict/monitoring, the primary task is lexical access and language processing rather than an executive function or cognitive-control task within established domains (working memory, inhibition as a primary process, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task falls within established executive function domains). The full text is complete and reports within-group voxelwise whole-brain activation maps and contrasts (meets I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Conclusion: exclude because primary cognitive construct targeted is language production, not executive function.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that places strong demands on cognitive control and temporal integration (working memory/strategy maintenance), meeting the review’s executive-function scope. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (state-item mixed design) and group-level contrasts (task > fixation; W2 vs W12), with healthy adult within-group results. Results are reported in text/tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG–fMRI study using a task (mental arithmetic) that engages central executive functions/working memory. The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain fMRI analyses (SPM99) with group-level one-sample t-tests (n=8) linking task and phase-synchronization indices to BOLD responses, and also reports a within-group task contrast (arithmetic vs rest). Results are reported as statistical maps and tables of coordinates. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all prespecified inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-group voxelwise group-level analyses (beta-maps normalized to a template, voxelwise t-tests across subjects) comparing switch vs. repeat conditions and reports whole-brain results (including coordinates: 30, −79, 48). ROI and matched-RT analyses are also reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (cognitive flexibility), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses performed), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (coordinates and maps described). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task-based study of verbal working memory (n-back), an executive function domain. The full text reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (generic brain activation maps, voxelwise FPQ maps, permutation tests) for both control and schizophrenia groups, and provides regional coordinates/tables and scatterplots of within-group task effects. Although slice coverage was limited (14 non-contiguous planes), the analyses were voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted, satisfying partial-brain acquisition allowance. The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not assess executive function or cognitive control task performance (it uses transcranial electrical stimulation of motor cortex with simultaneous fMRI/EMG to study interhemispheric inhibition). Inclusion/exclusion summary: Exclusion criteria met: none (E3–E6 do not apply). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise whole-brain/fixed-effects statistical maps reported), I8 (within-group task contrast: single-pulse vs baseline and IHI vs baseline), I9 (participant group reported: healthy volunteers), I10 (whole-brain results reported in maps/text). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study of executive function or cognitive control), I6 (tasks are not within established executive function domains — paradigm probes motor corticospinal physiology rather than working memory, inhibition as a cognitive control task, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore excluded because it fails to meet I5 and I6 required for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study of an auditory oddball task that probes vigilance/attention and working-memory updating processes (executive function domains). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (targets and novels vs implicit baseline) and parametric, group-level analyses of target-to-target and novel-to-novel intervals using whole-brain correction (familywise error) and cluster analyses. Sample is a within-group healthy adult cohort (n=100). Results are reported as statistical parametric maps, coordinates, figures, and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of phonological working memory (an executive function: working memory) using a task-based paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) and provides coordinates/tables and figures for task contrasts. It includes within-group task contrasts (WM trials vs control trials) and reports voxelwise results for stimulus-encoding, maintenance, and decision phases. Participant group (n=12) is described. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly assesses an executive function domain (working memory) using a task-based paradigm (delayed matching-to-sample). The methods describe whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects one-sample t-tests, Talairach normalization, voxelwise thresholds) and report voxelwise results in figures and tables (coordinates provided). Within-group contrasts are reported (memory vs control; manipulable vs non-manipulable; symmetry subanalyses), satisfying the requirement for at least one within-group task contrast. Participants were healthy adults; any participant group is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and the paper is empirical). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly compares working memory (an established executive function domain) and long-term memory within the same subjects using task-based paradigms. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses are reported (mapwise thresholds, stereotactic coordinates, conjunction analyses), and within-group task contrasts versus an implicit baseline (ITI) and between-task contrasts are presented. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (N-back), an established executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise group-level task contrasts (N-back vs fixation; 2-back vs 0-back), identifies whole-brain activated regions with Talairach coordinates and extracts β-values, and reports within-group task activation and between-group comparisons. Full methods (acquisition, preprocessing, GLM) and results (activation maps, coordinates, ROI statistics) are present in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion requirements (I5–I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive functions (attention-switching and response inhibition) reporting group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts. Methods and results show whole-brain GLM random-effects analyses (SPM99) with FDR correction and voxelwise contrasts (switch − nonswitch; incompatible − compatible) and blocked contrasts (High-Switch − Low-Switch). Results are reported as coordinates/tables and figures. Although acquisition used 15 axial slices (partial coverage), analyses were voxelwise and thus meet I7 (partial-brain acquisition acceptable). The study clearly meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 (fMRI task, executive domains, voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, and reported whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper reports an event-related, task-based fMRI study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), matching executive-function domains. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects contrasts (transition cue vs task cue) with reported Z-maps and coordinate tables, and reports within-group task contrasts (main effect of cue type and other contrasts). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive function—cognitive flexibility), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group contrast reported irrespective of participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (random-effects analyses) for word retrieval and for contrasts of task difficulty. Although the primary paradigm is word generation (language), the study explicitly manipulates task difficulty and interprets the additional activations as reflecting sustained attention, working memory, and executive response selection (executive control domains). It includes within-group contrasts (word retrieval vs baseline; difficult > easy), reports voxelwise results and coordinates, uses a healthy adult sample, and presents full methods/results/discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that investigates top-down attentional control (feature-based shifts), a form of cognitive control/cognitive flexibility (set-shifting). The study uses a task-based paradigm with within-group contrasts (shift vs hold; hold-motion vs hold-color), reports voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds, and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The abstract describes an empirical PET (15O-water) task-based study using the N-back verbal working memory task in nine healthy volunteers and reports localization of statistically significant regional CBF changes and generation of activation maps. This satisfies inclusion criteria: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (working memory, an executive function domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are implied by statements about localization and activation maps), I8 (within-group contrasts across N-back levels), I9 (participant group qualifies), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as activation maps/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Note: the provided content appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata rather than the full article, so fulltext_incomplete is set to true, reducing certainty.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that reports within-group voxelwise contrasts relevant to executive function. The study used working-memory (digit-verification) and temporal-production tasks (with motor and control conditions), meeting the executive domain requirement. Group-level SPM analyses (voxelwise t-maps converted to Z and thresholded) are reported for contrasts such as W–C, T–C, and T–W, demonstrating whole-brain voxelwise results. Participants are a within-group sample (five healthy adults). Results are described in detail (methods, results, discussion) with statistical thresholds and anatomical localization, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be included.

Full text provided is incomplete (HTML skeleton only) so core article content (introduction, methods, results) cannot be assessed. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Go/NoGo inhibition paradigm (executive function: inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) and explicit within-group contrasts (false alarms–hits; correct rejections–hits). Whole-brain processing and thresholds are described and fMRI activation maps/coordinates and focused ACC centroid analyses are reported. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This FDG-PET study used a trial-by-trial Stroop task (an executive/inhibition task) and includes patient and control groups, so I5, I6, and I9 are met. However, the imaging analyses are ROI-based (circular ROIs averaged across slices) and report regional metabolic rates and correlations rather than any group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps; therefore it does not provide whole-brain, voxelwise activation results (I7 not met). The study also does not report a within-group task activation contrast (e.g., task vs baseline or condition contrast) for any group — imaging data are reported as metabolic rates during task and group comparisons/correlations rather than within-group voxelwise contrasts (I8 not met). These features violate exclusion criteria E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results) and E5 (no within-group task activation contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Given these violations, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study probing cognitive control/executive function (attentional control over threat-related distractors). It uses a within-group task design with voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (voxel-wise comparisons, whole-brain correction and ROI small-volume corrections) and reports activation coordinates and figures. The task and contrasts (threat-related vs neutral distractors; block × trial interactions; start-trial contrasts) constitute within-group task contrasts relevant to executive function domains (inhibition/attentional control). Participants are healthy adults; results are reported in text, figures and coordinates. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility/task-switching (executive function). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level statistical maps (SPM2 random-effects one-tailed t-tests; whole-brain contrasts such as bivalent > univalent and bivalent switch > repetition) with coordinates and tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Tasks fall squarely within executive function (cognitive flexibility), and participants are a within-group sample of healthy young adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and tables/figures, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical PET study using the Stroop task (inhibition domain of executive function). It reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) computed via voxel-by-voxel t-tests and voxelwise regression, with whole-brain analyses and tables/figures of activations. Participant groups include patients with major depression and age-/gender-matched controls. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data present). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. It is an fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts (MI vs. LI object categorization), with group-level statistical maps and coordinate/figure reporting, and includes behavioral WM interference data; therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported in text/figures/tables). However, the primary tasks are visual object categorization and perceptual fragmentation manipulations, not tasks that fall within the meta-analysis’s required executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as defined by I6. Although the paper discusses recruitment of top-down control and working memory processes and includes a behavioral WM interference manipulation (Experiment 2), the fMRI task contrasts are not standard executive-function tasks (e.g., n-back, stop-signal, task-switching) and thus do not fulfill I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function) with voxelwise, whole-brain analyses reported (voxelwise t-tests and ANOVAs, cluster-size correction). The paper reports within-group task versus fixation contrasts for each participant group (schizophrenia, major depression, healthy controls), and provides whole-brain coverage and detailed methods/results. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for task modality, executive domain, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is an empirical human neuroimaging study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study that reports voxelwise, group- and within-group task contrasts (decision > no-decision) and provides coordinates/figures, the task used (a modified Iowa Gambling Task assessing decision-making under risk/reward) does not clearly fall within the review's specified executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrast reported), I9 (clinical participant groups included), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion is based solely on failure to meet I6 (task domain).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of inhibitory control (an executive function). The manuscript includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This full-text reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) with healthy adult participants. Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses using SPM99 (random-effects contrasts, corrected and uncorrected thresholds) and report coordinate tables and figures for task contrasts. The paper presents within-group task contrasts (memory load high vs low; reward high vs low; interactions) and a main effect of task across events. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise activations (tables of coordinates, cluster corrections), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function) with group-level voxelwise GLM analyses reported (activation maps and Talairach coordinates). Participants include clinical and control groups. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps (SPM99) for cognitive tasks (PASAT and a recall task). The PASAT involves working memory and sustained attention (vigilance); recall involves memory retrieval—both fall within established executive/working-memory and vigilance domains. Participant groups include clinical (RRMS) and matched healthy controls. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Fulltext appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory in first-episode schizophrenia patients and controls. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function: working memory). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (N-back and item-recognition), which falls squarely within executive function domains. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of antisaccade versus prosaccade performance (inhibition/cognitive control), satisfying executive function domain criteria. This is a task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function domain), with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects GLM analyses and within-group contrasts (what vs where; maintenance vs manipulation). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (N=12) that reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (discrimination vs identification) with whole-brain coverage and group-level statistical maps (Talairach coordinates, cluster-level and voxelwise thresholds). Results are reported in standard coordinate tables/figures and described in the text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This study reports task-based event-related fMRI in healthy adults performing an established cognitive control task (Preparing to Overcome Prepotency), directly addressing executive function/cognitive control. This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) using a task-based paradigm (I5, I6). This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of visual working memory (an established executive function domain). This is an empirical fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory manipulation (executive function). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes voluntary inhibition of the micturition reflex (a form of inhibitory control). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (delayed-response WM) manipulating distraction, satisfying the executive-function domain. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Based on the abstract, this is an empirical fMRI study using a spatial working memory task (an executive function domain). The study reports grouped and individual statistical maps aligned in stereotactic space and examines common regions of activation across sites, indicating group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses and within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, only the title/abstract/metadata were provided here (no full methods, results, or discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true and the decision is made cautiously; full-text retrieval is recommended to confirm details (e.g., exact nature of group-level voxelwise analyses and statistical thresholds).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a Sternberg working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2; second-level random-effects GLM) with within-group contrasts (within-group analyses of correctly retrieved items) and reports coordinates and statistical thresholds. Clinical sample (schizophrenia) is acceptable per the review objective. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory/executive control in schizophrenia. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task design, fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, voxelwise GLM analyses), Results (within-group one-sample t-tests, between-group voxelwise ANOVAs, tables of coordinates), and Discussion. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (FWE-corrected and uncorrected thresholds) and within-group contrasts (encoding vs baseline; alphabetize vs forward), and provides coordinate tables. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (task domain = working memory/executive function; fMRI task-based; whole-brain voxelwise group maps; within-group contrasts reported; clinical sample allowed) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study using a task-based n-back working memory paradigm (meets I5, I6). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (task vs. fixation) for adolescents and adults and provides group analyses (meets I8, I9), and results are described in tables/figures (meets I10). However, the authors used a region-of-interest (ROI)–based analysis (spherical ROIs derived from prior literature) to identify effects; there is no clear report of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map. Because the paper appears to report only ROI-restricted analyses with no voxelwise whole-brain group maps, it fails I7 and therefore meets exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI/small-volume analyses). Accordingly, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis that requires at least one group-level voxelwise activation map.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly probes inhibitory control and preparatory set using pro- and anti-saccade tasks (anti-saccade requires suppression of a prepotent response), which falls within executive function domains (inhibition). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (pro vs anti; task vs fixation) and uses voxelwise statistical mapping (saccade localizer t-test with cluster correction; Talairach coordinates reported). Although some acquisitions had limited slice coverage for event-related runs, analyses were voxelwise and group-level effects and coordinates are reported. Participants were healthy adults. Full article content (methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a 3-stimulus visual oddball task (sustained/selective attention = vigilance), which falls within the executive domain of vigilance. The paper reports within-group one-sample t-test contrast maps for targets/distractors/standards for each group and group-level random-effects two-sample t-tests; analyses are voxelwise and whole-brain (voxelwise and clusterwise corrections reported). Results are presented as statistical maps, tables, and figures. Participants are a defined human group (postmenopausal older women). The study therefore meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (vigilance executive domain), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory with within-group contrasts (amphetamine and control sessions), whole-brain acquisition, and clear reporting of behavioral and activation results. However, the primary analyses report counts of suprathreshold voxels within an a-priori load-dependent mask and focal ROI sphere analyses; the paper does not present or report a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the sample (group SPM maps are not described or tabled). Therefore it fails the requirement for a group-level voxelwise activation map (I7) and effectively reports ROI/mask-restricted results only, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E3.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines inhibitory control (antisaccade and nogo tasks) and voluntary response generation (prosaccade), directly addressing executive function (inhibition). The manuscript reports voxelwise, group-level mixed-effects whole-brain analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., anti_response vs pro_response, pro_response vs nogo_response). Results are presented as statistical maps, tables, and regional coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and provides within-group task contrasts (digit vs letter/face; letter vs digit/face; face vs digit/letter) with tables of coordinates and random-effects group results. Participants include adults and children. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the visuospatial n-back (working memory) task—an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects contrasts (memory-load-dependent increases/decreases) and within-group task contrasts (linear effect of n-back difficulty) with coordinates and cluster statistics; results are described in text, tables and figures. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study using the Stroop Color-Word Test (inhibition/cognitive control), with univariate voxelwise GLM analyses (SPM2) and group-level, whole-brain second-level contrasts. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent) and provides coordinate results and detailed voxelwise findings. Although DCM connectivity analyses are also performed, univariate task activation maps are reported, and partial-brain coverage (19 slices) still meets the review’s allowance for partial acquisitions so long as voxelwise analyses are performed. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI are satisfied (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is a PET task-based study using a continuous performance task (vigilance) with clinical and control groups, but analyses are ROI-based (60 predefined ROIs) rather than voxelwise whole-brain group-level statistical maps. The manuscript reports regional glucose metabolic rates extracted from ROIs and group/ROI statistics (t-tests, multivariate Hotelling's T2, correlations), and does not present a within-group voxelwise task>baseline activation map. Therefore it fails the whole-brain voxelwise requirement (I7) and does not present a within-group task contrast as a voxelwise map (I8). It therefore meets ROI-only exclusion (E3) and the exclusion for lacking any within-group task activation contrast (E5).

This paper is a computational modelling study that proposes an fMRI design and describes that ten subjects were scanned, but it does not report any task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise neuroimaging results or any within-group task contrasts. Therefore it does not provide the empirical task activation maps required for inclusion. Exclusion ID: E6 (non-empirical paper / no original neuroimaging results presented). Inclusion met: I6 (tasks are within executive function — working memory). Inclusion NOT met: I5 (no empirical fMRI/PET results reported), I7 (no voxelwise group-level maps), I8 (no within-group task contrasts), I9 (no within-group contrasts reported for any group), I10 (no whole-brain results presented). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-Back) — an established executive function domain — with healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2-Back vs 0-Back), including summary activation maps, voxelwise paired t-tests, and ROI analyses, satisfying within-group task contrasts and whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory manipulation (an executive function) reporting within-group, voxelwise task contrasts. The paper includes both ROI-based and exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analyses (manipulation > fixation and manipulation > maintenance) for younger and older adult groups, reports coordinates/tables/figures, and describes group-level GLM voxelwise statistics. Participant samples are acceptable (young and older adults). The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (third-level FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-thresholded Z statistic images) and presents within-group task contrasts (encoding, maintenance, retrieval each vs. baseline) with results reported in tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are available. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (faces and voices), which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (sample, delay, test periods) with voxelwise contrasts (face vs control, voice vs control, face vs voice) and corrected cluster thresholds; results are presented in tables/figures and described in text. Within-group task contrasts are reported for healthy adult subjects. Reporting of coordinates, Z-maps, and ROI and whole-brain analyses satisfy the review’s reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are violated. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain statistical maps and direct within-group task contrasts (WM vs sensorimotor control; object vs spatial contrasts), with thresholding and correction described. Participants are healthy adult subjects and analyses are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study that directly probes initiation and inhibition of hand movements—tasks that fall within executive function domains (inhibition and initiation). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ballistic vs smooth; stepwise vs ballistic), presents whole-brain group-level analyses (cluster-corrected voxelwise maps with coordinates and figures), and also provides ROI-masked analyses; results are described in the text and figures. Participants are a healthy adult sample. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. None of the exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (not ROI-only), this is not a connectivity- or resting-state-only study, and within-group task contrasts are presented. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (task switching/cognitive flexibility) with healthy adult participants. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., Stage 3 vs Stage 1) and whole-brain analyses with tables of coordinates and figures; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are reported. Tasks map to cognitive flexibility; analyses use random-effects, voxelwise contrasts and corrected thresholds. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses and explicit within-group contrasts (update > cued maintenance; memory blocks > category discrimination) with cluster-corrected voxelwise results and supplementary tables/figures. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. All required elements for inclusion are present (task-based fMRI, executive-function task, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, and reporting of voxelwise results). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI, task-based study using a standard working memory (N-Back) paradigm (executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxel-wise repeated-measures ANOVAs and ROI analyses derived from whole-brain contrasts) and within-group task contrasts (3-,2-,1-BACK vs 0-BACK). Participant group (healthy adults) is reported and within-group contrasts are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory (three-back) paradigm that probes executive function/attentional control. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (including conjunctions across word and face runs), provides coordinates and cluster-based results (Table 1, figures), and estimates event-related contrasts (lure, non-lure, target) against fixation/baseline within the same participant group. Participants are healthy adults. Thus all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (multiple object permanence tracking), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (random-effects, voxelwise T-threshold and cluster correction) and within-group task contrasts (MT−MC and ST−SC). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported in the text, figures, tables, and ROI analyses. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans using executive-function-related tasks (spatial working memory and verbal memory with executive demands), with group-level, voxelwise statistical parametric mapping (SPM) results and stereotaxic coordinates. The methods describe whole-brain preprocessing, normalization to MNI space, voxelwise GLM, second-level group maps, and thresholded activation clusters; results present within-group task activations and contrasts (predrug/postdrug/preplacebo/postplacebo and task vs baseline), and tables/figures with coordinates. Participant group (perimenopausal/recently postmenopausal women) is acceptable. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (task-switching), which falls squarely within executive function (cognitive flexibility). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses (shift vs repeat, response- and stimulus-conflict contrasts) with voxelwise t tests and cluster thresholds, and provides coordinates/ROI locations and supplemental data. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (main effects and contrasts against baseline and between trial types). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (N=19). Results are presented in full (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so the full text appears complete for screening. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of category learning (random dot patterns) with within-group, voxelwise activation maps. However, the task assesses category learning/visuospatial processing and attentional/eye-movement networks rather than an established executive function domain listed by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although it meets whole-brain imaging (I7), within-group task contrast (I8), reports voxelwise group results (I10), and includes an acceptable participant sample (I9), it does not target executive/cognitive-control processes as defined in I5–I6. Therefore it does not meet the core content criteria for inclusion.

This study reports task-based 3T fMRI using a standard executive-function working memory paradigm (2-back) and a motor task. It includes within-group task contrasts (2-back vs rest and finger flexion vs rest), voxelwise single-subject analyses (FILM) and group-level voxelwise maps generated with mixed-effects FLAME, and presents group activation maps and quantitative voxelwise metrics. Thus it provides whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps for an executive function task (working memory). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment of analyses and outcomes. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (mental calculation), directly addressing executive function (I5,I6). The paper reports group-level voxelwise statistical maps from nine healthy subjects (statistical maps and group-averaged analyses, t>4.0, p<0.05) and parametric within-subject contrasts across task difficulty (task vs baseline and difficulty levels), satisfying voxelwise whole-brain analysis and within-group contrast requirements (I7,I8). Participant groups include healthy volunteers and an epilepsy patient (acceptable per I9). Results are presented as statistical maps/figures and described in text (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and the article reports original human neuroimaging data (not E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects second-level analyses) with a main effect of task (2-back vs 0-back) and provides coordinates/tables/figures of activation. Although small-volume correction (SVC) was applied for a priori ROIs, the analyses are voxelwise and not limited to ROI-only reporting. Within-group task contrasts are reported (main effect of task across participants), and results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (main effect of time maps, FDR-corrected) and within-group contrasts (task vs baseline; short vs long delay comparisons) in a healthy adult sample, with results presented in text, tables, and figures. All inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI and PET study using the Tower of London planning task (an established executive function domain: planning). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM) with thresholded statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables, and includes within-group contrasts (categorical active vs zero-move baseline and parametric regression of task difficulty). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and provides voxelwise results and coordinates. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based paradigms that target executive functions (spatial working memory and planning). Group-level, voxelwise SPM99 analyses are reported (whole-brain task activations reported for placebo condition and figures/tables of coordinates), and within-group task contrasts (task vs control) are presented. Participants are healthy volunteers (acceptable). Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain executive-function activation studies are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based study using a continuous short-term verbal recognition paradigm that assesses processes within the working memory/short-term memory domain (falls within I6). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise t-statistics, conjunctions, whole-brain thresholds, coordinates and figures), and contrasts of task conditions within subjects (e.g., Repeat > Novel, Aud:Aud > Novel:Aud, Aud:Vis > Novel:Vis), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts (I8) and whole-brain evidence (I7). Participants are healthy adults (I9). Results and voxelwise maps/coordinates are reported in the text and figures (I10). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and this is an empirical neuroimaging study. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (experimental conditions vs number-matching baseline; trained vs untrained) using whole-brain SPM2 analyses with coordinates/tables. The arithmetic tasks explicitly engage working memory and executive control (authors report involvement of working memory/executive processes and fronto-parietal networks), which falls within the listed executive function domains (working memory). Results are reported as voxelwise activation maps and coordinates. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (delayed item recognition), which is an executive function domain (working memory). Analyses were voxelwise at the group level (SPM99 second-level GLM) and report spatial maps/thresholded patterns with tables of local maxima, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The paper computed within-group, load-dependent contrasts (linear effect of set size) and modeled young and elder groups separately, providing within-group task contrasts. Participant groups (young and old healthy adults) are acceptable. Results are reported as group-level voxelwise maps (figures/tables of coordinates), meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual working memory (an established executive function domain). It reports task-based, within-group contrasts (WM vs fixation; correct vs incorrect trials) and voxelwise whole-brain group maps (fixed-effects voxel-wise Z maps combined across subjects and random-effects ROI group analyses). Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures (and derived from standard-space voxelwise combinations). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of language control in bilinguals that directly addresses cognitive control/confl ict and selection processes (inhibition and cognitive flexibility). Methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM2 random-effects analyses and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., LSc vs SNc, TSc vs SNc, L2 vs L1), with coordinates and activation tables/figures. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy bilingual adults. The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI/PET; tasks capture executive domains— inhibition/cognitive flexibility; whole-brain voxelwise group analyses; within-group contrasts reported; participant group acceptable; results reported as tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract-level content). The study is a PET task-based study of attention (auditory continuous performance task), so it satisfies I5 (PET with task-based paradigm) and I6 (task falls within executive function domain of vigilance). However, the available content does not report or allow verification of whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (I7) nor confirm a within-group task contrast for any group (task vs rest or active control) (I8). Therefore not all inclusion criteria can be confirmed. No formal exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the available information. Because the full text is incomplete and key methodological details required to determine eligibility are missing, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/selection during verb generation, reported at the whole-brain level. The task manipulates selection demands (MANY vs FEW), a form of executive control/response selection, and includes within-group voxelwise contrasts (MANY>FEW) and group-specific contrasts. Whole-brain analyses were performed and reported (FDR-corrected maps and ROI plus whole-brain results), and participant groups (young and older adults) are included. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control/attentional selection in the motor system. The abstract reports group-level task activations (increased activity in prefrontal, premotor, and parietal cortex) and a within-group contrast (attention to action vs unattended performance), and also reports connectivity analyses. These correspond to the review’s executive-function objective. Therefore I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control), I6 (task addresses cognitive control/attentional selection within executive function domains), I7 (group-level voxelwise activations reported), I8 (within-group task contrast present), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results likely reported/acceptable formats) are considered satisfied. However, the provided full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata visible), so fulltext_incomplete=true. Confidence is moderate due to lack of complete article methods/results to fully verify voxelwise reporting and presentation format.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From the abstract: (a) This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (meets I5, I6). The abstract reports within-group task contrasts (3- vs 1-letter; 6- vs 1-letter), so I8 is met, and a within-group participant sample is reported so I9 is met. However, the full text required to verify that at least one analysis is a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map (I7) is not available in the provided content. I10 (that whole-brain results are clearly described in text/tables/figures) also cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3, E4, E5, E6) are explicitly met based on the abstract. Because I7 (and possibly I10) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of divided-attention/attention-switching and verbal working memory after total sleep deprivation. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (experimental vs baseline) with cluster correction, and presents activated regions in tables/figures/coordinates. The within-group task contrast (experimental > baseline) is reported for participant groups (normal night and TSD night). Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control using a Stroop task that isolates semantic and response conflict. It reports group-level, voxelwise GLM analyses with Talairach normalization, cluster-thresholded whole-brain statistical maps, and tabulated coordinates/figures for within-group contrasts (SI vs CO and RI vs SI). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (N=14). Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (inhibition/cognitive control task), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses, albeit with limited slice coverage stated), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/figures in text). No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity/rest-only (E4), not only between-group contrasts (E5), and is an empirical paper (not E6). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function. It reports within-group voxelwise group-level SPM analyses (contrasts S>NS, SC>OS, interaction) with whole-brain normalization, cluster/voxel thresholds and coordinates (Table 1, figures). Participants are healthy volunteers (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported as group statistical maps and coordinates. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and References, so full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). This is an empirical 3-T fMRI study using task-based working memory (an established executive function domain). It reports within-group, voxelwise group-level (random-effects) analyses with whole-brain voxelwise results (voxelwise threshold P<0.001) and provides coordinate tables and figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level (random effects) analyses using SPM99, with within-group parametric task-load contrasts (Sternberg and n-back), conjunctions, and encoding vs responding contrasts. Results are reported as tables and figures with corrected and uncorrected thresholds. The sample comprises healthy adult participants. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports a task-based H2 15O PET Stroop paradigm (meets I5) examining selective attention/inhibition (meets I6) in a within-group design comparing incongruent, congruent and control states (meets I8). Participants are healthy normal subjects (meets I9). The abstract describes regional rCBF increases/decreases across numerous cortical and subcortical regions, consistent with whole-brain activation reporting, but the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata available), so I could not verify that a group-level voxelwise statistical map was reported (I7 not fully verifiable). Full text retrieval is recommended to confirm whole-brain voxelwise analyses and exact reporting format. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive functions (motor response inhibition and motor timing). It reports within-group voxelwise analyses (generic brain activation maps, voxelwise permutation tests, regional analyses) and provides whole-brain results with coordinates for adults and adolescents. The stop task is a canonical inhibition paradigm (an established executive domain). The paper includes group-level task-vs-baseline contrasts and voxelwise statistical maps/analyses, satisfying whole-brain, within-group and task-based criteria. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete.

The paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a Sternberg working-memory task (executive function domain). It acquired whole-brain EPI, performed voxelwise, group-level statistical analyses (e.g., 6-digit vs 2-digit load contrasts for encoding and delay), and produced task-evoked activation/deactivation maps. Thus it provides within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for pooling. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and voxelwise analysis), Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Accordingly, the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of sequencing/planning (meets I5 and I6). It reports within-group task contrasts (script vs non-word; syntax vs non-word) and adult participants (meets I8 and I9). Results are presented as regions and numbers of subjects activating each ROI and described in the text (meets I10). However, the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map; authors performed per-subject voxelwise correlation and a qualitative ROI-based tally across subjects rather than a voxelwise group analysis, so I7 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) clearly apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses comparing task conditions (visual search vs control; memory search vs control). The tasks engage executive processes (monitoring/manipulating multiple items, cognitive planning, and shifts of attention) consistent with executive-function domains. Group-level random-effects SPM99 analyses and tables/figures of coordinates are reported. Healthy adult participants were tested. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that manipulates working memory load (an established executive function) and controlled semantic processing. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level activation contrasts (e.g., primed vs unprimed; WM load effects) with whole-brain preprocessing and cluster-thresholded statistical maps and tabulated coordinates. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The manuscript contains full sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) and presents whole-brain results (maps and coordinates), satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without activation maps, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). The methods report within-group, voxelwise group-level statistical analyses (FLAME mixed-effects) with thresholded statistical maps and conjunction contrasts (VIEW SIGNS, REHEARSE SIGNS vs rest). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented (figures and a table), and partial slice coverage is noted but voxelwise group analysis was performed, which is acceptable per criteria. Participant group (native deaf signers) is acceptable. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain within-group activation reporting are met, with no exclusion criteria triggered.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The abstract indicates an fMRI, within-subjects comparison of working memory (n-back) and long-term memory tasks, satisfying I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (working memory = executive domain), and I8 (within-group task contrasts). However, I cannot verify I7 (presence of group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps) from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, I must exclude this record pending full-text verification. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I8. Inclusion IDs not met/unable to verify: I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis).

Exclusion E3 applies: the study's analyses are restricted to predefined ROIs (ROI-based voxelwise tests within those regions) rather than reporting a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported for groups), I9 (participant groups included clinical and controls with within-group contrasts), and I10 (results reported as coordinates/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; analyses were confined to a priori ROIs). Full text appears complete and includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore exclude per E3.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps for a syllable-decision task that the authors frame and analyze in terms of phonological control and verbal working memory processes. The task engages phonological control (part of verbal working memory), an executive function domain (working memory), and the paper reports within-group contrasts (e.g., All Trials>Fixation; pseudo-English>English) using SPM99 with voxelwise group-level analyses and tables/figures. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus the study meets the review inclusion requirements and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (with concurrent ERP) using a visual three-stimulus oddball paradigm that probes attention/vigilance and working-memory-related processes (executive domains). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps (GLM group maps; figures and Table 3 with Talairach coordinates) and within-group contrasts (target vs baseline/standard and distractor vs baseline/standard). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=13). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based executive-function activations and reports whole-brain voxelwise within-group results suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the PASAT, a well-established working memory/executive task. The paper reports group-level voxelwise activation analyses (SPM99, activation clusters assigned to Brodmann areas) and extracts task-evoked time series from activated voxels to perform SEM; thus whole-brain (partial coverage acceptable) voxelwise task maps and within-group task contrasts (PASAT vs rest/baseline) are present. Participants include a clinical MS sample and matched controls; within-group contrasts are reported for at least one group. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a gambling/guessing paradigm that engages executive processes (working memory, response selection). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain coverage and presents within-group task contrasts (predicting/guessing vs reporting), with tables/figures of activations. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes working-memory contributions to sentence processing. It reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (grammatical violation vs correct sentences) analyzed with SPM99 and provides whole-brain activation maps and peak coordinates. The experimental design explicitly manipulates working memory demands (distance/filler and secondary task dual-task manipulations) and interprets activations in the context of WM/executive resources. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables/figures. Therefore all meta-analysis inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This is an empirical fMRI study that uses a task-based paradigm engaging verbal working memory and decision-making (executive processes). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (fixed- and random-effects SPM contrasts) comparing the verbal-transformation (VT) condition to a baseline within a healthy participant group. Results are provided as voxelwise statistical maps and coordinate tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (figures and stereotaxic coordinates) for within-group contrasts (Melody Discrimination and Harmony Discrimination contrasted with a button-press control, and Melody Listening contrasted with rest). The discrimination tasks require maintaining and comparing auditory sequences, engaging working-memory and cognitive-control processes (authors report dorsolateral PFC and anterior cingulate activations), so they fall within the working memory/executive domain. Participants are a healthy group (amateur musicians). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and the text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive function (working memory/reading span task). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM99) with tables of coordinates and figures, and within-group task contrasts (RST vs control; RST vs read) for participant groups (HSS and LSS). Results are reported as voxel-level and cluster-level corrected maps and coordinate tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive processes (branching integrates working memory and attentional allocation/planning). Group-level, voxelwise statistical parametric maps were computed (SPM96) and reported with thresholds and coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain voxelwise analysis requirements. Within-group task contrasts are reported (branching vs control, delay, dual-task; main effects and interactions). Tasks fall within established executive domains (working memory, planning/goal management). Participant data are reported (group of right-handed healthy adults, with replication samples).
