No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are present. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Full text is incomplete (only metadata/redirect text provided). Based on the title and available metadata, this is a resting-state fMRI study of networks in MCI and mild Alzheimer’s, and it does not appear to report task-based executive function activations. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (resting-state/connectivity analyses without task activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI/PET study of executive function), I6 (no executive function task reported), I7 (no voxelwise task-evoked whole-brain analysis reported), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported), I9 (no within-group task contrast for any participant group), I10 (no task activation results reported in any form). Because the full text is not available, this decision is based on title/metadata; if full text shows task activation results, inclusion should be re-evaluated.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working-memory manipulation and calculation (addition of four two-digit numbers), directly assessing executive function processes. It reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (Manipulation minus Maintenance for numbers, syllables, locations), with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster- and voxel-level corrections, and provides activation coordinates and figures. The design, methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an original human fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (delayed non-matching-to-sample) which falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM2 analyses at the group level (main effects: task > baseline; task load effects), with peak coordinates and tables/figures describing activations. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (activation vs implicit baseline and parametric load effects). Participant groups include clinical (childhood-onset GHD) and matched controls, but the within-group and pooled group activation maps satisfy inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes a verbal working memory (letters) task, which falls within the executive function domain (I5,I6). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., experimental > control; novel > repeated; negative > neutral) and performs group-level, voxelwise analyses using SPM with normalized, smoothed data and mixed-effects group statistics (satisfying I7 and I8). Participants are healthy volunteers and within-group contrasts are reported (I9). Whole-brain/global activation analyses and voxelwise SPM{t} maps are described and presented in the full text (I10). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is suitable for inclusion.

This full-text reports an empirical fMRI study using an n-back working-memory task (executive function) in schizophrenia and healthy subjects, with complete methods, results, and discussion. It includes voxel-wise, group-level mixed-model ANOVAs and reports whole-brain load main effects and group-by-load interactions (thresholds, cluster extent), fulfilling whole-brain voxelwise reporting. Within-group task contrasts are presented/used (load main effects, 2-back vs 0-back comparisons, and analyses of signal change within groups), and results are reported in text, tables, and figures. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study assessing spatial working memory/attention and motor preparation. It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (task vs control) using whole-brain SPM analyses and provides coordinates and group-level results. The tasks fall within established executive domains (working memory/attention). Participant group (healthy adults) has within-group contrasts. Whole-brain voxelwise analysis and reporting in tables/figures satisfy reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports event-related delayed-recognition tasks and group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses using SPM2, with whole-brain (near whole-brain) coverage and thresholded statistical maps and stereotactic coordinates. Within-group task contrasts (main effect of task against baseline for placebo and drug sessions, and tests of drug-related changes within task-related conjunction regions) are reported. Participants are human healthy adults. Results are reported as voxelwise maps, tables of coordinates, and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses of a covert orienting task that probes inhibition of return (IOR). IOR is an inhibitory attentional process and maps onto the review domain of ‘inhibition’ within executive/cognitive control. The paper reports within-group contrasts (long SOA vs short SOA) and random-effects group-level SPM analyses with corrected thresholds, and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI/MEG study of auditory spatial attention reorienting using a passive listening, sound-localization paradigm. It provides whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and within-group contrasts (condition vs rest; conditions compared). However, it does not assess an executive function or cognitive control task within the defined domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the discussion mentions response inhibition and no‑go literature, the experimental paradigm did not include an established executive task or manipulate executive control. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study used a Stroop (inhibition) task (meets I6) and reports within-group analyses on healthy participants (meets I9). However, it does not present any group-level, voxelwise fMRI/PET task-activation maps or voxelwise whole-brain activation results; the manuscript’s primary reported results are EEG-derived connectivity (PDC) and graph-theoretic metrics. Therefore it meets exclusion criteria E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without a task activation map) and E3 (analyses are ROI-/source-based rather than voxelwise whole-brain results). It does not satisfy I5 (an fMRI or PET activation study with reported activation maps), I7 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map), I8 (a within-group task contrast in fMRI/PET), or I10 (provision of qualifying whole-brain results in text/tables/figures). Full text appears complete. Excluded on the basis that no qualifying fMRI/PET whole-brain activation contrast is reported; primary outcomes are connectivity/ROI-based rather than voxelwise task activation.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using an N-back working memory task (executive function) with voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (2-back > 0-back) reported. Methods describe whole-brain SPM2 analyses and voxelwise Biological Parametric Mapping; results present significant clusters and coordinates. A within-group task contrast is reported for healthy older adults. All required criteria for inclusion are met (I5–I10). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting voxelwise, group-level within-subject task contrasts of working memory/item maintenance (rote rehearsal) and relational (elaborative) processing. Working memory is an established executive function domain, and the paper provides whole-brain/MTL voxelwise analyses (group one-sample t-tests and direct task contrasts versus fixation and between tasks). Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Results are reported as voxelwise statistical maps and ROI follow-ups. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

The study is excluded because it does not test an executive function task as defined by the review (I6). It uses an attention-to-prepulse (PPI) paradigm probing sensorimotor gating and selective attention rather than established executive domains listed (working memory, response inhibition as in stop/go paradigms, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The paper does report task-based fMRI, within-group contrasts, and voxelwise/statistical mapping across slices, so it meets I7, I8, I9, and I10, but it does not meet I5/I6 (does not assess an executive/cognitive-control task within the specified domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM and MLM) across 40 subjects, provides voxelwise spatial maps and MNI coordinates, and includes within-group contrasts (delay-period/task vs implicit baseline and set-size effects). The paper presents full methods, results, and figures/coordinates suitable for coordinate-based or image-based meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text is complete.

Meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: this is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a working-memory/executive task (modified PASAT). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation analyses (SPM2; FDR correction) and presents within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline and task-related maps for combined group and for each group/block). Results are reported as whole-brain maps/tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that assesses executive function domains (working memory, selective attention/vigilance, associative memory) using established paradigms (STERN working memory, SAT selective attention, PMT associative memory). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., NT vs CT, TO vs RS, AL vs SC, RE vs SC) and constructs group-level voxelwise statistical maps (z-statistics, voxel-by-voxel SPM analyses with FWE correction). Whole-brain/group voxelwise results and peak coordinates are reported (Table 2). Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study directly investigates response inhibition (an executive function: inhibition) using a task-based Go/NoGo paradigm and reports whole-brain voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (NoGo>Go) with coordinates and figures. It includes a within-group task contrast, whole-brain results in tables/figures, and healthy adult participants. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory selective attention (spatial negative priming), which falls within the executive function domain of inhibition. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps (task vs rest) and presents group within-subject contrasts (control vs spatial inhibition), with voxelwise analyses for task activation and ROI follow-ups; coordinates and figures/tables are provided. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (response inhibition; go/no-go), using a within-subject design across menstrual phases. It reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (with thresholding and cluster-size correction) and within-group contrasts (emotional distracter vs target; phase-specific one-sample and paired t-tests). Hormone assays and behavioral data are provided; results include tables/figures of significant clusters and coordinate-based reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation that includes an executive-function task (oculomotor delayed response = spatial working memory). The paper reports voxelwise group- and within-group one-sample t-tests (task vs fixation or task contrasts) with results presented as activation maps and tables. Partial brain coverage was used but voxelwise whole-brain (focused) analyses were performed, which meets the meta-analysis requirement allowing partial coverage. Participant groups include patients and controls, and within-group contrasts are provided for at least one group. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task, domain, voxelwise analysis, within-group contrasts, and reporting are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study of working memory/integration (executive function). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (random-effects ANOVAs) with cluster thresholds and tables of coordinates, and presents within-group task contrasts (IN vs SG, MO, RO and other contrasts). Participants are healthy adults. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition using a stop-signal task (executive function domain: inhibition). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (pre-SS vs pre-SE) with thresholding and stereotactic coordinates, and performs ROI and ROC analyses. A within-group task contrast is explicitly reported. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results are reported as voxelwise maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly tests cognitive control, response inhibition, and conflict during an intentional false-response task—clearly within executive function domains (inhibition, cognitive control). The methods report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FDR-corrected) with reported clusters/coordinates and figures for within-group contrasts (FALSE > TRUE; FALSE_AUTO > TRUE_AUTO). Task is task-based, with within-group contrasts against baseline/other conditions. Participant sample is healthy adults and qualifies under participant inclusion. Results are presented as tables/figures with coordinates. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This study reports an fMRI n-back working memory task (phonological and spatial), which is an established executive function domain. It provides voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (ON>OFF, PWM>SWM, SWM>PWM) with thresholding and coordinate localization, and within-group contrasts are reported. Results are presented in tables/figures and fully described in text. Participants are a human sample (healthy adults). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is an empirical fMRI study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (executive function) using a task-based Sternberg paradigm. The paper reports first-level contrasts (loads 5/7/9 modeled with load 3 baseline) and a second-level/group analysis with probands, co-twins, and controls modeled separately, indicating group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps and within-group task contrasts. ROI analyses are also reported, but whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (partial slice coverage but voxelwise analysis used). Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (clinical participant groups allowed), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Small sample size is noted but does not disqualify inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (ANOVAs and paired t-tests) with cluster-size correction and presents within-group task>fixation contrasts for each participant group (controls, schizophrenia patients, siblings). Results include within-group activation maps and tables/figures describing whole-brain task-related activations across stimulus types. Participant groups include clinical samples. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical work) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and there are no applicable exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) that reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain activation results (LST vs rest and LST vs Listen) and provides coordinates/tables. Analyses include within-group contrasts for participant groups (HSS and LSS). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an auditory 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM activation maps (grouped session-specific maps) and single-session voxelwise maps, based on whole-brain EPI acquisition. Within-group task contrasts (2-back task vs rest/baseline) are reported. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Results are presented as voxelwise statistical maps and ROI summaries. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only contrasts; not a non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is an fMRI study of episodic memory encoding/recognition (continuous face-recognition) rather than an executive function or cognitive-control task. Although it includes voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts, it does not assess tasks within the meta-analysis’ specified executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because it does not assess executive function or cognitive control tasks as required by I5/I6. While it is an empirical fMRI group study with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and within-group task contrasts and reports coordinates (satisfying I7, I8, I9, and I10), the experimental tasks are object categorization, recognition memory, and a mental-rotation/object localizer—these are perceptual, memory, and spatial processing tasks rather than established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore I5 and I6 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI experiment reporting group-level voxelwise task activation maps (rest vs. motor task), with partial-brain acquisition but voxelwise analyses. The paradigm examines timing/predictability of externally cued finger movements and specifically addresses preparatory/initiation processes (readiness potential), which falls under the ‘initiation’ executive-domain listed in inclusion criteria. A within-group task contrast is reported, and whole-brain voxelwise statistics and functional images are presented. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, contains within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Some uncertainty remains whether a simple motor execution task is considered an executive ‘initiation’ task for the meta-analysis, so confidence is moderate (0.75).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (attentional control using Stroop-like tasks). The paper reports within-group voxelwise group-level contrasts (incongruent vs. neutral) with whole-brain statistical maps and peak coordinates (Talairach), despite limited slice coverage (15 slices) which is allowed. The tasks fall squarely within executive function domains (inhibition/attentional control). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is appropriate to include in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of stimulus–response incompatibility that probes cognitive control/inhibition and working-memory demands. The abstract reports within-group task contrasts (mixed vs compatible; VGS/compatible vs fixation) and names activated cortical regions, indicating task-evoked activation maps. Inclusion criteria met based on available text: I5 (fMRI task-based study) and I6 (task within executive function domain: inhibition/working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), and I9 (participant group acceptable). Full text is not provided here (only title/abstract/metadata), so I cannot confirm whether group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate reporting are explicitly present (I7/I10 unverified). Therefore fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the abstract.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (MAT vs MAT_CONT, REP vs REP_CONT, REP vs MAT) with SPM group maps thresholded and cluster criteria; analyses are whole-brain voxelwise (despite limited slice coverage, which is allowed). Results are reported in figures/tables and described in the text. Participants are a healthy within-group sample. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and figures/tables; it appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study (meta-analysis of nine PET activation protocols) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level contrasts (SPM conjunction analysis) comparing REST to task conditions. The protocols include tasks within executive function domains (spatial working memory, mental calculation/reasoning, tasks requiring manipulation/inhibition), and at least one within-group task contrast (REST vs each task) is reported and analyzed. Whole-brain maps and stereotactic coordinates are provided and compared across studies. The sample (63 healthy participants) and analyses satisfy the review’s participant and analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not purely connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, and the paper is empirical. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study that explicitly investigates cognitive control/conflict detection and resolution (ACC–PFC mechanisms) during the tip-of-the-tongue (TOT) state. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with corrected statistics and ROI follow-ups, and includes within-group contrasts (TOT vs know vs don’t know and task vs baseline). Participants are human healthy adults. Although the task is semantic retrieval rather than a canonical working-memory or task-switching paradigm, the authors frame and test it as a cognitive-control/conflict-monitoring task analogous to Stroop-style conflict and post-retrieval monitoring; therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirement to assess executive/cognitive-control processes within established executive function constructs (conflict/inhibition/monitoring). Full text is complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based sustained attention (Conners’ CPT) paradigm, which maps to the executive domain of vigilance (I5, I6). Methods describe voxelwise SPM5 analysis with preprocessing, normalization and group-level analysis of 9 subjects to obtain mean activation maps (within-group active vs rest t-tests), satisfying whole-brain, group-level voxelwise reporting and a within-group task contrast (I7, I8). Participants are healthy adults (acceptable per I9). Results report whole-brain activation patterns in text/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in schizophrenia patients and healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (second-level SPM results) including within-group contrasts (2-back > 0-back and 0-back/2-back versus fixation) with whole-brain and small-volume-corrected results, and tables/figures of activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion, allowing verification of analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task-based, within-group, whole-brain study that reports voxelwise contrasts (semantic vs phonological lists and vs baseline). However, the task targets language processing (attention to semantic and phonological relations) rather than established executive function domains enumerated in the inclusion criteria (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) reporting within-group task effects and training-related Time × Task interactions. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (group-level and single-subject), including cluster-corrected statistical maps and stereotactic coordinates. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI of executive function, whole-brain voxelwise results, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based n-back working memory paradigm (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise within-group contrasts (e.g., 1-/2-/3-back vs 0-back; parametric complexity effects; verbal vs spatial contrasts) analyzed with SPM and random-effects group maps. Although slice coverage omitted inferior occipital/cerebellar regions, analyses were voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is acceptable per criteria. Coordinates and cluster tables are reported. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a GO/NOGO inhibition task (an executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise thresholding, cluster extent, Talairach normalization) and presents within-group contrasts (Stops vs baseline; separate Fast and Slow conditions analyzed with one-sample t-tests and between-condition ANOVAs). Participants are healthy adults; results are reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an N-back working memory task (executive function domain) with whole-brain BOLD acquisition and voxelwise group-level analyses. The authors created single-subject contrasts and performed second-level (1-sample t-test) group maps and reported voxelwise task-evoked activations (including coordinates and ANOVA results), satisfying within-group task contrasts. Methods, results, and discussion are present, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain executive-function fMRI are met.

Full text is complete and reports an fMRI study with voxelwise, within-group task contrasts (perceive emotion vs control; label emotion vs control) and provides coordinate/whole-brain results. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise/whole-brain analyses, partial-brain acquisition acceptable), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (clinical and control groups both reported), I10 (results reported in text/tables). However, the task paradigm is affective face perception/labeling (emotion processing), which does not fall within the meta-analysis' required executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore I5 and I6 are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Because not all required inclusion criteria are met (specifically I5 and I6), the study must be excluded from the executive-function meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines working memory (verbal N-back) — an established executive function domain — in postmenopausal women. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses using SPM2 (e.g., 3-back > 0-back contrasts), with coordinates and cluster statistics corrected for whole-brain search, and includes within-group task contrasts and paired t-tests. Results are reported as cluster coordinates and described in the text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based n-back working-memory paradigm (one-back vs two-back) that probes executive function (working memory). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (e.g., WM load high > low, Pain × Visibility interactions) using SPM2 with corrected thresholds and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. At least one within-group task contrast is presented (high vs low WM load and main effects), and results are reported in the text with coordinates. Participants are a healthy within-group sample (16 males), which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating top-down attentional control (zooming in/out) in healthy adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and includes coordinate tables and contrasts (e.g., zooming out > zooming in, conjunctions vs HLB). These are within-group task contrasts and therefore provide task-evoked activation maps appropriate for meta-analysis. The task probes cognitive control/top-down attentional processes (vigilance/attentional control), which fall under executive function/cognitive control domains. Participants are healthy adults, and whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Go/NoGo motor inhibition task (executive function: inhibition). The paper reports within-group contrasts (correct NoGo minus correct Go) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with coordinates and cluster statistics. Participant groups include manic patients and healthy controls, and within-group task activation maps are described for each group. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of antisaccade and visually guided saccade tasks (inhibition/volitional saccade generation), which falls within the executive function domain of inhibition. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 with random-effects statistics, reported statistical maps, tables of activation coordinates, and figures. Within-group contrasts are reported (saccade vs control; antisaccade vs control; antisaccade vs saccade). Participant sample is a within-group healthy adult cohort. Results are presented as voxelwise activations and coordinates in the text/tables/figures. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (4T) that reports group-level voxelwise activation contrasts for an attention-shifting task. The task operationalizes nonspatial shifting of attention (feature-based set-shifting), which maps to cognitive flexibility (an executive function domain). Within-group voxelwise contrasts are reported (shifting attention vs sustained attention; sustained attention vs fixation), with group-level statistical maps, reproducibility maps, and tables of stereotactic coordinates (Talairach) for activated centroids. Although some acquisitions focused on cerebellum only, study 2 used whole-head volume coil allowing stereotactic, voxelwise, group analyses. The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based, rule-guided go/nogo paradigm that requires inhibition and rule-based decision-making (executive functions). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain group analyses (SPM99) contrasting ocular baseball conditions (decided-go/decided-nogo) with control conditions, with thresholding and Talairach coordinates. Thus it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition/rule-based executive function), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (results clearly reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is present (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The methods describe voxel-based (voxelwise) analyses and report group activation maps (supplementary figures), and percent signal change relative to baseline, indicating within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline and domain-specific contrasts). Both clinical (Turner syndrome) and control groups have within-group activation results. Reporting includes whole-brain voxel-based analysis (not ROI-only) and figures/tables of activations. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The provided text describes an fMRI task of working memory order (meets I5 and I6) and reports a within-subject contrast comparing Order vs Item conditions (meets I8). Any participant group would be acceptable (I9). However, the full text appears to be only an abstract/summary and does not provide sufficient methodological detail to verify that group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps were produced or reported (I7 not confirmed). Because I7 is a required inclusion criterion and cannot be confirmed from the incomplete/fulltext provided, the study is excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met based on the available information.

The study is an fMRI/EEG investigation of working memory (an executive function) using task-based paradigms, with within-group contrasts and healthy participant samples. However, the fMRI analyses are reported primarily as subject-specific ROI extractions and ROI-based time-course analyses; the paper does not present a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation map. Because the study reports only ROI-focused voxel selection and subsequent ROI analyses without group-level voxelwise activation results, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I6 (working memory task), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant group). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study reports task-based verbal working memory (Sternberg) activations, with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) including linear and quadratic load contrasts and load 6 vs 2 within-group contrasts, and practice (session) effects. Methods and results include voxelwise statistical maps, thresholding, and tables/figures of coordinates. All inclusion criteria are satisfied: it is an fMRI task of working memory (I5, I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (I7), reports within-group task contrasts (I8), includes a participant group with within-group results (I9), and reports voxelwise results/coordinates in tables and figures (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text is not available (only abstract/metadata and a note that PDF is paywalled). Abstract indicates an fMRI 1-back working memory task in Alzheimer’s patients and reports group differences, so it likely meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (working memory). Participant groups (AD and controls) are reported, so I9 is met. Results are described in text (brain regions), so I10 is provisionally met. However, the full article (methods/results) is not accessible here, so I cannot verify key required criteria: I7 (that a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported) and I8 (that a within-group task contrast is reported for at least one group). Because these cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the full article. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are demonstrably met with available information.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg paradigm) in schizophrenia and healthy controls. The paper reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., 5-target vs Arrows) and averaged group-level statistical maps with Talairach coordinates and thresholding across voxels (voxelwise analyses). Partial-slice acquisition was used but analyses are voxelwise and group-level, meeting the meta-analysis whole-brain requirement. Both clinical and control participant groups have within-group activation contrasts reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (tables of Talairach coordinates and figures). Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., first vs. last maintenance-retrieval, parametric exponential modulation across blocks, task vs baseline), and results are presented in the text, tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts are reported for this group). Thus all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain activation maps are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is an empirical study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based study using the PASAT, a well-established working memory/executive task. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level (random-effects) whole-brain analyses (SPM99), including within-group one-sample t-tests (PASAT > control task) and between-group contrasts, with activation clusters and MNI/Talairach coordinates reported in tables/figures. Participant groups include clinical (CISSMS/MS) and healthy controls. Results include regional activation maps and correlations. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, conclusions) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met.

The provided full-text appears to be an abstract/summary (fulltext_incomplete=true) and the study does not clearly test an executive function domain. While this is a task-based fMRI study and reports within-group task contrasts (speech vs tone), the task is a phonological speech-discrimination paradigm focused on segmentation and perceptual phonology. The authors only speculate that frontal activation may reflect working-memory demands; the task was not designed or described as an executive function (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, etc.) task. I therefore judge that inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met, and I cannot confirm I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group maps) from the incomplete text. The study meets I8 and I9 (within-group contrasts and a participant group), but does not satisfy the core requirement that the paradigm assesses executive function/cognitive control. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on the available content.

Full text is incomplete (only references/metadata provided). Cannot verify whether the study meets inclusion criteria: no methods, participants, tasks, analyses, or results are present. Inclusion criteria met: none (I5-I10 not verifiable). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (fMRI/PET task-based paradigm not confirmable from content), I6 (task falls within executive function domains not established; virtual radial arm maze likely spatial/navigation rather than core executive domains), I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps reported in the provided content), I8 (no within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (participant groups not described in full text), I10 (no whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E6 can be confirmed from the incomplete text. Because core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing, I must exclude. Recommend obtaining the complete full text and re-screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm that reports within-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain analyses relevant to executive function domains. The study explicitly models and reports contrasts such as Action Planning > Coasting and Traffic Rules > Coasting (planning and rule retrieval/control), which map onto established executive domains (planning; rule maintenance/cognitive control). Images were acquired with whole-brain coverage and analyzed at the group level using SPM2 with random-effects t-tests; results are reported as voxelwise activations and peak coordinate tables. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and tables, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is a task-based, event-related fMRI study that investigates interval encoding and decision processes, including working memory and decision-making components relevant to executive function. The full text includes introduction, methods, voxelwise group-level statistical analyses (mixed-model ANOVAs), whole-brain activation results reported in tables/coordinates and figures, and within-group contrasts (encoding > baseline; hard vs easy decision contrasts). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. The manuscript thus meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements for (1) task-based fMRI of executive/cognitive control processes (working memory/decision-making), (2) tasks within an executive domain (working memory), (3) voxelwise whole-brain/group-level analyses, (4) within-group task contrasts, (5) acceptable participant group, and (6) reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (contains methods, results, discussion).

Study is an event-related fMRI investigation of working memory (an executive function) using a task-based paradigm in premanifest Huntington’s disease and healthy control groups. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level spatial ICA maps that were temporally sorted to the task delay period and tested with within-group one-sample t-tests (FWE-corrected), satisfying whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map requirements. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrast/maps), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates and results reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task maps, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a delayed match-to-sample paradigm that explicitly engages working memory and categorization processes. It reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise contrasts (e.g., CAT vs AUD) with thresholded statistical maps and tables of peak coordinates. The contrasts are within-group task contrasts (category discrimination vs auditory discrimination), and the acquisition/analysis is voxelwise (SPM random-effects), so even if slice coverage was partial it still qualifies. Participants are healthy volunteers. Results are reported as figures and tables (coordinates). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not trigger any exclusion criteria (E3–E6).

This is a task-based fMRI study that examines sentence comprehension with explicit working-memory/executive demands. It reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM99 analyses and provides within-group task contrasts (sentence conditions vs pseudofont baseline) for healthy seniors and FTD subgroups (PNFA, EXEC). Results are reported as coordinates and described in the text. Participants include clinical groups (FTD subgroups) and controls. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study is an fMRI investigation of auditory digital working memory (meets I5, I6) with a within-group task contrast (working memory vs control; meets I8) in healthy adult participants (meets I9). However, the paper does not report a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical activation map or stereotactic coordinates. Analyses appear to rely on visualization of single-subject activation images and region-of-interest counts analyzed with the McNemar test, rather than a voxelwise group SPM or equivalent. Therefore it fails I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis). This constitutes exclusion under E3 (reports only ROI/ non-voxelwise analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines mental calculation while explicitly dissociating components that include working memory, inner speech, and rule-based manipulation. The tasks clearly engage executive processes (notably working memory and rule-based planning/decomposition) so they fall within the executive function domains specified. The study reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (with coordinates, figures and tables) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., calculation vs pseudo-calculation, substitution vs calculation). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). Although the sample is small and analyses use a fixed-effects model, these limitations do not violate the meta-analysis inclusion rules. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is excluded because it does not provide the required whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation results or report a within-group task contrast suitable for inclusion. (a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (an fMRI experiment was performed to localize LDLPFC), I6 (task falls within executive function — verbal working memory/reading span), I9 (a within-group participant sample of healthy adults is reported). (c) Inclusion IDs NOT met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map or whole-brain activation map is reported in the full text; fMRI results are only described as subject-specific/localization), and I8 (the paper does not present a clear within-group voxelwise task contrast map or statistical activation maps for the RST at the group level). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study does not meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive set-shifting (a cognitive flexibility/executive function task) with healthy participants. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects GLM results (FDR-corrected whole-brain maps) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., negative vs positive feedback; first vs subsequent events; task vs fixation baseline). Coordinates and maps are described in text/tables/figures. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation mapping and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and references, so appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study using a 2-back verbal working memory task (an executive function) with healthy participants. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM96 (images transformed to stereotaxic space, smoothed, thresholded and cluster-reported) and within-group task contrasts (WM vs control and comparisons with/without rTMS). Results are reported as distributed activations/deactivations with statistics and anatomical labels. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion provided.

This is a task-based fMRI empirical study of working memory (an executive function domain) in an elderly group. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (voxel-level threshold P<0.001 uncorrected) and describes whole-brain activation maps and ROI results for within-group task contrasts (read+memory and recognition phases vs baseline). Tasks clearly fall within executive function domains (working memory), and results are reported in text, tables, and figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI, task-based experimental study of working memory (executive function) with within-group task contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise analyses at the individual subject level; however, the paper does not report a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I6 (working memory domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group qualifies), I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no clear group-level voxelwise statistical map reported; results are described primarily per subject with averaged coordinates rather than a group-level voxelwise statistical map). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are applicable. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude because it fails to satisfy I7 required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study reporting voxelwise group contrasts (SPM Z-maps) with task vs control block contrasts in healthy participants, and whole-brain results are described in the text/tables. Thus I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. However, the experimental paradigms are lexicosemantic decision, tone discrimination, and visuomotor sequence learning (language, auditory discrimination, and motor learning), which do not fall within the review's predefined executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore the study does not meet I5 (fMRI/PET study assessing executive function tasks) or I6 (tasks within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory/item-recognition) and I6 (working memory is an established executive function domain) are satisfied based on the abstract. However, I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) and I8 (a within-group task contrast reported) cannot be verified from the provided content. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met, but because core full-text information (methods/results showing voxelwise group analyses and contrasts) is missing, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all required inclusion criteria. Therefore excluded due to incomplete/full-text verification failure.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based counting Stroop (executive/inhibition) paradigm. It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM99 analyses including whole-brain contrasts and small-volume corrections, and provides within-group incongruent vs. neutral task contrasts with coordinates and tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy volunteers. Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps (SPM) for within-group task contrasts (COPY, PHONO, PUZZLE vs rest/controls). The PHONO task explicitly engages phonological retention/transfer (verbal working memory), and PUZZLE requires visuospatial manipulation and motor planning — both mapping onto established executive domains (working memory and planning/manipulation). Although the study’s primary focus is handwriting, the reported whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (with partial-slice coverage) and within-group contrasts satisfy the meta-analysis requirements. Results are presented as activation maps, ROI counts and statistical comparisons across tasks. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (executive domain) that reports within-group task contrasts and random-effects group analyses, satisfying I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I8 (within-group contrasts), and I9 (acceptable participant group). However, the authors state that "All our analyses were performed with ROIs," and group tests collapse across voxels within ROIs rather than presenting a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analysis) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI/small-volume analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of the stop-signal task (inhibition), reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., SS vs G, SE vs G, pSS vs pG, pSE vs pG). Participant sample is healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are reported as voxelwise activations with family-wise error correction and coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The provided full text is incomplete and appears to be a non-empirical review (Nature Medicine 1995) consisting only of references and metadata, with no methods, results, or original human neuroimaging data. Exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical papers/reviews without original human neuroimaging data) applies. No inclusion criteria are met: there is no task-based fMRI/PET experiment (I5 not met), no executive-function task identified (I6 not met), no group-level voxelwise whole-brain maps reported (I7 not met), no within-group task contrast (I8 not met), and nothing to evaluate regarding participant groups (I9 not met) or reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures (I10 not met). Additionally, the supplied text is only references (fulltext_incomplete=true), preventing confirmation of any qualifying analyses.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm (immediate serial recall and control repetition) probing working memory, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM (fixed-effects SPM[t] images, normalization, smoothing, voxelwise contrasts) and provides statistical thresholds and coordinates for activations and deactivations. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., main effect of working memory [RM+RS+RQ] − [CM+CS+CQ] and interaction [RM−CM] − [RS−CS]), satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in text with coordinates. The full text provided contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of feedback-based rule learning involving intradimensional/extradimensional rule shifts (cognitive flexibility), an executive function domain. It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2; negative>positive contrasts with tables/coordinates and figures), within-group task contrasts (negative vs positive feedback; ID vs ED), and ROI follow-ups. Participants are healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical).

The study reports an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (2-back CPT), an established executive function domain. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed using SPM (one-sample t-test for 2-back vs 0-back and regression analyses), and coordinates/cluster statistics are reported (e.g., BA10 cluster). At least one within-group task contrast (2-back vs 0-back) is presented for a participant group (healthy adults). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a sustained and an epoch-related sequential two-back working memory task (an established executive function). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses: epoch-related task activations/deactivations modeled with SPM2 (GLM) and second-level random effects maps (figures and tables describe voxelwise results and thresholding). It also includes within-group task contrasts (WM vs rest/visual fixation) and reports coordinates/figures for whole-brain results. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines inhibition-related processes (inhibition of return) — mapping onto the executive domain of inhibition. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level contrasts (e.g., Long_SOA (Cued+Uncued) > Short_SOA (Cued+Uncued); Cued > Uncued at long SOA) analyzed with a random-effects flexible factorial in SPM5. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported with cluster-level correction and coordinates in MNI space. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task within ‘inhibition’ executive domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group participant sample), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures, references).

Full text incomplete: provided HTML contains no article content (only empty <head> and <body>). Based on title and metadata, the study appears to be an event-related fMRI task of context processing in schizophrenia, so I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (executive/cognitive control domain: context processing/working memory) and I9 (participant group: clinical sample acceptable) are likely met. However core inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the incomplete text: I7 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise map) not verifiable, I8 (at least one within-group task contrast) not verifiable, I10 (reporting of whole-brain results/coordinates) not verifiable. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are explicitly met based on available info. Because the full article (methods/results/discussion) is missing, I must exclude the study pending full text.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of interference resolution / inhibitory control within working memory (executive functions). It reports task-based, within-group voxelwise group analyses (interference vs control contrasts) using whole-brain voxelwise statistics (z-maps, Talairach coordinates, p<0.001) and provides tables/figures of activations. Participants are healthy adults; at least one within-group task contrast is reported. Although slice coverage was limited (14 slices), analyses were voxelwise and partial-brain acquisition is allowed by the inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text is complete.

Full text is unavailable (API error in provided full text), so critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified. Based on title/metadata, the study likely used fMRI and a Stroop (inhibition) task in bipolar patients, supporting I5 (task-based fMRI/PET), I6 (executive function: inhibition), and I9 (clinical participant group). However the full article is needed to confirm whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I7), presence of at least one within-group task contrast (I8), and whether whole-brain results are reported in acceptable formats (I10). Because these essential inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included.

This is a motor execution fMRI study (finger tapping with visual cue) that investigates temporal modulation and motor sequencing, not executive functions. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain RFX maps reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts vs baseline/task conditions), I9 (healthy volunteer participant group reported), I10 (whole-brain results described with coordinates and figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (does not assess executive function/cognitive control), I6 (task does not fall within executive domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the review’s executive-function task domain.

This is an fMRI task-based study probing executive function domains (verbal working memory and selective attention). The manuscript reports within-group, voxelwise task contrasts (NT–CT for Sternberg working memory; TO–RS and TO–DO for the selective attention task) and combines individual maps into group-level whole-brain maps normalized to CMNI space with cluster thresholds and z-statistics, satisfying whole-brain, group-level task-evoked mapping. Behavioral and fMRI results, methods, and discussion are present (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only contrasts; this study provides within-group activation maps). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that elicits cognitive control/conflict (incongruent vs congruent prosody/semantics), i.e., inhibition/attentional control. They report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (contrasts including CONF vs NOCONF) with corrected statistical maps and coordinate tables. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participants are healthy adults. All inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based saccade countermanding paradigm that probes inhibitory control (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (e.g., main effect of time F-maps thresholded and displayed), despite ROI-focused follow-up analyses and partial dorsal-cortex slice coverage; partial-brain acquisition is allowed. Within-group contrasts are reported (STOP-success, STOP-fail, GO, CATCH; STOP vs GO etc.). Participant sample and full methods/results/discussion are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Although primarily a methods/power-analysis paper, the full text reports original task-based fMRI data including a verbal working memory (executive function) experiment with a group-level random-effects, voxelwise contrast (working memory vs rest) across 12 subjects and reports activation maps/ROIs. This satisfies executive-function task domain (working memory), a within-group task contrast, and group-level voxelwise results. The paper contains complete core sections (intro, methods, results, discussion) and empirical data (not solely methods or simulations), so it does not meet exclusion criteria (e.g., not a review/methods-only paper). Therefore it is eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory/episodic memory in schizophrenia and reports within-group task vs fixation effects computed within anatomically defined thalamic ROIs. Exclusion met: E3 — the paper presents only ROI-based analyses and does not report any group-level voxelwise (whole-brain) task activation maps in this full text (the authors reference whole-brain analyses published elsewhere). Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive-related working memory), I6 (tasks fall within executive function domains — N-back working memory), I8 (within-group task contrasts against fixation were computed), I9 (clinical participant group reported). Inclusion not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise/whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps are reported in this article). Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study that probes executive-function domains (working memory) with task-based within-subject contrasts and healthy participants, but the reported analyses are restricted to ROI-based small-volume-corrected measures rather than whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/cognitive tasks), I6 (working memory is an established executive domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts used to generate single-subject activation maps), I9 (healthy participant group qualifies). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; the authors explicitly used ROIs and SVC and derived ROI/BOLD metrics rather than presenting whole-brain voxelwise group maps or coordinate tables). Exclusion criterion triggered: E3 (study reports ROI/SVC analyses without voxelwise whole-brain results). Full text appears complete for screening.

Although this is an empirical PET study with voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses and a within-group task contrast (baseline vs numerical calculation), the imaging task (numerical calculations) is not clearly an established executive-function/cognitive-control paradigm (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The study assessed executive function behaviorally (neuropsychological tests) but did not report a task-evoked activation map for an executive-function task per se. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 and I6, despite meeting I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are directly triggered by the report. Full text is complete.

The paper reports an empirical task-based fMRI study probing the central executive component of working memory (number subtraction task). It includes voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (SPM99 one-sample t tests; coordinates and thresholding reported), and reports within-group task contrasts (high-demand vs low-demand; each subtraction condition vs baseline). Results and coordinates are presented in text/tables/figures. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Inclusion criteria met (from available text): I5 — fMRI task-based study; I6 — task involves sustained attention (vigilance), an executive function domain. Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed from provided content: I7 — no sufficient information showing a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map; I8 — no explicit within-group task contrast (group-level voxelwise contrast) is reported in the provided text. Exclusion criteria met: none (E3,E4,E5,E6 do not apply based on abstract). Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I8) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive control (dual-task) training reporting task-evoked activation maps. It includes group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (Z-statistic images, cluster thresholds) and reports within-group task contrasts (DM > SM, SM > SP) and pre/post (time) contrasts. Behavioral and neuroimaging results, tables/figures, and peak coordinates are provided. The manuscript is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive function studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (meets I5) with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and reported Talairach coordinates (meets I7 and I10). It reports within-group task contrasts (conditional vs. baseline, relational vs. baseline) (meets I8) in a healthy adult sample (meets I9). However, the experimental tasks are deductive reasoning problems rather than tasks that clearly fall within the review's specified executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). While the authors discuss working memory/central executive involvement, the primary task is reasoning, not a canonical executive-function task; therefore I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task-based study using a classic visual oddball paradigm that probes attention/vigilance and working memory processes (executive domains). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain (near full coverage) activation maps for both low-risk and high-risk groups and presents within-group task contrasts (task vs implicit baseline) as well as between-group comparisons. Methods detail voxelwise permutation-based analyses and corrected activation maps. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function/cognitive control), I6 (task maps to working memory/attention/vigilance), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis, albeit with limited frontal/temporal coverage noted), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported for each group), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is an fMRI investigation that includes a continuous verbal 2-back working memory task (I5, I6 satisfied). However, the paper reports connectivity analyses (ICA, marginal and partial correlations) of the default mode network during rest and the 2-back task and does not present any group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or within-group task activation contrasts. Therefore it reports only connectivity analyses / resting-state/task-modulated connectivity without providing the required voxelwise activation maps, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map) and I8 (within-group task contrast) are not satisfied. Because of E4, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis of task activation maps.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) contrasting fixed vs. random sequence conditions and time effects. Although the primary paradigm is an implicit serial reaction time (DoSRT) motor-learning task, the authors explicitly interpret key activations in terms of spatial working memory and response monitoring/selection—domains within established executive function constructs. Results are reported with stereotaxic coordinates and cluster-corrected voxelwise statistics. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI task assessing executive/cognitive-control-related processes (I5), falls within executive domains via working memory/response monitoring (I6), provides whole-brain voxelwise group maps (I7), includes within-group task contrasts (I8), involves an eligible participant group (I9), and reports coordinates/tables (I10). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function). It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group analyses (SPM2) with thresholded statistical parametric maps and tables of coordinates, and presents contrasts of interest (manipulation vs maintenance; high vs low load) for participant groups. Although acquisition used noncontiguous slices (partial-brain coverage), analyses were voxelwise and therefore qualify under the review’s allowance for partial-brain studies. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text provided is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata). Based on available abstract, the study meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (working memory task) and indicates group-level subject analyses consistent with I9 (within-sample reporting). However, the full text does not allow verification of essential meta-analysis requirements: I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) and I8 (at least one within-group task contrast explicitly reported) cannot be confirmed from the abstract alone. I10 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures) also cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and the full text is incomplete, I exclude this record pending access to the complete article.
