This is an fMRI task-based empirical study of executive-function tasks (Stroop, response inhibition, Sternberg) and reports within-subject/task contrasts and healthy adult participants; however the paper performs ROI-based analyses and does not present group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain, group-level voxelwise evidence (I7) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no voxelwise group results). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study (Young et al., 2005) reports whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps (Experiment 1) and within-group contrasts (NPE vs PE) and thus meets I5, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the task probes learned irrelevance / associative attentional learning rather than a canonical executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The task does not clearly fall within the meta-analysis’ required executive-function domains (I6 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I6.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts (imitation vs incongruous; imitation vs spatial), reported with coordinates and images. Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (eligible participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported). However, the experimental task targets imitation/perception–action matching (a social sensorimotor process) rather than a canonical executive function domain. Although the authors discuss involvement of working memory and inhibition, the primary task is not designed to probe established executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Thus it fails inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (color–word Stroop: inhibition/cognitive control). It reports group-level, voxelwise mixed-effects whole-brain analyses (FLAME) with tables of peak coordinates and figures, and includes within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; one-word vs four-word). Participants are healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based 2-back working memory paradigm (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects, FDR-corrected maps) and provides Talairach coordinates and condition contrasts (Word, Cross, Within) and comparisons against baseline/rest, satisfying within-group task contrasts. Participant sample is healthy adults. Results are reported in text, figures, and coordinates. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study that reports voxelwise, whole-brain task activation maps for executive function paradigms. It includes within-group task contrasts (WCST vs control and RPM vs control) analyzed with SPM voxel-by-voxel methods and reports group-level statistical maps and tabulated maxima. The WCST is a canonical executive function task (cognitive flexibility/working memory) and RPM engages higher-order reasoning/working memory; thus tasks fall within the review's executive domains. Participant sample (healthy adults across 18–80) is acceptable. The paper provides full methods, results (voxelwise maps, statistical thresholds, coordinates), and discussion, meeting the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

Excluded because the study reports ROI-confined fMRI analyses focused on the anterior cingulate cortex rather than a group-level, voxelwise whole/partial-brain task activation map. Exclusion criterion met: E3 (ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task = sustained attention/vigilance, an executive function domain), I8 (within-group task contrast: no-pain vs pain components tested), I9 (clinical and healthy participant groups allowed). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported; analysis restricted to ACC ROI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study using an n-back working memory task (executive function) with a balanced placebo design. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2) including within-group task contrasts (3-back vs baseline) with tables of coordinates and figures. The methods, results, and discussion are provided in full. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group is acceptable), and I10 (results reported via coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete. The confidence is high because the full methods and voxelwise group results are reported in the full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based verbal Sternberg working memory paradigm (an executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise single-subject and group-level analyses (FEAT/FSL, FLAME) with within-group contrasts (WM vs rest; linear and nonlinear load contrasts) for children, adolescents, and adults. Results are reported as group statistical maps, cluster tables, and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (2-back), an executive-function domain. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (2-back minus 0-back) at the second-level random-effects model and an interaction contrast ((2-back–0-back)_caffeine – (2-back–0-back)_placebo). Results are reported with cluster-level statistics and coordinate tables/figures. Participants are a defined group (healthy adult males). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function: working memory). It reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., Task > fixation; set-size effects) and uses group-level voxelwise analysis (Task > fixation reported at P<0.05 corrected) to define ROIs, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise evidence. Coverage omitted only the bottom of the cerebellum (partial-brain acquisition acceptable). Behavioral and fMRI within-group contrasts are reported and analyzed. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses of a task requiring interference resolution and working memory (arithmetic verification: incorrect vs correct equations). It includes within-group contrasts (incorrect vs correct; arithmetic vs control), uses random-effects group analysis and voxelwise SPM statistics, and reports activation clusters in prefrontal and parietal cortex. Task demands map onto executive function domains (working memory, interference/inhibition). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text incomplete: only title and abstract are available. From the abstract, the study meets I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (WCST — cognitive flexibility), I8 (within-subject task contrast: WCST vs sensorimotor control), and I9 (clinical participant group allowed). However, I7 (clear evidence of a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) cannot be confirmed from the abstract, nor can I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). It is therefore not possible to verify that the study provides the required voxelwise whole-brain activation data; the methods/results needed to rule out ROI-only analyses (E3) are missing. Because the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text review.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise contrasts relevant to executive function domains. It includes a spatial working memory task (within the working memory domain) and a sustained spatial attention task (vigilance/attention domain), meeting the review’s executive-function task requirements. Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise (SPM, random-effects; results reported with whole-brain correction and peak coordinates) and include within-group contrasts (attention vs control, WM vs control, delay vs baseline). Participants are healthy adults (acceptable), and results are reported in text, figures, and coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (update vs. hold; RULE vs. NMBR). Methods and results describe voxelwise GLM, cluster-corrected thresholds, and extracted beta weights; supplemental tables are available online. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Thus the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (task-based fMRI, executive function domain—working memory, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, within-group contrasts, participant group reported, and acceptable reporting via text and supplemental materials). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based operation span working memory paradigm that targets the central executive/semantic coding (executive function). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects), provides voxelwise thresholds and Talairach/MNI coordinates in tables/figures, and presents within-group task contrasts (Concrete vs Abstract and task vs baseline). Participants are healthy adults. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The supplied full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical PET study using task-based paradigms (uncovered and covered maze) that probe spatial working memory and planning (executive functions). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM (voxelwise contrasts such as C−A, D−A, C−B, D−B, D−C, and combined contrasts), with stereotactic coordinates and SPM{Z} maps described in the text and tables. Multiple within-group task contrasts are presented (e.g., covered vs motor control, uncovered vs motor control), satisfying the requirement for within-group activation maps. Participants are healthy right-handed adults. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task that probes context representation, maintenance, and selection (missing-letter task), which maps onto executive functions (working memory/selection). The paper reports whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise GLM analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., context-appropriate vs context-inappropriate; task vs baseline), with results described across frontal and temporal regions. Participants are healthy adults. The report is a full-text article including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (Arrow task requiring response inhibition/cognitive regulation) with within-group voxelwise contrasts (Reverse vs Go) reported for both heroin-dependent patients and healthy controls. The authors conducted whole-brain, second-level SPM2 analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent, generated t-maps, and report activations (tables/figures), fulfilling whole-brain reporting and coordinate reporting. All required inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). None of the exclusion criteria apply: analyses are voxelwise whole-brain task activations (not ROI-only), not connectivity-only, and within-group contrasts are reported (not only between-group). Full text appears complete (includes background, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This is a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study that reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts probing deception (lying) vs truth and true vs false recognition. The deception contrasts are explicitly interpreted as engaging executive functions/cognitive control (lateral prefrontal activity), which maps onto established EF domains (inhibition/response control). Analyses use whole-brain voxelwise statistics with reported coordinates and thresholds, and conjunction and ROI follow-ups. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts (e.g., LN vs CR, LT vs TR, TR vs FR) are reported. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for task-based executive-function-related fMRI, whole-brain voxelwise results, and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study (working memory 2-back) that reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps and within-group task contrasts. The paper presents voxelwise correlation and GLM/contrast images (group-level maps), reports within-group task effects (task vs fixation and task differences within controls and patients), and provides figures/tables of whole-brain results. Participants include a clinical sample (schizophrenia), which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI study of saccade (oculomotor) task with repeated measures following theta-burst TMS. It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects GLM) and reports within-group contrasts (saccade vs fixation), so I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. However, the task does not probe established executive function domains listed in I6 (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation); it is an oculomotor/saccade execution paradigm rather than an executive-control task. Therefore I5 and I6 are not met, so the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive control mechanisms (conflict detection, selection/inhibition) during selective retrieval. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task contrasts (e.g., retrieval success vs failure; first vs third retrieval practice) and whole-brain regression analyses with coordinates and ROI follow-ups. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Although the paradigm is episodic retrieval, the study explicitly targets executive control processes (ACC, DLPFC, VLPFC) and memory suppression (inhibitory control), fitting the review’s executive-function/inhibition domain. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The available content is limited to chapter title and abstract; full text (methods, results, analyses) is not provided. From the abstract, the study is an fMRI Stroop task examining attentional selection, so it clearly meets I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function) and I6 (inhibition domain). However, I7 (confirmed whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) and I8 (at least one within-group task contrast explicitly reported with verifiable details) cannot be verified from the abstract alone. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because I7 and I8 cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study cannot be included per the review’s requirement that ALL inclusion criteria be verifiable. Recommend obtaining the complete article; inclusion may be possible if group-level voxelwise within-group contrasts are documented.

Full text (abstract) indicates an event-related fMRI study with group-level voxelwise analyses and a within-group contrast (orthographically related vs unrelated distractor conditions). However, the task is a picture–word naming/priming paradigm focused on lexical access and phonological/orthographic facilitation, which does not clearly fall within the predefined executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Note: No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group reported/acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (fMRI/PET assessing executive function or cognitive control task), I6 (task within established executive function domains). Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/title provided).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a Go/No Go inhibition paradigm (executive function) with whole-brain voxelwise SPM2 analyses. The paper reports within-group contrasts (errors of commission and correct rejects vs Go baseline) for OCD patients and healthy controls, provides group-level voxelwise results with coordinates/tables and figures, and has full-text methods, results, and discussion. Coverage includes clinical and control groups. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based delayed matching-to-sample paradigm that probes mismatch/conflict during brief working memory (executive) processing. The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (incongruent vs congruent), group-level activation maps and statistical thresholds (voxelwise composite maps, ROI analyses, Talairach-normalized maps), and behavioral results in healthy adults. Partial brain coverage (12 axial slices) is reported but permitted by the criteria because voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study satisfies I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps for a Go/NoGo response inhibition task (executive function: inhibition). The full text contains introduction, methods (scanning and analysis), results (tables of significant clusters and coordinates), and discussion. A within-group task contrast (STOPS vs baseline/tonic task activity) is reported, and results are presented with cluster maps and coordinates. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based whole-brain fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (high vs low load contrasts), conjunctions, and tabulated coordinates/figures for activations. Tasks fall within the working memory domain and include within-group task contrasts (high>low load) suitable for inclusion. Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain), using a task-based delayed-recognition paradigm (meets I5 and I6). The study used whole-brain echo-planar imaging and reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (normalized group-average t-maps and ROI-based analyses derived from voxelwise contrasts), satisfying I7. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., Delayunfilled RVF vs Delayunfilled LVF; Delayunfilled RVF+Delayunfilled LVF; filled vs unfilled), meeting I8. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy young adults (I9), and results are reported in figures/tables and described in text (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper includes voxelwise task activation maps (not ROI-only), is empirical task-activation fMRI (not connectivity-only), reports within-group contrasts (not only between-group), and is primary empirical research (not review). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes a Stroop color-word interference paradigm (an inhibition executive function task). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs. neutral) and voxelwise group-level analyses across subjects, with whole-brain statistical maps (group activation maps displayed at corrected P < 0.001 and data transformed to stereotactic space). Resting-state data are used for CNR analyses but the functional experiment provides task-evoked activation. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented as group-level voxelwise activations (figures and descriptive text). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task domain, imaging modality, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, within-group contrasts, participant inclusion, and reporting. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise analyses (random-effects group analyses, paired t comparisons, and conjunctions) and reports task-evoked activation coordinates (Talairach x,y,z) for activation maps and contrasts (emotional vs neutral distracters; correct vs incorrect trials). Thus it provides group-level voxelwise task activation results (qualifying whole-brain/voxelwise maps reported in text/figures/coordinates) and at least one within-group task contrast. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes a counting Stroop (interference) task—a canonical inhibition/executive function paradigm—and reports group-level, voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM2 fixed-effect group maps) with coordinates and figures. Within-group contrasts are reported (reading vs rest; neutral and interference counting vs rest). Although the paper focuses on connectivity (Bayesian networks), it also provides whole-brain within-group activation maps and tables of coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures).

This is an empirical PET task-based study using the Hayling Test to probe verbal initiation and suppression (executive functions). It reports group-level, voxelwise statistical parametric mapping (SPM) analyses and within-group contrasts (e.g., initiation vs reading; suppression vs reading). Although the scanner had limited 10 cm field-of-view, analyses were voxelwise and whole-brain inference was reported where possible. Participants are healthy volunteers (within-group data are provided). Results are reported in the text with statistical thresholds and anatomical localization. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria are violated. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical PET task-based study directly assessing an executive function (manipulation/updating component of working memory). It reports group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (ANCOVA, SPM(t)/SPM(Z)) across subjects with whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (manipulation vs serial, memory vs reading, interaction, conjunction, post-hoc contrasts). Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., alphabetical vs serial; reading vs recall). Participant sample (healthy adults) is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based working memory paradigm (Sternberg Item Recognition) — an executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects contrasts, Talairach and surface-based maps) and provides coordinates/tables and figures of activation. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (Encode vs fixation, Delay contrasts, Probe contrasts). Participant group (healthy adults) is an allowed sample. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables, references) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses and multivariate (MLM/CVA) results derived from voxelwise contrasts (load-dependent slopes) and presents within-group activation patterns for young and older adults. The paper includes complete methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (working memory task), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts and group-specific expressions), I9 (participant groups reported), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract confirms this is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (so I5 and I6 are satisfied). However, I cannot verify whether the paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (I7), whether a within-group task contrast is reported (I8/I9), or whether whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) are clearly met based on the available information. Because critical methodological details cannot be confirmed from the provided content, exclude pending retrieval of the complete full text.

Excluded because the study does not evaluate a task that clearly falls within established executive-function domains (I6) nor does it explicitly assess executive function/cognitive control as required by I5. The paper reports fMRI whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Rotation>Control; Intact>Scrambled) with group results (I7, I8) on healthy participants (I9) and reports voxelwise results in text/figures (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. However, the tasks are primarily visual object categorization and mental rotation (spatial/perceptual), not standard executive tasks (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation); therefore I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a visual oddball paradigm that probes selective attention/vigilance (executive domain). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level GLM analyses (cluster-corrected Z>2.3) and describes whole-brain target-related BOLD maps and residual-variance maps. A within-group contrast (target vs baseline) is explicitly analyzed for participant groups (healthy adults), and whole-brain results are presented in text/figures. All required methodological details (subjects, task, MRI acquisition, voxelwise group analyses) are present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI, task-based, within-group study that reports whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and coordinates. The encoding task requires maintaining an initial associate across a delay and binding it with a later stimulus, engaging working memory/maintenance processes (an established executive function domain). The paper reports multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., hit discontinuous association vs. hit simultaneous association; successful associative encoding vs. misses) using whole-brain random-effects voxelwise statistics (with SVC for MTL as supplement) and presents coordinate tables and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or between-group-only, empirical human fMRI data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating alertness (phasic alertness/vigilance-related attention) using within-subject, within-group contrasts (cued vs uncued) and random-effects voxelwise whole-brain analyses. The tasks map onto an executive domain listed in the inclusion criteria (vigilance/alertness). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise activation results (coordinates, conjunctions, SPM analyses) and provides whole-brain voxelwise contrasts under placebo and nicotine, satisfying the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Results are reported as coordinates and statistical maps/descriptions. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided.

The study is an fMRI investigation of auditory orienting and inhibition of return (an attentional/overt orienting phenomenon), not a task probing established executive function domains (working memory, response inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore it does not meet I5 (fMRI assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task within established executive function domains). The provided full text appears to be an abstract/summary rather than the complete article, so fulltext_incomplete=true. The study does report within-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain activation descriptions (satisfying I7, I8, I9, I10), but because it fails the core domain criteria (I5, I6) it must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an emotional Stroop task (a cognitive control/inhibition paradigm) with voxelwise whole-brain analyses. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (separate activation patterns for controls and for euthymic bipolar patients), and also reports between-group contrasts; imaging was whole-brain (28 axial slices, 300 volumes) with thresholded voxelwise results presented in figures/tables. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI studies (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References).

This study reports task-based fMRI of an n-back working memory task (executive function domain: working memory) with group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99 random-effects), including within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back > 1-back) and reported results in tables/figures. The paradigm and analyses directly assess cognitive control/working memory and provide voxelwise activation maps and interaction effects (e.g., visibility × load) suitable for inclusion. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results (group fMRI results, tables), and Discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (2-back), which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise second-level group analyses (one-sample t-tests for within-group contrasts and two-sample t-tests for between-group contrasts) using SPM, with contrasts such as 2-back > 0-back and 2-back degraded > 0-back degraded reported for both patient and control groups. Results are reported in tables/text and are voxelwise rather than ROI-restricted. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Based on the abstract, the study used event-related fMRI on a working memory (executive function) task and reports within-subject contrasts (maintenance vs selection), so it satisfies I5, I6, I8 and I9. However, I cannot verify I7 (that at least one analysis is a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) from the available text, nor confirm I10. Because full-text methods/results are not available to confirm whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (and the review requires verification of whole-brain voxelwise reporting), I am excluding the study pending access to the full article. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I8, I9. Inclusion criteria NOT confirmed: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I10 (reporting format). Exclusion criteria met: none (E3-E6 not confirmed). Full text incomplete: true.

Excluded per E5. This is a PET, task-based study that reports group-level voxelwise contrasts, but the contrasts are drug (nicotine) vs placebo during an aggression provocation task rather than task-evoked activations (task vs baseline) in an established executive-function domain. It therefore does not provide a within-group task activation contrast required for the meta-analysis. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E5. (b) Inclusion IDs met: none. (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (does not assess executive/cognitive-control task as defined), I6 (Bushman Aggression Task is not one of the specified executive domains; CPT was mentioned but no task-activation maps were reported), I7 (no group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reporting task vs baseline), I8 (no within-group task contrast for any group). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task (PVSAT) that probes working memory and executive processes. The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (SPM2 one-sample within-group contrasts for controls, CIS, and CDMS; two-sample between-group tests), with thresholds and cluster correction described and figures/tables of activations provided. At least one within-group task contrast (calculation vs control) is reported for each group. Results are reported in text, figures, and tables of coordinates, meeting the reporting requirements. The study thus satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory/central executive processes (operation span dual-task), meeting executive-function domain criteria. The manuscript reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 with random-effects models and corrected thresholds (P < 0.05 voxel- and cluster-level), tables/figures of activation coordinates, and within-group task contrasts (Arithmetic+Memory vs baseline and dual-minus-single contrasts). Participants are a healthy adult sample (within-group contrasts reported). Results include voxelwise activation maps, coordinates, and statistical thresholds. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain within-group activations are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM99; voxelwise thresholds reported, maps/figures described) contrasting memory conditions with matched control tasks (within-group contrasts). Whole-brain preprocessing and voxelwise statistics are described; results reported voxelwise (P<0.05 corrected and P<0.001 uncorrected). Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided full text.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (semantic event sequencing requiring planning/sequencing). The paper reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts (PS>CON) for both HIV+ and Control groups with whole-brain correction (FDR) and provides coordinate tables and figures. Group-level random-effects analyses and voxelwise functional connectivity and activation maps are reported. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (executive function domain: planning/sequencing), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant groups allowed), and I10 (results reported as figures/tables/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Based on the abstract and metadata, this is an empirical PET activation study using a task-based paradigm (simple calculation and number repetition) in healthy volunteers. The tasks engage executive function domains (working memory/phonological store and articulatory loop) and report group-level activation patterns across multiple brain regions, implying voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts (calculation vs repetition/baseline). Therefore the study appears to meet inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the provided full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided), so core methods/results/discussion cannot be verified; fulltext_incomplete is set to true and lowers confidence. Recommend obtaining the full article to confirm voxelwise whole-brain analyses and exact contrasts before final data extraction.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive-function domain). The study reports within-subject, within-group voxelwise contrasts (face vs control, encoding vs retrieval, memory delay vs control) derived from whole-brain echo-planar acquisitions and group-level voxelwise statistics with reported coordinates and ROI maps. Results include voxelwise maps, volume changes, and Talairach coordinates. Participants are a human within-group sample (healthy young adults). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, references included).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) using a Sternberg-variant task. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects t-maps contrasting negative vs. positive responses (a within-group task contrast), with thresholding and Talairach coordinates reported across the whole brain. Participants are a healthy sample (undergraduates), and full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of conflict/inhibition (numerical Stroop) examining cognitive control processes. It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (t and F contrasts) including within-group contrasts (conflict vs nonconflict; error vs correct), with coordinates and detailed methods and results. The participant sample (18 healthy adults) is acceptable. Whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise random-effects analyses are described; results are reported in tables/coordinates. All inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This study reports an empirical PET task-based investigation of working memory (an established executive function domain) in humans, with group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses comparing task versus rest within the physostigmine and control groups. Methods and results describe whole-brain voxel-by-voxel analyses (SPM), thresholded statistical maps, and within-group task contrasts (rest subtracted from task) and group-level comparisons. Participant sample is reported and a within-group task contrast is provided. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (task-based PET of executive function, working memory task, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, within-group contrasts, any participant group allowed, and reporting of whole-brain results in text/figures).

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps and within-group task contrasts for an executive task. The letter-fluency task is a canonical executive function (initiation/switching/verbal fluency) and was implemented as a block-design fMRI paradigm. The methods describe voxelwise median activation maps computed across subjects and thresholded, and group-level cluster-wise statistics; results are presented with cluster centroids/coordinates and tables. Although acquisition uses limited (14-slice) coverage, analyses are voxelwise and thus meet the partial-brain allowance. A clinical participant group (non-demented ALS) is included and within-group task contrasts (task vs baseline) are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based executive function paradigm (counting Stroop; inhibition). Methods describe whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (mixed-effects; thresholded Z statistical images) and report coordinates/tables and figures. Within-group I–N (interference minus neutral) contrasts were performed for each condition (Trp and Placebo), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5-I10). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures; not truncated. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-group, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., untrained vs trained, trained vs untrained, fact retrieval vs number matching) using SPM random-effects analyses with tables/figures. Tasks involve significant working-memory and planning/executive demands (complex mental multiplication) and the paper explicitly interprets activations in terms of working memory and executive processes. Participants are healthy adults and contrasts are within-group. Whole-brain voxelwise results are reported in tables/figures and described in the text. The full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop task (inhibition/selective attention), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM group activation maps) and provides within-group contrasts (Stroop activation vs. rest) for both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients, with tables of coordinates and figures. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, within-group contrasts are present, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a visual N-back working memory paradigm (an established executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (parametric working-memory load; corrected voxelwise thresholding) and within-group task contrasts (parametric increase contrasts and mean activation versus baseline), with results presented in figures/tables. Participants (chronic smokers) are an eligible group and within-group contrasts are reported for them. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (attention-switching/working memory) with healthy adult participants. It reports within-group, voxelwise group-level statistical analyses (one-sample t-tests and repeated-measures voxelwise ANOVAs) and whole-brain activation maps (with cluster-corrected thresholds). Tasks fall clearly within working memory/executive domains, and results are reported across the brain (voxelwise maps and ROI follow-ups). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm that probes working memory (an established executive function domain) via structured vs. unstructured digit sequences. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects; whole-brain FDR thresholding; coordinate reporting) and presents within-group task contrasts (structured > unstructured during encoding and delay). Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in text, figures and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI task-based study with within-group voxelwise analyses (object change vs no change) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain coordinates. However, the paradigm investigates visual object and spatial discrimination/perception and medial temporal lobe involvement, not an established executive function or cognitive control domain. Although the authors speculate about short-term visual working memory, the task involves simultaneous comparison with minimal retention and was explicitly designed to minimize declarative memory demands; it does not operationalize working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation as defined by the meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met, despite I7, I8, I9 and I10 being satisfied. Full text is complete.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Abstract indicates an empirical PET study of verbal working memory (meets I5, I6), uses task and control conditions consistent with a within-group task contrast (meets I8), and includes human participants (meets I9). However, I cannot verify from the provided content whether a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map was reported (I7) or whether results are reported in the forms acceptable per I10. Because the full text (methods/results) is not available, key inclusion criteria (particularly I7) cannot be confirmed and exclusion via inability to verify is necessary pending retrieval of the full article.

Full text is incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates a task-based 18FDG-PET working memory study (so I5, I6) with within-group contrasts implied (I8) and includes clinical groups (I9). However, I cannot verify whether group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps were reported (I7) or whether results/coordinates sufficient for inclusion were provided (I10). Because the complete methods/results are not available, I cannot confirm the critical whole-brain voxelwise evidence required by the review. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone, but inability to verify I7 and I10 prevents confident inclusion. Therefore I exclude this record pending access to the full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study that explicitly investigates planning, an established executive function domain (planning). It uses a task-based within-subject design (Final Goal vs Immediate Goal) and reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects whole-brain analyses (SPM; cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates/figures described. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI task-based), I6 (planning), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (color-word and emotion-word Stroop tasks involve inhibition/selective attention). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (incongruent-minus-neutral; negative-minus-neutral) and group-level voxelwise statistical maps (paired t tests, thresholded via Monte Carlo simulations/AlphaSim), with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reported activations. Tasks fall within the inhibition/executive control domain. Participants are a within-group sample. Results include voxelwise group maps (figures, ROI and whole-brain cluster-based maps). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (object and spatial delayed-recognition), which is an established executive-function domain. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (mapwise contrasts and thresholded activation maps) and provides within-group task contrasts vs. fixation and object vs. spatial contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), Results (mapwise, regional, ROI analyses) and Discussion, indicating completeness. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (within-group contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cued task-switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility). Methods report group-level, voxelwise GLM contrasts (random-effects t-tests, contrast maps transformed to z-scores) and selection of ROIs from whole-brain contrasts; contrasts include within-group task comparisons (e.g., combined conditions vs null, switch vs repeat, left vs right responses). Participants are healthy adults and within-group analyses are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not a non-empirical methods paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based counting Stroop (executive control/inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (incongruent > congruent contrast), provides group-level within-group activation maps for both patient and healthy groups, and reports coordinates/figures. Core sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activation maps and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical PET task-based study of executive function (working memory updating) that reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM95) comparing a within-group task contrast (variable-target vs fixed-target). Results are reported with Talairach coordinates, figures, and a table of activations. Participants are a healthy adult sample. Therefore the study meets I5 (PET task assessing executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group qualifies), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This PET study reports voxelwise, group-level task activation contrasts comparing simultaneous interpreting (SI) vs shadowing within eight professional interpreters, using SPM and whole-brain subtraction analyses. The SI task clearly engages verbal working memory and related cognitive-control processes (described in the paper), placing it within established executive-function domains (working memory/controlled retrieval). Group-level within-subject contrasts (SI vs shadowing; direction contrasts) are reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level inference, satisfying whole-brain, task-evoked mapping requirements. The participant sample is acceptable, and results are reported in text/figures. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI task-based study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility) that reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (searchlight maps normalized and subjected to second-level voxelwise statistics) and within-group contrasts/testing of decoding accuracy against chance. Participants are healthy adults. The report includes full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function fMRI and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory with distraction (executive function domain). The paper reports task-based fMRI analyses (I5) using a working memory paradigm (I6). The methods describe whole-brain activation maps and voxelwise linear contrasts (delay1 vs baseline) used to define ROIs and secondary uniform-threshold whole-brain analyses, indicating group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (I7). Multiple within-group task contrasts and within-subject comparisons (e.g., delay1 vs baseline, face/scene vs face/face) are reported (I8). The sample is a within-group healthy adult cohort (I9) and whole-brain results are described in the text and analyses (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an established executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise surface/volume analyses and contrasts (e.g., EAR > NO-MEMORY, EAR > EYE) that are within-group task contrasts. Whole-brain analyses and statistical maps are described and thresholding/clusters reported; supplemental data and coordinates are available. Participants are healthy adult subjects. The report also includes methods, results, and discussion (full article content provided). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical).

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E5 — the paper reports behavioral group comparisons but provides no within-group task-evoked whole-brain activation maps or voxelwise task contrasts for any group. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I6 — the tasks are within an executive function domain (working memory). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no fMRI or PET task-based activation data are reported in this paper; the authors used behavioural versions of tasks previously used in fMRI studies), I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain activation maps are provided), I8 (no within-group task activation contrasts are reported), I9 (requires a within-group task contrast for at least one participant group — not met), I10 (not applicable because no whole-brain imaging results are reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not provide the task-evoked neuroimaging activation maps required for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (face recognition within a working memory/search task), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses: voxelwise thresholds (Z>3.09), counts of significant voxels across six participants, Talairach coordinates, and regional volumes—i.e., whole-brain activation results reported as coordinates/figures. Within-group task contrasts are reported (targets vs nonrepeated distracters; repeated distracters vs nonrepeated distracters), and behavioral within-group results are also presented. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion included).

This fMRI study directly investigates working memory (an executive function domain) using a task-based retro-cueing paradigm and reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked analyses. The paper includes whole-brain statistical comparisons (FDR-corrected), ROI and time-course analyses, and a table of coordinates for network activations. Within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., cue vs implicit baseline; switch vs stay), and analyses are conducted on healthy participant groups. Results include voxelwise maps and coordinate tables, satisfying requirements for inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI task study of response selection (executive/cognitive control). It reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level SPM contrasts (e.g., free selection vs externally specified, action vs colour, main effect of task vs rest) with whole-brain inference and tables of coordinates. The paradigm probes executive selection processes (selection/choice), satisfying executive-domain criteria. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults (n=12). Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and coordinate tables/figures, indicating complete full text for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a working memory task (executive function domain) with whole-brain, voxelwise group- and within-group analyses reported. The manuscript includes full methods, results (within-group task>rest and stage-specific contrasts), and coordinates/cluster statistics, meeting all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function activations. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text is complete. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/interaction with retrieval), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported, e.g., Strong > Weak and Weak > Strong), I9 (healthy adult participant group; within-group contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Did NOT meet I6: the experimental task is an associative episodic recognition memory task, not one of the listed established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation); although the paper examines cognitive-control-related regions (ACC, DLPFC), the primary task does not fall within the required EF task categories. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI (overt word-generation paradigms) using voxelwise whole-brain analyses and within-group task contrasts. Evidence: (1) fMRI acquisition and GLM analyses are described in detail; (2) tasks (categorical, alphabetical, semantic word generation) map onto executive processes (initiation/controlled retrieval and cognitive control of language production); (3) voxelwise statistical maps (t- and F-contrasts) and mixed-effects analyses are reported; (4) within-group contrasts (paradigm vs baseline per session and mixed-effect across sessions/subjects) are explicitly tested; (5) participants are human healthy volunteers. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation that includes a sustained visual attention (vigilance) task and directly reports whole-brain voxelwise group-level contrasts (task>baseline, ER>VA, VA>ER) using SPM99 with tables/figures of coordinates. This satisfies inclusion: I5 (fMRI task-based study), I6 (vigilance – an executive function domain), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample), and I10 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Tables, References). Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Continuous Performance Task (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise GLM analyses (random-effects t-maps for CPT vs control) used to select voxels/VOIs and to compare within-group activation patterns; although analyses focus on frontal mask, the procedure used voxelwise statistics (partial-brain voxelwise analysis is acceptable). Within-group contrasts are reported for control and patient groups. Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and matched controls. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

While this is an event-related fMRI study using an anti-/pro-saccade task (an inhibition-based executive function), and it reports within-group contrasts and Talairach coordinates, it does not present a group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the main event-related analyses. The authors used single-subject localizer voxelwise maps to define ROIs and then extracted ROI time courses for group ANOVAs; the primary analyses are ROI-based/ROI-extracted rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map. Therefore Inclusion criteria I5, I6, I8, I9, and I10 are met, but I7 (group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map) is not met. This study effectively reports ROI-based analyses without the required group-level voxelwise activation maps, meeting Exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI methods paper using visual stimulation (flashing checkerboards) and simulations to compare GLM modeling approaches. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, within-group task contrasts and group maps, so it meets I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results reported as maps/statistics). However it does NOT assess executive function or cognitive control tasks and does not use tasks within established executive-function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, flexibility), so it fails I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study is excluded because it does not address the meta-analysis objective of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (novel AX-CPT) in healthy adults. The full text reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (random-effects second-level maps, FDR-corrected) and within-group task contrasts (reward expectancy, verbal/spatial bias, all-tasks vs rest). It also reports coordinates and figures for activations and includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (a core executive function) that reports group-level, voxelwise SPM2 analyses and group maps with stereotactic peak coordinates. The paper provides within-group task contrasts (encoding, delay, retrieval; delay-period activity contrasted against baseline), includes healthy participant data, and presents whole-brain voxelwise results in figures/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical article) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based 2-back verbal working memory paradigm (an executive function), with group-level, voxelwise SPM99 whole-brain analyses reported (coordinates and cluster sizes). The paper reports within-group task-related rCBF changes (2-back vs reference) and correlations of performance with rCBF, meeting the requirement for within-group contrasts. Results are reported as voxelwise maps/coordinates. All inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based mental rotation paradigm that explicitly probes visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM2 random-effects group analyses (one-sample t-tests for within-group activation maps, two-sample and paired t-tests for between-group contrasts) and provides tables/figures with coordinates. The primary within-group contrast (mental rotation vs passive viewing/control) is reported for each group. Participant characteristics and hormone-state manipulations are detailed but do not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and within-group contrasts are present). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study examines inhibition (a core executive function) with task-based fMRI and within-subject contrasts (INT vs COV), and reports behavioral, ERP, and fMRI results. However, the fMRI analysis is ROI-based (AROI parcellation) with AROI-level statistics rather than group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function/inhibition), I6 (task falls within inhibition domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (acceptable participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise whole-brain task activation map reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study using an emotional Stroop paradigm that requires participants to inhibit word meaning and report ink color (an inhibition/cognitive-control executive function). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (negative vs neutral; positive vs neutral), provides cluster-thresholding and coordinates/tables, and extracts within-group activation maps and ROIs. Multiple participant groups are included and within-group contrasts are explicitly reported. Therefore it satisfies I5 (fMRI task), I6 (inhibition/cognitive control task), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task (antisaccade/prosaccade delayed saccade paradigm) that probes inhibition and volitional response generation—core executive functions (inhibition/response control). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM2), whole-brain activation maps and cluster-level results (tables and figures), and within-group contrasts (e.g., standard antisaccade vs fixation; delayed task phases). Participants are a within-group healthy sample. Results are reported as coordinates and SPMs with full methods, results, and discussion. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This fMRI study uses a task-based continuous performance test (CPT), which falls under vigilance/attentional executive functions. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses (task vs baseline and degraded vs non-degraded contrasts), with whole-brain voxelwise inference constrained by anatomical masks and tables of peak coordinates and figures. Within-subject contrasts were generated and entered into second-level (within-group and between-group) analyses; task main effects and condition (degradation) effects are modelled and reported. Results include coordinate tables and activation maps and psycho-physiological interaction analyses, so the paper provides task activation maps (voxelwise) and within-group contrasts for at least one group. Participants include clinical groups (schizophrenia) and healthy controls. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of decision-making that explicitly tests cognitive control/conflict (ACC, DLPFC) during moral dilemmas. The task is task-based and requires inhibition/cognitive control (overriding prepotent emotional responses), meeting the executive-function domain (inhibition/cognitive control). Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain and ROI-constrained contrasts (e.g., high-RT vs low-RT; utilitarian vs nonutilitarian) reported with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction. Within-group task contrasts are reported and RT was controlled in comparisons. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Results are presented in the full article (text, figures, and reported thresholds/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual-spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (mixed-effects ANOVAs, corrected cluster thresholds), within-group task contrasts (main effect of time maps for each age group; long vs short delay contrasts within groups), and provides coordinates/figures/tables of activations. Participant groups include children, adolescents, and adults. The paper is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, nor solely between-group contrasts. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI of working memory and spatial attention within the same subjects. The abstract describes group-level conjunction and double-subtraction analyses that identify distributed activations across frontal and parietal regions, indicating voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses and within-group contrasts. These features satisfy inclusion criteria for an executive-function (working memory) task-based fMRI study with within-group contrasts and group-level voxelwise results. I cannot verify full article contents (methods, results tables/coordinates, or figures) because only the abstract/metadata were provided; therefore fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are apparent from the abstract. Inclusion criteria applied are listed below.

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study that explicitly investigates a cognitive control strategy (‘reality checking’) during anticipation of emotional stimuli. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses and within-group contrasts (e.g., negative vs neutral; unknown vs neutral) with Talairach-transformed whole-brain results reported in tables/figures. Participants are human (healthy adults). Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so it appears complete.

Full text is complete. The study uses task-based fMRI of working memory (an executive function), reports within-group contrasts (Order vs baseline) in healthy adults, and meets I5, I6, I8, I9, and I10. However, all reported group-level results are ROI-restricted (analyses conducted on predefined ROIs with ROI-based statistics reported) and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task-activation map is presented. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis) is not met and exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no voxelwise results) applies.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based flanker/ANT variant that probes executive function (inhibition/cognitive control). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (group-averaged activation maps and random-effects contrast maps with FDR thresholding) and extracts regional hemodynamic timecourses. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., incongruent > congruent/low-arousal; high-arousal > low-arousal within groups), and results are presented across both neurotypical and autism participant groups. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and provides coordinates/figures of whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes an n-back working memory paradigm (an established executive-function domain) and an auditory target detection task. It reports group-level, voxelwise task activation maps (group t-maps and thresholded activation networks), and within-group contrasts (sustained attention > fixation; average 1–2–3 back > ‘look for X’). Whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are presented (figures/tables of activations and ROIs) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. Participants are human (healthy adults). The full-text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function in ASD and controls. It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (Random > Baseline; Stimulus-Oriented > Stimulus-Independent) analyzed with SPM2 across whole-brain volumes, includes coordinate tables and corrected thresholds, and describes results for each group separately. Tasks map onto executive domains (random generation: inhibition/cognitive flexibility; alphabet task: attentional selection/multitasking/prospective memory). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). The abstract confirms a PET task (degraded CPT) examining glucose metabolism correlated with task performance, so I5 (PET task) and I6 (vigilance/executive domain) are met, and I9 (participant groups) is met. However, the available content does not allow verification of I7 (presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps) or I8 (at least one within-group task contrast such as task vs baseline). The abstract reports region correlations for selected regions, which could reflect ROI-only analyses (potential E3), but this cannot be confirmed. Because core article content (methods, voxelwise results, statistical maps) is missing, inclusion criteria I7 and I8 cannot be confirmed; therefore the study is excluded pending full text. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be definitively applied from the abstract alone.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm of vigilance/selective attention (executive domain: vigilance). It reports voxelwise, whole-brain SPM analyses and provides group-level within-group contrasts (S vs NS, time-on-task covariate) with coordinates and thresholded statistical maps. Participants are a healthy adult sample (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.
