The abstract describes a methods-focused paper proposing a modification to proportional scaling and notes use of an event-related oddball paradigm and a block-design working memory task to illustrate the model. This indicates the study addresses executive-function tasks (working memory) and uses task-based fMRI (satisfies I5 and I6). However, the provided content does not allow verification of critical inclusion criteria: no full text or results are available to confirm the presence of whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (I7) or that at least one within-group task contrast is reported (I8). Because these criteria cannot be confirmed from the incomplete record, the study is excluded pending the complete full text. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I7, I8. Exclusion criteria met: none (insufficient information to apply any E3–E6).

This fMRI study includes an event-related Sternberg working memory (WM) task, which falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports within-group, whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses (single-subject maps and random-effects group-level SPM5 analyses), and compares activation maps before and after latency correction. Participants are human adults and a within-group task contrast (WM task vs baseline/control) is presented. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly manipulates and tests top-down intentional control (instructions to ‘remember’ vs ‘look’) and examines resulting changes in mid-ventrolateral prefrontal activity. It therefore assesses cognitive control/executive function (intention/initiation of mnemonic processes). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM random-effects), with multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., high-intention encoding vs low-intention encoding; task vs non-event baseline). Results are presented with coordinates, tables, and figures. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Given these points, the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (task switching) in healthy adults. It reports within-group, group-level voxelwise contrasts (task-switching conditions vs baseline; main effects and interactions) using whole-brain SPM analyses with reported voxelwise thresholds and tables/figures of activations. Tasks map onto cognitive flexibility/switching (an established executive function domain). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI including a visuospatial working memory task (an executive function), with within-subjects, group-level random-effects, voxelwise contrasts (experimental minus control). Whole-brain coverage was used and voxelwise statistical maps and voxel counts are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I6 (working memory), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a delayed-match-to-sample working memory task (an executive function domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM99 time-series modeling, parametric maps per subject, brain-wide Ordinal Trend CVA) and provides group-level results with Talairach coordinates and figures for encoding, retention, and probe phases. Within-group task contrasts (e.g., retention phase 6-item vs baseline; ordinal trend across 1/3/6 loads) are reported, and behavioral correlations are presented. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Although this paper reports group-level, voxelwise fMRI contrasts (random-effects SPM analyses) and within-group task contrasts on a healthy adult sample (satisfying I7, I8, I9, I10), it does not assess an executive function or cognitive-control task as defined by the review inclusion list. The paradigm is a visuospatial attention/visuomotor study probing implicit visuomotor responses to graspable objects (spatial orienting), not tasks in the specified executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

Full text is incomplete (provided content shows API error). From available metadata/title: fMRI study and oddball task => meets I5 (task-based fMRI) and I6 (oddball = vigilance/attention). However the full text does not allow verification of required criteria: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps) not confirmed; I8 (within-group task contrast reported) not confirmed; I10 (reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures) not confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3-E6) can be assessed as met. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot verify key inclusion criteria (I7, I8, I10) necessary for inclusion, so the study is excluded pending full-text access.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (Visual Delayed Matching to Sample), which falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM2 analyses (contrast: 4s delay minus 1s delay) isolating working memory, and provides tables/figures with coordinates of whole-brain results (Tables 2 and 3, Figure 2). A within-group task contrast is reported and analyzed at the group level. Acquisition and preprocessing indicate voxelwise whole-brain normalization and smoothing; partial-brain coverage would still qualify but here voxelwise analyses are present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that administered a 2-back (working memory) and 0-back control task (executive function domain: working memory). The paper reports within-group task contrasts (2-back vs 0-back and each condition vs rest) using group-level voxelwise analyses (ICA followed by GLM) and provides Talairach coordinates and group results. Although acquisition covered only two contiguous slices (partial-brain), the criterion allows partial-brain voxelwise analyses and the study performed voxelwise, group-level statistics. Behavioral and imaging methods, results, and discussion are fully reported. Therefore the study meets the inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study using task-based paradigms that probe spatial working memory (memory-guided saccade and spatial working-memory tasks), which fall within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports voxelwise task-evoked analyses (Fourier-based and regression-based voxelwise maps), within-group contrasts (task vs fixation/baseline and task conditions), and group-level summaries (Talairach coordinates, group polar plots, mean volumes). Although acquisition covered frontal, parietal, and dorsal occipital cortex (partial-brain coverage), the analyses were voxelwise and meet the whole-brain/partial-coverage allowance. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical restrictions). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) with event-related design and appropriate task contrasts. Group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses are reported (e.g. L1>control, L2>L1, L3>L2 and within-group paired t-tests for targets vs non-targets) with whole-brain coordinates and cluster statistics; results were reported as voxelwise maps and coordinates. At least one within-group task contrast is provided. Participants are a healthy adult sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete reporting). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a task-based spatial working memory (delayed-recognition) paradigm, reporting group-level voxelwise activation maps and contrasts (memory vs control; positive vs negative probes). The manuscript contains full methods, results, figures, and coordinate-based reporting of supra-threshold clusters (Talairach coordinates) and group composite maps, satisfying whole-brain voxelwise analysis requirements. It reports within-group task contrasts (memory > control; negative > positive probes) and includes healthy adult participants. Reporting of results in text, figures, and tables satisfies acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI task-based study of verbal working memory (an executive function). It reports within-group, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with whole-brain inference (voxel- and cluster-corrected results) and provides coordinates and figures. The contrasts include memory vs control (letter recognition vs letter case judgment), meeting within-group task-contrast requirement. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Because core article content is missing, I cannot determine whether the study provides qualifying voxelwise within-group task activations; per instructions I mark fulltext_incomplete=true and exclude pending full-text availability.

This is an empirical fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise/surface-based statistical maps (permutation-corrected group t-maps) and within-group task contrasts (encoding, maintenance/delay, response; and MGS vs SIR contrasts). Although imaging coverage emphasized frontal/parietal regions via custom coils, analyses were voxelwise/surface-wide and therefore satisfy partial-brain but voxelwise requirements. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activations and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (auditory 2-back working memory). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPM second-level 1-sample t-tests) and within-group task contrasts (2-back series vs baseline) with results presented in tables/figures and described in the text. The study uses healthy adult participants. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (haptic orientation matching), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (contrasts such as exploration vs ITI, matching vs ITI, intermediate vs short delay, long vs intermediate delay) with tables of Talairach coordinates and figures. At least one within-group task contrast is reported. Participants are a healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using a task that manipulates working memory (retro-cueing of spatial attention) — an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (mixed-effects), with cluster-based thresholding and presents coordinates and figure/table results for within-group task contrasts (e.g., interaction [(Q4 − Q2) − (N4 − N2)], N4−N2), satisfying voxelwise within-group contrasts. Participants are healthy volunteers; analyses and results are fully described (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (an executive function domain). The paper reports a within-group contrast (Incorrect Matching minus Correct Matching) using voxelwise t-tests averaged across the five subjects, with activation maps spatially normalized to Talairach space and Talairach coordinates/cluster volumes reported. Scanning covered the whole brain (20 axial slices to cover whole brain) and results are presented as group-level statistical maps (thresholded t-maps, clusters reported). Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (inhibition task), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinates/maps reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical human neuroimaging). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a target-detection oddball paradigm to probe cognitive control/executive processes (vigilance/attentional control). The paper reports within-group, whole-brain, voxelwise mixed-effects analyses (shape targets vs novels; face targets vs novels; direct contrasts), with coordinates and figures, and thus provides task-evoked group-level statistical maps/results. Participant group and reporting meet eligibility. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly examines working memory (active maintenance) — an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects statistical parametric maps and provides stereotactic coordinates for activations (whole-brain analyses, with correction and ROI follow-ups). Within-group task contrasts (delay/maintenance vs baseline; encoding/retrieval vs baseline; novel vs familiar) are reported. Participant groups are healthy adults; within-group contrasts are provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so content appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with tables and figures. The tasks involve dynamic manipulation of auditory imagery and working memory/central executive processes (word reversal) and rhyme judgment; these fall within established executive function domains (working memory/manipulation). Within-group contrasts are reported (word reversal vs baseline, rhyme judgment vs baseline, and word reversal minus rhyme judgment). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is included. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive processes involving working memory/executive resources during quantifier comprehension. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (random-effects SPM contrasts) and provides coordinate tables and figures of activations. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., verification/proposition+response minus proposition alone; higher-order vs first-order quantifiers), with healthy adult participants. Results are presented in tables and figures in the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion all present). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations: (I5) fMRI task assessing executive function, (I6) tasks tapping working memory/executive domain, (I7) whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, (I8) within-group task contrasts, (I9) acceptable participant group (healthy adults), and (I10) whole-brain results reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study probing working memory/executive function (memory-guided and colour-coded manipulation of saccade sequences), meeting the review objective. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 preprocessing and a nonparametric random-effects group analysis with SnPM2) and presents within-group task contrasts (memory-guided vs fixation; colour-coded memory-guided vs fixation; retention-period and manipulation contrasts). Participants are a healthy volunteer group, and results are reported in standard coordinate/cluster form in the text/tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (cognitive flexibility/task switching). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (GLM, random-effects), presents activation maps and coordinate tables, and reports within-group task contrasts (e.g., switch vs repeat main effect and interactions). Participants are healthy adult subjects (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition, preprocessing, whole-brain contrasts), Results (behavioral and whole-brain activation maps), and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI (simultaneous EEG–fMRI) during a mental arithmetic task that is interpreted as engaging working memory/attention (executive processes). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM99 and reports voxel coordinates and figures (Table 1, Fig. 5). The primary within-group contrast (mental arithmetic vs closed-eye rest) is reported and used for voxelwise inference. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion provided.

This is an empirical, task-based PET study that reports group-level, voxelwise task activation contrasts and whole-brain SPM results with stereotactic coordinates. Tasks include a Flexibility subtest (cognitive flexibility) and a Divided Attention subtest (vigilance/attentional control), both within established executive-function domains. The paper presents within-group contrasts (ethanol influx vs placebo, elimination vs placebo, influx vs elimination) analyzed via SPM (voxelwise, corrected thresholds) and reports coordinates/tables/figures. The full article contains introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging data).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control). Methods report whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses at the group level (averaged z-maps, thresholded Z maps, reported Talairach coordinates in Table 1). Within-group task contrasts are reported (incongruent vs. neutral, task vs. null), and results are provided as group-level statistical maps and peak coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an auditory go/nogo paradigm (response inhibition), which is an executive function domain. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain GLM analyses (nogo vs control) for each group, with thresholding and cluster reporting; although slice coverage is limited (10 slices), analyses are voxelwise and thus meet the ‘partial-brain allowed’ criterion. Within-group contrasts (nogo minus control) are explicitly reported for patients and controls; results are reported in the main text (locations, BAs, cluster extents), and clinical samples are included. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using a visuospatial working memory (DMTS) task, which falls within the executive function domain (working memory). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (permutation-based cluster inference) with coordinates and figures, and presents within-group task contrasts (activation during encoding and recognition at Time 1 and Time 2). Participants are human (healthy pre-menopausal women). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and tables of coordinates. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI task-based study of executive function (spatial working memory), satisfying I5 and I6. The authors performed whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (I7) and report within-group task contrasts (WM>AV and WM>PV) for both patients and controls (I8). Participant groups include a clinical schizophrenia sample and healthy controls, which are permissible (I9). Whole-brain results are described with coordinates, t-values and cluster information in the text/tables (I10). The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI task-based, whole-brain, within-group study in healthy adults, but the task (auditory temporal discrimination/time perception) does not fall within the review's required executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the paper discusses DLPFC and working-memory load, the paradigm is a perceptual timing task rather than a task explicitly within the specified executive function domains. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation contrasts (Predict vs Detect; Predict vs Detect 3-back; Detect 3-back vs Detect) analyzed with SPM and reported with coordinates and statistical thresholds. The paradigm involves prediction and an explicit manipulation of working memory load (1-back vs 3-back), which falls within the executive function domain (working memory/cognitive control). Within-group task contrasts are reported for healthy adult participants, and whole-brain results are presented in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using an established executive function task (verbal working memory; 0-back/2-back). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses including a within-group contrast of 2-back vs 0-back (one-sample t-test across all 21 participants) and tables/figures with coordinates. Results are reported at group level and satisfy the meta-analysis requirement for task activation maps. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function), with detailed methods and full results. It reports within-group task contrasts (delay-period activity vs baseline) and performs group-level, voxelwise analyses (spatial normalization-based group analysis with reported suprathreshold voxels and coordinates). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study that explicitly examines categorization processes that rely on executive resources (working memory, selective attention, response monitoring). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM with coordinates and thresholding, and includes within-group contrasts (e.g., early vs late training, stimulus-type analyses, task vs baseline) and a factorial condition × phase design. Participants are healthy young adults (eligible per I9). Results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

No exclusion criteria are explicitly met. Because key inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed from the provided content and full text is incomplete, the study must be excluded pending full text.

Full text appears incomplete (only title, abstract, and metadata provided). This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that investigates inhibitory control/cognitive control (effect of task-irrelevant motion on task performance and LPFC activity). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked BOLD results (MT+, LPFC, pOTS, angular gyrus) and within-group contrasts across coherence levels (e.g., 5% vs 0%, 10%, 20%). Results are presented in text and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting and within-group contrasts. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). The provided full text includes introduction, methods summary, results, and discussion; supplemental material is referenced. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is included in the meta-analysis.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of sentence comprehension and lexical ambiguity. It reports voxelwise, group-level activation maps (whole-brain-style analysis with partial slice coverage), and reports within-group contrasts (Ambiguous vs Unambiguous) and RSPAN correlations. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise group-level maps, albeit partial-brain acquisition), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 and I6 — the task is a language comprehension/lexical ambiguity paradigm rather than an explicit executive-function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility defined as the primary task). Although the paper discusses suppression, reanalysis, and working-memory correlations, the experimental manipulation is linguistic ambiguity resolution, not a task designed within established executive-function domains. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise, within-subject and group-level statistical maps (retention-delay vs baseline and comparisons to no-delay trials), with Talairach coordinates and corrected thresholding. Although slice coverage was limited dorsally, analyses were voxelwise (partial-brain acquisition allowed by criteria). Participants were healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract and metadata provided). Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I8) cannot be verified from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending full-text availability.

Full text reports an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (auditory n-back), a classic executive function task. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (mixed-model repeated-measures ANOVA with FDR correction and cluster threshold) and coordinates/tables/figures of task activation and interactions are provided. At least one within-group task contrast (activation vs control, and effects of working memory load) is reported. Participant groups (smokers and nonsmokers; adults) are acceptable. The article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

The study is an fMRI task study of working memory (meets I5, I6) and reports a within-group task contrast (activation vs control; meets I8) in healthy participants (meets I9). However, the abstract and provided text state that data were analyzed on the basis of manually defined anatomical regions-of-interest in each subject, indicating ROI-only analyses with no voxelwise, group-level statistical map described. Therefore it fails the whole-brain / voxelwise requirement (I7 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Full text is incomplete here (only abstract/metadata available), so this decision is based on the available abstract and lowers certainty.

The study is a PET activation experiment of passive and active recognition of one’s own face (facial identity recognition); it does not assess executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, set-shifting, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain PET voxelwise activations reported in task contrasts as described in the abstract), I8 (within-group task contrasts: P and A vs control), I9 (healthy volunteer participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (although PET was used, the paradigm does not assess executive function or cognitive control), I6 (tasks are face-recognition/sustained attention to self-face, not one of the specified executive domains). Exclusion criteria: none of E3–E6 apply. Full text appears incomplete here (only abstract/metadata provided), so fulltext_incomplete=true; this increases uncertainty but the available information is sufficient to conclude exclusion because the experimental task does not target executive functions.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study manipulating working memory load and attentional demand (executive function domain: working memory). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps, FDR-corrected) and multiple within-group task contrasts (e.g., load 3 vs. load 1; difficult vs. easy search; interactions). Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in the main text with tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain), with whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise, group-level statistical analyses (SPM5 random-effects contrasts). The paper reports within-group/task contrasts (e.g. main n-back effects, errors vs. corrects for all participants and for each group), provides peak coordinates and cluster-level inferences (tables/figures), and includes standard preprocessing and GLM modeling. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) with younger and older adult groups. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (GLM, stereotaxic transformation, voxelwise mixed-effects ANOVAs) and provides tables/figures of coordinates and contrasts (within-group sustained vs transient, task contrasts). At least one within-group task contrast is reported (task vs baseline and task differences), meeting the requirement for within-group voxelwise activation maps. The methods, results, and discussion are fully present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in schizophrenia. It reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses, provides within-group task contrasts (load levels > control; paired within-patient contrasts over time), and reports activation coordinates for these contrasts. The task (parametric verbal WM) clearly falls within executive function (working memory). Results are reported in standard coordinate tables/text and the full article includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study using a visual conditional delayed-response paradigm that probes working memory and action planning (executive functions). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM{F} maps), presents within-group contrasts (e.g., specific vs non-specific preparation; reward vs no-reward; interaction), and provides coordinates/tables of activation. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that assesses working memory (2-back) and episodic recognition — both within executive function domains. The manuscript reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (GLM/ANOVAs, voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction) and contrasts of task versus fixation and material-type contrasts (within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported). Participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable per inclusion rules. Results are described in text and include region/coordinate information and voxelwise statistical mapping procedures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective and is suitable for inclusion.

The study reports task-based fMRI assessing executive function (N-back working memory and attention tasks) with group-level voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain BOLD data were acquired and analyzed in SPM99; analyses include within-group contrasts (Two Back vs Zero Back and encoding vs rest) and report voxelwise results and Talairach coordinates. Participant groups include healthy controls (and clinical samples elsewhere) with within-group task contrasts reported. Although some medial temporal results used small-volume correction, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

Empirical task-based fMRI study of planning (an executive-function domain). Reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (SPM99) with cluster-level correction and provides coordinates/figures/tables. At least one within-group task contrast (planning and movement execution contrasted against four-move reference/baseline) is reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and not solely between-group contrasts).

The study is an empirical PET task-based study that examines visuospatial working memory and related cognitive control processes (I5, I6). The abstract reports group-level statistical analyses (ANCOVA and t statistics) with reported activation loci and task contrasts (immediate pointing vs detection; pointing to previous vs detection; immediate vs previous), which satisfy within-group voxelwise contrasts and whole-brain reporting (I7, I8, I10). Participants are healthy adults (within-group sample), so I9 is met. However, only the abstract and metadata are provided here; the full article (methods/results/discussion) is not present to fully verify analytic details (e.g., exact voxelwise maps, correction methods), so fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based Stroop paradigm probing conflict/error processing (executive function/inhibition). It reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (e.g., incongruent vs congruent; error vs correct) at the group (second) level, uses whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and conjunction analyses, and presents results in tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article reports an empirical, task-based fMRI study of conflict monitoring/cognitive control using the size-congruity paradigm (an executive-function conflict/inhibition task). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects; cluster results reported with corrected p'<0.05 and Talairach coordinates in Table 1), and multiple within-group contrasts (incongruent vs neutral, neutral vs congruent, etc.). Participants are a within-group sample (healthy students). Results are reported as tables/figures and described in the text. The paper also includes methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of task-based cognitive control/conflict resolution (executive function). It used within-subject, within-group contrasts (high vs low conflict resolution) and random-effects group-level voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain (exploratory FDR-corrected) analyses and voxelwise ROI-based analyses with reported coordinates are provided. Participants were healthy volunteers and behavioral and neural results are reported. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task-based executive function), I6 (cognitive control/conflict resolution within executive function), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses / whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group reported), and I10 (whole-brain results and coordinates described). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (selective attention/conflict resolution) using a cued global/local task. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (one-way repeated-measures ANOVA to define dACC ROI and planned voxelwise t-contrasts), within-group task contrasts (incongruent vs congruent targets; cue-only vs cue-plus-target), and reports whole-brain coordinates and figures. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is present. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical PET task-based study reporting task-evoked cerebral activations for the Perceptual Maze Test (PMT). The PMT involves visually guided motor planning and rule-following, which map onto the executive domain of planning/cognitive control. The abstract reports extensive bilateral activations and deactivations from group-level PET analyses comparing PMT to motor control (SHAM) and rest, indicating within-group, voxelwise task contrasts and whole-brain results described in the text. Participants are healthy volunteers, which is an acceptable sample. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for imaging modality (PET), task domain (planning/executive), whole-brain voxelwise analyses, within-group contrasts, and reporting format. Note: the provided content appears to be limited to title/abstract/metadata (no full methods/results/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study explicitly investigating 'refreshing' as a minimal executive function. It reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects contrasts (e.g., Refresh > Repeat; Face > Scene) derived from whole-brain EPI volumes and describes locations and statistics of activations. The design includes within-group task contrasts, healthy adult participants, and comprehensive methods/results/discussion sections. Results are reported in the main text with ROI and whole-brain analyses. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI experiment that directly investigates cognitive control/executive processes during temporal context retrieval and ordering. It meets I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive/cognitive control), I6 (tasks involve working memory/strategic ordering, response selection and monitoring — established executive domains), I7 (group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects SPM2 analyses with reported coordinates and tables), I8 (multiple within-group task contrasts, e.g., recency>ordering, stimulus and response number manipulations), I9 (healthy adult participants — acceptable participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described in text). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and Tables, so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the antisaccade task examining cognitive control/inhibition. It reports group-level, voxelwise GLM contrasts (e.g., correct antisaccade vs prosaccade; correct antisaccade vs errors) with whole-brain statistical maps (cluster correction) despite limited slice coverage, which meets the partial-brain allowance. Within-group task contrasts are explicitly reported and results are presented in text, figures, and tables. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) using task-based paradigms (auditory and visual temporal sequencing and comparison). Group-level, voxelwise analyses are reported via ST-PLS and nonrotated ST-PLS with tables of local maxima and hemodynamic response profiles, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Within-group task contrasts and task-by-modality effects are explicitly analyzed (including separate within-group ST-bPLS for FAST and SLOW groups and main effects of modality and task), meeting the requirement for within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (acceptable per criteria). Results are reported as coordinates and voxelwise patterns in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and empirical with original data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based PET study of executive/cognitive control processes (controlled semantic retrieval, monitoring) using within-subject contrasts (semantic vs syllable; degraded vs clear) in healthy adults. Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses were performed in SPM99 with corrected thresholds and reported peak coordinates and statistical maps. Results include within-group task contrasts and whole-brain figures/tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full article text provided (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied.

The study reports a PET task-based investigation of random number generation versus a control counting task, which is an executive function paradigm involving response suppression and selection. The abstract describes group-level task contrasts (RNG relative to COUNT) with reported regional activations across the whole brain (DLPFC, anterior cingulate, parietal cortex, cerebellum), indicating voxelwise task-evoked results. Therefore it appears to meet inclusion criteria for modality (I5), task domain (I6), within-group task contrast (I8), whole-brain voxelwise evidence (I7), applicability to any participant group (I9), and acceptability of reporting format (I10). However, only title/abstract/metadata are provided here (full text not supplied), so I cannot fully verify methods/analyses or confirm voxelwise maps in the full text; hence fulltext_incomplete=true and confidence is moderate.

This is an fMRI task study with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts (meets I7, I8), healthy adult participants (meets I9), and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (meets I10). However, the experimental tasks primarily probe visuospatial perception, motion extrapolation and temporal estimation rather than established executive function domains specified by the review (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Although the discussion invokes working memory and ‘‘planning’’ processes as interpretations, the tasks do not manipulate or operationalize an executive function domain explicitly (no classic working memory load, inhibition, set-shifting, or planning manipulation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 and I6 and should be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (delayed response tasks), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level analyses (random-effects/map-wise) and within-group task contrasts (item-order vs reordering, memory-load effects, task-period contrasts), with results described in the main text and figures/tables. Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults. Although ROI analyses are emphasized, the methods and results describe map-wise random-effects analyses consistent with voxelwise group-level task-evoked maps. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (visuospatial working memory/attention shifting) that reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and coordinates. The paper includes within-group contrasts (Rotation+Arrow, Rotation, Arrow vs baseline), random-effects group analyses, reported clusters and Talairach coordinates, and SEM connectivity as supplementary analyses. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. Partial slice coverage (20 slices) is acceptable per criteria as voxelwise analyses were performed and reported.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses (group-level contrasts) and within-group task contrasts contrasting criterion-attribute (CA) and family-resemblance (FR) categorization. The tasks explicitly involve rule maintenance and working-memory processes (authors report prefrontal ‘rule maintenance in working memory’ and attentional control), which fall within an established executive function domain (working memory/cognitive control). Whole-brain results are reported in tables and figures and the methods describe voxelwise SPM analysis. Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion) so inclusion is appropriate for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a Sternberg verbal working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses (encoding, maintenance, retrieval, and load contrasts), provides whole-brain activation maps, coordinates in tables and figures, and uses within-group task contrasts (high vs low load and phase-specific contrasts). Acquisition was adequate (voxelwise analyses performed; partial-brain coverage allowed by criteria). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study using a task that clearly engages executive functions (working memory, short-term maintenance, retrieval, comparison and decision making). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise contrasts (e.g., P2 vs P1, P1 vs spheres) using whole-brain coverage and provides peak coordinates and corrected statistical thresholds across subjects. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based whole-brain activation studies of executive function.

This fMRI study does not assess executive function or cognitive control tasks within established executive domains. Although it reports whole-brain, within-group voxelwise contrasts (introspection vs slow categorization; rapid vs slow categorization) in healthy participants and provides coordinate-based results, the experimental tasks are sensory categorization and self-introspection about emotional responses rather than working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant groups acceptable), I10 (results reported in maps/coordinates). Exclusion criteria met: none (does not meet E3–E6). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical PET study using a task-based paradigm that assesses working memory (digits forward/backward), an established executive function domain. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (SPM contrasts, voxel-level thresholds) including within-group contrasts (DF vs control, DB vs control, DF vs DB, and parametric linear contrasts). Whole-brain results are reported and pooled across participants; analyses satisfy voxelwise group-level reporting. Participants are healthy adults (within acceptable participant groups). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of analogical reasoning that explicitly manipulates working memory and abstract relational integration (an executive process). It reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (e.g., ANA>CAT, ANA>SEM) analyzed with SPM99 and provides coordinates, figures, and ROI analyses. At least one within-group task contrast is reported (direct task vs control contrasts). Participants are healthy adults (within-group results reported). Thus the paper satisfies all inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI, falls within executive domains via working memory/relational reasoning, whole-brain voxelwise analyses, within-group contrasts, and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed-saccade/working-memory task (meets I5 and I6). The paper reports within-group task contrasts and parameter estimates (task > baseline) and subject-level statistical parametric maps, satisfying I8, I9, and I10. However, the reported analyses focus on anatomically constrained ROIs (FEF and IPS) with voxel selection conducted within those structural masks and group results are reported as ROI-averaged parameter estimates/time series. The full text does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (or clearly state any group-level voxelwise SPM), and the primary results are ROI-based. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI/limited-volume analyses with no voxelwise group map) and fails to meet inclusion criterion I7. On that basis it must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed face recognition (working memory) task in healthy adults that reports within-group task contrasts (match vs nonmatch) and performs whole-brain, group-level random effects voxelwise analyses (t maps normalized to Talairach space, thresholded). The task falls within the executive function domain (working memory/cognitive control). The full text includes introduction, methods (subjects, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), results (ROI and whole-brain random effects), and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group contrasts, is empirical).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study (1.5T) that examines neural responses to infrequent target stimuli (oddball) and interprets them in terms of working memory/attention processes. It reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (spatially normalized, group-averaged segments with voxelwise thresholding) despite limited slice coverage (partial-brain), and shows within-group task effects (target-synchronized activations vs randomly synchronized control/implicit baseline). Results are reported in text and figures. Participants are neurologically normal adults. Thus all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function fMRI (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because imaging modality does not meet I5: the activation results are from 99mTc-HMPAO SPECT (not fMRI or PET). Although the study includes an executive-function task (phonological verbal fluency) and reports voxelwise group SPM analyses with within-group contrasts, the meta-analysis inclusion criterion I5 specifically requires fMRI or PET task-based studies. FDG-PET was obtained but the reported activation contrast was performed with HMPAO-SPECT, and no task-based PET activation map is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (executive task), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrast), I9 (participant groups allowed), I10 (whole-brain results reported in text). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (modality). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study that directly assesses cognitive control processes (belief-bias/inhibition during deductive reasoning). It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses (SPM, random-effects) with corrected thresholds and reports peak coordinates. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., reasoning vs baseline; belief-laden vs belief-neutral; correct vs incorrect inhibitory trials). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts present). Results are reported in text/tables with coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study that includes a short-term verbal working memory (STM-W) task and contrasts isolating syntactic re-analysis and working memory load (GP–NGP, SEN–MEM). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (cluster-corrected) and provides within-group task contrasts (SEN–MEM, GP–NGP, GP–CTRL, etc.). Participants are healthy adults. Whole-brain results are presented in the text and figures. Thus the study meets criteria for task-based executive function (working memory) assessment, whole-brain voxelwise analysis, and within-group contrasts required for inclusion.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive control (Preparing to Overcome a Prepotent Response) comparing RED vs GREEN conditions. It directly assesses inhibition/cognitive control (an accepted executive domain). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise F-maps and cluster-thresholded group-level statistical maps and provides tables of coordinates and figures. There is a group-level within-task contrast (condition × scan effects and main condition effects reported across the pooled sample and described as cue- and probe-related RED>GREEN activations), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task activation map. Results are reported as voxelwise maps and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain). The authors report voxelwise group-level activation maps analyzed with SPM (thresholded at p<.001, Z>3.1) and describe whole-brain activated regions (even though acquisition used 20 slices, partial-brain coverage is allowed). The primary contrasts are within-group task vs fixation/control for verbal and visual working memory, fulfilling a within-group task contrast requirement. Participants are human healthy adults. Results are reported in the main text (regions and counts) and meet the requirement that whole-brain results be clearly described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI with a within-group task contrast (task vs rest) and voxelwise whole-brain analysis (SPM) reporting activation foci and Talairach coordinates. The task examines initiation/programming of repetitive movements, which maps onto the executive domain 'initiation' in inclusion criteria. Partial-brain (9-slice) acquisition is used but analyses are voxelwise and reported, which meets I7. Healthy control group within-group contrasts are reported (I8/I9). Results are presented as tables of coordinates and figures (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it’s empirical). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of reasoning/problem solving that engages executive processes (relational integration, working memory and planning). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99 linear-trend and subtraction contrasts) including within-group task versus rest and parametric contrasts, with results described in tables/figures and detailed methods, sample (healthy adults), and complete results and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete — only title/abstract and metadata provided. From the abstract, this is an event-related fMRI study of conflict monitoring (meets I5) using an interference task within executive function domain (meets I6). The abstract also describes contrasts between congruent and conflicting conditions, implying a within-group task contrast (I8). However, the provided content does not include methods or results sufficient to confirm that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analysis or maps/coordinates were reported (I7 cannot be verified). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are apparent from the abstract. Because I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise group analysis) is a required inclusion criterion and cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article (recommend obtaining full text to reassess).

This is a task-based PET study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group contrasts relevant to executive processes. The M_SEQ condition explicitly probes spatial working memory and sequence learning (an executive domain), and the paper reports SPM voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates and contrasts (M_SEQ–M_PRED, M_ROT–M_PRED, M_PRED–S). Participants are a within-group sample of healthy adults and within-group task contrasts are provided. Reporting includes group-level statistical maps and coordinates. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5 (PET task-based), I6 (task involves working memory/executive demands), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise SPM), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (within-group healthy adult sample qualifies), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and described). No exclusion criteria apply.

The provided content appears to be an abstract/summary rather than the full article (introduction, full methods, results, figures/tables, coordinates). Therefore fulltext_incomplete=true. Based on the available text: met inclusion criteria: I5 (fMRI, task-based study), I6 (investigates motor planning — falls under ‘planning’ domain), I8 (within-group task contrasts and parametric modulation reported), I9 (participant group present). Not verifiable from the incomplete text: I7 (cannot confirm that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical map was reported or that coverage was whole-brain), I10 (cannot confirm whether voxelwise results/coordinates or maps are reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met from the abstract alone. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and I10) cannot be confirmed from the truncated/fulltext-absent content, I exclude the study pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive function (abstract reasoning/sequencing). It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain contrasts (e.g., R>Rc, R>M) with FDR-corrected maps and tables of coordinates, and includes anatomically defined ROI analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical PET activation study using O-15-water that contrasts sustained and divided attention in Alzheimer patients and healthy elderly (task-based paradigm). The abstract reports voxel-by-voxel t statistics after stereotactical normalization (i.e., whole-brain, voxelwise analyses) and describes within-group task activations for both controls and Alzheimer patients (task vs baseline/contrast yielding activated and deactivated regions). Tasks map onto established executive domains (sustained attention = vigilance; divided attention involves cognitive control). Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Note: only title/abstract/metadata are provided here — the full article text (introduction/methods/results/discussion) is not present in the supplied content, so fulltext_incomplete is set to true.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain). It reports group-level, voxelwise GLM analyses and thresholded activation maps (e.g. HIGH>LOW, ORG>HIGH, ORG>LOW) with whole-brain normalization and cluster thresholds, and presents within-group task contrasts and corresponding tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults; results include voxelwise activation maps and timecourses; beta-series functional connectivity is supplementary. The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that probes memory for a temporally encoded interval using an encoding–delay–recall (pacing–delay–continuation) paradigm. The task involves working-memory–like maintenance of temporal information (explicitly invoking prefrontal–parietal working memory networks). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses are reported (AFNI random-effects ANOVA, coordinates/tables/figures provided). Within-subject/task contrasts (Pattern, Task, Delay; pacing vs continuation; main effects and interactions) are presented. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (working memory) in postmenopausal women. The paper reports voxelwise (voxel-by-voxel) group-level analyses and contrast maps (whole-brain/voxelwise), includes within-group task contrasts for encoding/storage/retrieval versus baseline and reports condition (estrogen vs placebo) effects and task effects. Full article (methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a delayed-response working memory task (an established executive function domain) with emotional and neutral distractors. It reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level analyses (voxel-wise t maps, thresholds, Talairach coordinates, activation tables/figures) comparing task conditions (emotional vs neutral vs scrambled), satisfying the requirement for a within-group task contrast. Participant sample (healthy females) is acceptable. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and provides whole-brain coordinate-based results and figures, so full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This fMRI study reports within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts relevant to executive processes: Experiment 2 includes a Selection vs No-Selection delay contrast (controlled lexical selection) and a Go vs No-Go contrast (inhibition), both analyzed at the group level with voxelwise thresholds and reported coordinates/tables. Imaging methods and random-effects group analyses are described; results include whole-brain/voxelwise maps (tables and figures) though slice coverage varied across runs (partial-brain acquisition noted). Thus the study supplies task-based fMRI evidence for cognitive control domains (selection/initiation and inhibition) and meets the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI empirical study of executive function (attentional control/set-shifting) using a task-based paradigm. It reports within-group, voxelwise group-level contrasts (e.g., extradimensional vs intradimensional shifts, reversals vs set changes) and also presents unconstrained whole-brain analyses (FDR-corrected) and ROI results. The sample (16 healthy volunteers) is a within-group participant set and multiple within-group task contrasts are reported. Whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that probes executive-function–relevant processes (monitoring, response selection/suppression, planning) during cooperative and competitive game play. The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, whole-brain group-level contrasts (cooperation vs independent; competition vs independent; direct contrasts) analyzed with SPM and reports regional activations/tables, satisfying requirements for whole-brain voxelwise results and coordinate reporting. Participants are healthy adults (within eligible participant groups). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based cognitive inhibition paradigm (novel number-order task) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation contrasts. The paper reports within-group task contrasts (backward vs motor control; backward vs forward; forward vs motor control) for combined subjects and separately for men and women, and provides detailed methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Task falls within executive function domain (inhibition). Although slice coverage was limited to 16 near-axial planes, analyses were voxelwise and group-level, satisfying partial-brain allowance. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly examines response inhibition/proactive control (an executive function). The paper reports an event-related whole-brain group-level, voxelwise contrast (mixed-block no-cue vs. pure-block no-cue) using a one-sample t-test and provides coordinates/cluster results (Table 1) and statistical thresholds. The task and analyses include within-group task contrasts, use whole-brain voxelwise statistics, and the participant sample is an acceptably described healthy adult group. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study reporting within-group, voxelwise task activation contrasts examining endogenous vs exogenous orienting and inhibition of return (IOR). It uses whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group-level ANOVA, voxelwise t tests with cluster correction) and reports coordinates/tables and figures. The paradigm includes an inhibitory component (IOR), which falls under the review’s ‘inhibition’ executive-function domain. At least one within-group contrast (e.g., endogenous facilitation vs exogenous facilitation; IOR vs endogenous) is reported. Participant details and methods are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that examines visual short-term memory (VSTM), which falls under the working memory domain of executive function. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected maps and ROI supplementary analyses), includes within-group task contrasts (K-weighted and set-size regressors; set-size-specific contrasts), and presents whole-brain results in text, figures, and tables. Participants are healthy adults, satisfying participant inclusion. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI task study that reports whole-brain, voxelwise group- and within-group contrasts for task conditions. The decision-making/feedback-learning task engages executive processes (learning, working memory, error monitoring/decision-making), and analyses include within-group contrasts (gains vs losses, early vs late phases) reported via SPM voxelwise ANOVAs and coordinate tables. Whole-brain voxelwise results are presented, and qualifying contrasts are reported for both patient and control groups. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met.

This article reports an fMRI task-based experiment that directly probes working memory for kinesthetic movement information (an executive function domain). The paper reports within-group, voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses (parametric contrasts for movement encoding and delay/maintenance), with whole-brain voxelwise maps and cluster correction; results are presented in tables, figures and described in text. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study that used a task-based paradigm probing working memory and anticipatory aspects of decision making (executive functions). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise analyses (SPM99) including within-group contrasts (activation vs rest) for both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients, with tables/figures and coordinate reporting. Although slice coverage began mid-temporal lobes and moved upward (partial-brain acquisition), analyses were voxelwise and reported at the group level. All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the provided full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based paradigm assessing working memory (an executive function domain) in both schizophrenic patients and healthy controls (I5, I6, I9). The authors report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with statistical maps and tables of peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying voxelwise reporting even though slice coverage was partial (I7, I10). At least one within-group task contrast is reported (task activation vs. rest/delays) for each group (I8). No exclusion criteria are triggered: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and within-group contrasts are provided (exclusion criteria E3–E5 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment with group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group contrasts (meets I7, I8), includes eligible participant groups (I9), and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures (I10). However, the experimental tasks are phonological (final consonant discrimination and rhyming) and are designed to investigate phonological processing and sensory/linguistic mechanisms rather than to assess core executive function domains. Although the authors discuss working-memory/monitoring contributions, the tasks do not fall within established executive function domains (working memory paradigms such as n-back, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) in the sense required by the meta-analysis. Therefore the study fails to meet I5 (task assesses executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task falls within established executive domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of healthy adults that directly probes set-shifting/divergent problem solving and related executive processes. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (random-effects, multiple-comparison correction) with coordinates and contrasts (Match Problems vs baseline; Successful vs Unsuccessful; parametric within-group analyses), satisfying requirements for within-group task contrasts and voxelwise activation maps. The task maps onto executive domains (cognitive flexibility/set shifting and working memory). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study probing working memory during linguistically cued spatial and nonspatial judgments. It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 random-effects), including within-group task contrasts (Space>Nonspace, Nonspace>Space and All>Baseline), parametric within-subject and between-subject modulation analyses, and provides tables of coordinates and figures. Participants are human healthy adults.
