Therefore it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (working memory domain), I7 (voxelwise whole-brain analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts reported), I9 (acceptable participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI event-related study of covert spatial attention (Posner-like cueing) focusing on anticipatory spatial bias in posterior cingulate and mPFC. It does NOT assess executive function or cognitive control as specified by the review (I5) and the task does not clearly fall within the specified executive-function domains (I6); therefore it fails key inclusion criteria. It DOES satisfy I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts such as V+ vs ND and V+ vs V−), I9 (within-group contrasts in a healthy participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results described in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly investigates conflict/response-selection processes (goal-selection conflict) — a form of executive control/inhibition. The experiment uses within-group, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM99) with reported group-level contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; symbolic vs spatial), thresholded and reported as statistical maps and tables of coordinates. Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are provided. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task of executive/cognitive control), I6 (task involves response selection/conflict, an executive/inhibition domain), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (eligible participant group), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in maps/tables). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of mood induction (happy/sad) using emotional face stimuli and a gender-discrimination control; it does not assess executive functions per the meta-analysis definition. Although it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group task contrasts, the experimental tasks do not fall within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails primary inclusion criteria I5 and I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study that directly examines language switching, reporting within-group task contrasts (language switching vs non-switching; forward vs backward switching) and implicating executive-control processes (inhibition/cognitive flexibility). It uses whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses with tables/figures of coordinates and thresholds, and reports behavioral and imaging results for a defined participant group. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References).

The study is an empirical PET task-based neuroimaging study that includes working-memory tasks (1-back, 2-back, random-number generation), which fall within established executive function domains. The authors report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM99 and task PLS, and provide within-group task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs reading baseline, cued recall vs cued word retrieval). Participants are healthy adult subjects. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses event-related fMRI to investigate spatial attention and visual processing (attentional facilitation/inhibition), not executive-function cognitive control tasks. It therefore does not meet inclusion criteria I5/I6 (not an executive function task as defined). While the study includes within-group task contrasts (I8), reports participant groups (I9), and presents results in figures/text (I10), it does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map and instead analyzes ROI/retinotopically-defined early visual cortex probe representations and extracted event-related timecourses (violating I7). This amounts to ROI-restricted analyses rather than the required voxelwise whole-brain map, meeting exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete.

This empirical study reports task-based fMRI results from an auditory oddball (target detection) paradigm, which maps onto the executive domain of vigilance/sustained attention. It includes group-level, voxelwise fMRI analyses (SPM2 one-sample voxelwise t-test, thresholded P<0.001 corrected) and explicitly reports a within-group contrast (targets vs. standards) with whole-brain activation maps and coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study using a task-based paradigm that probes response inhibition/error processing (Error Awareness Task), which falls squarely within executive function (inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests of event-related activation maps vs baseline) and presents coordinate tables and cluster results. Within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., Aware errors, Unaware errors, Stops, Oddball vs baseline and Aware vs Unaware ROI comparisons). Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10), and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and references).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an executive function (inhibition). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (one-sample t test of Go/NoGo vs Go; between-group ANOVA with small-volume correction) and provides coordinate tables and figures for activation maps. A within-group task contrast (Go/NoGo vs Go) is explicitly reported. Participants are healthy adult males (acceptable per I9). The full text contains background, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of response inhibition (GO/NOGO), an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps (one-sample and between-group t tests) and within-group contrasts (high vs low conflict condition), and describes results at the group/voxel level with coordinates and cluster reports. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and figures/tables descriptions, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a whole-brain, task-based fMRI study reporting group-level voxelwise within-group contrasts (R>NR, A>NA) with coordinates and full methods/results, its primary aim and paradigm target semantic memory/object-recall rather than an established executive function domain. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (voxelwise whole-brain results reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control — it is a semantic memory study), I6 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation; although some recruited regions relate to control, the paradigm was designed to probe semantic object recall). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study reporting within-group, voxelwise, group-level activation maps and Talairach coordinates for cognitive tasks. The four-choice reaction time (4CRT) involves planning/cognitive control (an executive domain), and the paper provides whole-brain voxelwise results (group activation maps, tables of coordinates) and within-group task versus rest contrasts. The full text contains methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is original human imaging data). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using working memory paradigms (auditory/visual temporal sequencing and comparison), which fall under executive function (working memory). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (spatiotemporal PLS with singular images and local maxima), including within-group task contrasts (experimental vs control; modality and task-demand contrasts). Results (activation and connectivity) are reported across the brain and summarized with local maxima and hemodynamic response profiles. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports within-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory/selective attention (executive function). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The study reports within-group, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Remember/Ignore vs Passive View) using random-effects analyses and thresholded whole-brain maps and MNI coordinates (tables/figures). It uses a working memory/selective attention paradigm (executive domain), reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and provides within-group contrasts and coordinate tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that examines feedback processing and learning, engaging executive processes (working memory, cognitive control/conflict) and reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (SPM2 one-sample t-tests) with tables of MNI coordinates. Multiple within-group task contrasts are reported (e.g., gains vs losses, exploratory vs proficiency phases), and results are presented across methods, results, and discussion. Participants are a healthy adult group (female). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that directly contrasts memory-guided saccadic sequences (New and Familiar) against rest and against each other. The memory-guided (M) condition requires spatial working memory and sequence planning, which falls within the executive function domain of working memory/cognitive control. The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; Z-thresholds, Talairach normalization) and provides within-group task contrasts (New > Rest, Familiar > Rest, New > Familiar). Participants are a within-group healthy adult sample. Results are reported in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Paced Visual Serial Addition Task (PVSAT), which probes executive functions (working memory, sustained attention). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM99 analyses (within-group contrasts of PVSAT vs rest) for both patients and controls, with activation clusters/Brodmann areas, Z-scores and cluster sizes reported in text/figures/tables. Partial supratentorial slice coverage is used but voxelwise whole-brain/group analyses are presented, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not meet the core inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis: I5 (fMRI/PET assessing executive function) and I6 (task falls within established executive function domains). Although the paper includes an fMRI experiment with group-level voxelwise analysis (satisfying I7) and a within-group task contrast (satisfying I8), and uses an eligible participant group (I9), the fMRI task (self-paced dot writing) is a motor/self-paced task and not an executive-function/cognitive-control paradigm. The intracerebral recording task that manipulates executive load (writing a different letter) was not performed with fMRI or PET, so it cannot be used for the meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI, task-based, whole-brain, within-group study of spatial attention (endogenous/exogenous orienting). It meets I7 (reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and coordinates), I8 (reports within-group task contrasts: cue vs neutral), I9 (healthy adult participant group qualifies), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text). However, it does not meet I6: the tasks (spatial orienting/involuntary vs voluntary attention) do not fall within the specified executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) required by the meta-analysis objective. Thus it fails the domain inclusion criterion and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based verbal fluency (silent word generation) paradigm that falls within executive function domains (initiation/working verbal fluency). The paper reports voxelwise whole-brain fMRI analyses (FuncTool and SPM99) with group-level activation maps (e.g., left inferior frontal gyrus activation thresholded and shown), and reports within-group task contrasts (silent word generation vs number listing baseline) for young and aged participant groups. Results are presented in methods, results, figures and discussion, and the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses of task-evoked activity during motor imagery and visual imagery tasks. The tasks probe movement planning (an executive domain: planning/initiation of action), include within-group contrasts (e.g., MI > VI, rotation-related effects), and report whole-brain results (SPM99 random-effects analysis; coordinates and cluster results provided). Participant groups include clinical (CFS) and healthy controls but within-group task contrasts are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full article appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is EXCLUDED because it does not primarily assess an executive function or cognitive-control task as required by I5/I6. This is a visuomotor sequence/force-tracking motor-learning study addressing automaticity and sensorimotor control; although it discusses prefrontal involvement, the task is not within the specified executive domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts vs matched rest/perceptual baseline), I9 (healthy participant group within-group contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain results described in text/figures/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not target executive function/cognitive control per review definition), I6 (task does not fall within listed executive domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

Exclusion IDs met: E4 and E5. This is a resting-state FDG-PET study that reports between-group contrasts (OCD vs controls) and voxelwise correlations between resting metabolism and neuropsychological scores, but it does not include any task-based imaging or within-group task activation contrasts.
Inclusion IDs met: I6 (the behavioral/neuropsychological tests administered assess executive function domains) and I10 (results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise analyses in the text/tables).
Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no fMRI or PET task-based paradigm; PET was performed at rest), I7 (no task-evoked voxelwise statistical maps), I8 (no within-group task contrast reported).
Because the meta-analysis requires task-evoked, within-group activation maps, and this study only reports resting-state metabolic contrasts/correlations, it fails required inclusion criteria and violates exclusion criteria E4 and E5. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical PET study using task-based paradigms that probe executive functions (notably cognitive flexibility/set-shifting via response reversal and concurrent-discrimination with random pairing). It reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses using SPM with voxel thresholds and corrected inference, provides within-group task contrasts (e.g., recognition vs concurrent discrimination with fixed pairing; reversal vs recognition; fixed vs random pairing), and reports coordinates/regions of activation. Participants are healthy adults. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study reporting within-group, task-evoked contrasts that probe motor intention/motor planning. The task probes selection and preparation of actions (motor planning/intention), which maps onto the executive domain of planning. The study reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (cluster-level corrected) and provides stereotactic coordinates for activations (e.g., left SMG), satisfying requirements for voxelwise reporting. Multiple within-group contrasts (MC>NC, MC>SC, conjunctions, parametric analyses) are reported. Participants are healthy adults and group-level maps are presented. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (delayed face-recognition) — an established executive function domain — using whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise GLM analyses. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (delay-period VOIs identified from t-maps) and within-group contrasts (e.g., memory-present/distraction-present vs memory-absent/distraction-present; memory-present/distraction-absent), in a sample of healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (antisaccade task), which is an established executive function (inhibition). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps and voxelwise ANOVA results (corrected maps and exploratory whole-brain contrasts), and presents within-group task contrasts (task vs implicit baseline and correct vs error within groups). Participants include developmental groups (children, adolescents, adults), and results are reported in figures/tables in the full text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of antisaccade and refixation saccades that directly assesses inhibitory control (an executive function). The full text reports group-level, voxelwise random-effects t maps (whole-brain voxelwise analyses with standard-space normalization and cluster-thresholding) and presents within-group contrasts (refixation vs fixation; antisaccade vs refixation) for both normal and schizophrenia groups. Participants include clinical and control samples and within-group activation contrasts are reported in the text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and it is an empirical neuroimaging study). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence it meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of antisaccade/prosaccade performance (inhibition domain), reporting voxelwise, group-level random-effects analyses and coordinates (MNI). The study includes within-group contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; saccades vs fixation) and whole-brain voxelwise SPM results, plus ROI checks; acquisition and voxelwise analyses are described in detail. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that identifies prefrontal activation related to executive control demands during a speeded lexical decision task. The study (1) uses fMRI (whole-brain BOLD acquisition) and reports voxelwise group-level activation maps and cluster coordinates; (2) demonstrates involvement of domain-general executive processes (inhibition/behavioral monitoring) in resolving neighborhood-size effects; (3) includes within-group contrasts (lexicality, neighborhood size, their interaction, and parametric analyses); (4) tests healthy adult participants; and (5) reports whole-brain results in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion requirements.

Full text provided is incomplete: HTML contains only meta tags and no article content (no introduction, methods, results, or discussion). Therefore I cannot verify any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / cannot be confirmed: I5 (cannot confirm this is an fMRI/PET task-based study), I6 (cannot confirm tasks are within executive function domains), I7 (cannot confirm whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (cannot confirm a within-group task contrast is reported), I9 (cannot confirm participant groups or within-group contrasts), I10 (cannot confirm reporting of whole-brain results). Exclusion criteria met: none (cannot determine). Because core article content is missing, study is excluded from the review until a complete full text is available.

Full text provided appears to be limited to title, abstract, and metadata; core article (methods, full analyses, results, figures/tables) is not available. From the abstract the study is a PET task-based investigation of action planning (meets I5) and examines planning-related tasks (meets I6). The abstract reports differential activations across conditions, implying within-group task contrasts (meets I8) and participants were healthy volunteers (meets I9). However, I cannot confirm that a group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistical analysis was performed or that whole-brain results/coordinates are reported (I7 and I10 cannot be verified) because the full text and methods/results are missing. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because key inclusion criteria (I7 and/or I10) cannot be confirmed from the incomplete full text, the study is excluded pending availability of the complete article.

Although this is an fMRI study of an executive-control task (POP) with within-group contrasts (high vs. low load) in both young and older adults, the full text describes ROI-based time-series and mean % signal-change analyses mapped to Brodmann areas rather than reporting any group-level voxelwise, whole-brain statistical activation maps or coordinate tables/figures. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function), I6 (task falls within executive domains—attention/response selection/inhibition), I8 (within-group task contrast: high vs low load), I9 (participant groups qualify). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of voxelwise, whole-brain group-level statistical maps presented). Exclusion criterion met: E3 (study reports only ROI-based analyses with no voxelwise results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis because it lacks the required voxelwise whole-brain task activation results.

The article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in schizophrenia (I5, I6). The methods describe group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed- and random-effects) and report whole-brain activations with tables/figures/coordinates (I7, I10). Within-group contrasts (activation vs rest; mnemonic vs anticipatory task conditions) are reported for both patient and control groups (I8). Clinical participant groups are included and within-group contrasts are present (I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or non-empirical) apply.

The study uses an fMRI face-matching emotion-processing paradigm (fear/anger faces) targeting corticolimbic reactivity and connectivity, not an executive function or cognitive control task. Therefore it does NOT meet I5 (must be an fMRI/PET study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I6 (task must fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). It DOES meet I7 (reports voxelwise whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), I8 (reports a within-group task contrast: face-processing vs sensorimotor control), I9 (participant group acceptable — healthy adults), and I10 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not provide a group-level, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map (I7 not met). The paper reports individual-subject voxelwise t-maps and then performs group-wise statistics on voxel counts within manually segmented VOIs (an ROI-based group analysis) rather than presenting or analysing group-level voxelwise statistical maps. It is an fMRI task-based study of executive function (meets I5 and I6), includes within-subject task contrasts (search vs maintain and task vs rest) (I8), includes clinical participants (schizophrenia) (I9), and reports whole-brain acquisition and results in text/figures (I10). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because the meta-analysis requires at least one group-level voxelwise activation map (I7), the study cannot be included. Exclusion is based on failure to meet inclusion criterion I7.

This fMRI study investigates selective attention effects on action observation (left IFG) using an attentional load task, not an established executive function domain per I6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and ROI analyses reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts: High vs Low load), I9 (within-group contrasts in healthy adult sample), I10 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (tasks must fall within defined executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) — the primary manipulation concerns selective visual attention/action perception rather than a canonical executive control task. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on executive function task activations.

This is a task-based fMRI study that investigates voluntary suppression of negative affect via cognitive reappraisal, which engages cognitive control/inhibitory processes relevant to executive function. The paper reports voxelwise, group-level whole-brain SPM analyses (e.g., S > B, S > M, M > S), with coordinates and thresholds provided. Within-group contrasts are reported (Suppress vs Baseline, Suppress vs Maintain, Maintain vs Suppress). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for an executive-function/cognitive-control task with whole-brain, within-group voxelwise results.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (delayed-recognition) reporting within-group task effects of memory load. However, analyses are described as anatomically-defined ROI time-course analyses (mean time courses within SFG, MFG, IFG, IPS, FFG and subsets of voxels within those ROIs). There is no indication of a group-level, voxelwise/whole-brain statistical activation map reported in the provided text. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Additionally, the supplied full-text appears to be an abstract/summary rather than a complete article (missing full introduction/methods/discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=true. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task fMRI), I6 (working memory), I8 (within-group contrasts/load effects), I9 (acceptable participant group). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level voxelwise/whole-brain map). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (ROI-only analyses).

This is an event-related fMRI study that experimentally manipulates attention (overt and covert shifts) and the maintenance of attention (long variable delays with target-dimming detection), tapping sustained attention/vigilance. It reports group-level, voxelwise/surface-based statistical maps (whole-brain analyses with permutation correction) and peak MNI coordinates, and presents within-group task contrasts (shift- and maintenance-related activations vs baseline and paired contrasts). Participants are healthy adults and within-group contrasts are reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (task in executive domain: vigilance/sustained attention), I7 (whole-brain, voxelwise/surface statistical maps reported), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (participant group acceptable), and I10 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study with voxelwise, group-level analyses comparing continuation tapping with hand SHIFT vs NO-SHIFT (satisfying I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10). However, the paradigm is a motor timing/continuation tapping task focused on transfer of timing between hands and motor control; it does not clearly probe an established executive function domain (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that reports within-group voxelwise task contrasts implicating executive function. Evidence: (1) fMRI task paradigm explicitly targeting response selection/inhibitory control (Incompatible vs Compatible mapping) and a related Chocolate-Box task; (2) tasks fall within established executive domains (response selection/inhibition); (3) whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (individual-subject and random-effects group contrasts; peak activation tables and brain maps are provided); (4) at least one within-group task contrast is reported (Incompatible > Compatible; Belief > Photograph; Chocolate-Box contrasts); (5) participant group (healthy adults) is acceptable; (6) results are reported as coordinates and figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the classic identity negative priming task, which implicates inhibitory selective attention processes (an executive function domain: inhibition). The paper reports within-group voxelwise contrasts (repetition ignored vs control) at the group level, with both ROI (SVC) and an exploratory whole-brain voxelwise analysis described and thresholded. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task-based empirical study that reports voxelwise, whole-brain analyses of an executive function task (Hayling Sentence Completion Test — verbal initiation). The paper presents within-group contrasts (sentence completion vs rest and parametric difficulty contrasts) with cluster-corrected whole-brain results and MNI coordinates, satisfying reporting requirements. Participant group (subjects at high genetic risk for schizophrenia) is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI task-based study of attentional switching that probes executive functions (cognitive flexibility and inhibitory control). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM) with reported contrast maps and peak coordinates (e.g., object-switch vs rule-switch; combined switch vs nonswitch), and presents within-group task contrasts. Participant sample is a healthy volunteer group. Although some ventromedial signal dropout is noted, analyses were voxelwise and whole-brain contrasts are reported, and partial coverage does not disqualify the study per criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a task-based random number generation paradigm that probes executive functions (inhibition/cognitive flexibility). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM99 analyses (RNG minus counting) with thresholding, cluster counts and Talairach coordinates, and presents figures/tables of activation — satisfying voxelwise within-group task contrasts. Participants are healthy adults (within-group contrasts reported). All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) apply. Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, discussion and references.

This peer-reviewed study is a task-based fMRI experiment that examines goal-directed coherence-building and strategic inferencing, engaging cognitive control and executive processes (e.g., updating task representations, decision under uncertainty, strategy use). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and within-group task contrasts (e.g., closely related vs. distantly related; distantly related vs. unrelated). Healthy adult participants were tested. Results identify fronto-parietal regions (including the inferior frontal junction, dorsolateral/superior frontal and parietal areas) commonly implicated in executive function and cognitive control. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI task activations in executive domains. Methods/results are complete in the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) and voxelwise maps/coordinates are reported in tables/figures and described in text.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study of antisaccade performance, which probes inhibition (an executive function). The paper reports group-level voxelwise, whole-brain analyses (with correction thresholds) and explicitly presents within-group contrasts (e.g., antisaccades vs. prosaccades; combined saccade activation) and resulting activation maps and statistics in the text. Participant groups (unaffected siblings and controls) are acceptable. Whole-brain results are described in the manuscript. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task-based, experimental study of executive function (overt letter verbal fluency), reporting within-group voxelwise whole-brain group activation maps (verbal fluency vs word repetition) for healthy participants under placebo and ketamine. The paper includes full methods, results (main effect of task, main effect of drug, task×drug interactions), and reports coordinates/cluster results. It therefore meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

The article reports an empirical task-based fMRI study of an executive process ("refreshing"), satisfying executive-function domain criteria. The methods and results describe within-group task contrasts (refresh vs read; effects of number of active items) for young and older adults and report brain areas (e.g., left dorsolateral frontal cortex, anterior cingulate, left mid-ventral frontal cortex), consistent with whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses reported in the text. Thus inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. However, the provided content appears to be only the abstract/summary and not the full article (methods, full results, figures, supplements missing), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true; this reduces certainty but the available information is sufficient to include the study pending full-text confirmation.

This is a well-reported, whole-brain fMRI study with voxelwise group analyses and within-group task contrasts (Age > Colour) in both Alzheimer’s and control participants, and it reports coordinate results. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I8 (within-group task contrasts), I9 (clinical participant group acceptable), and I10 (coordinate reporting). However, the experimental tasks probe visuo-attentional/selective-attention processing (shallow colour vs deeper age judgements) rather than one of the specified executive-function domains listed in the inclusion criteria (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Because it does not meet I6, it must be excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text content provided is limited to title, abstract, and metadata; core article content (methods, full results, figures/tables) is not available. From the abstract we can confirm this is an fMRI task study addressing executive function during language tasks (meets I5 and I6) and reports condition contrasts in a healthy adult group (likely meeting I8 and I9). However, the full text is incomplete so we cannot verify that at least one group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical map was reported (I7) or that whole-brain results are reported as coordinates/figures as required (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E6) are clearly met. Because I7 (and I10) cannot be confirmed from the provided content, the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis at this time. Full text is incomplete.

This is an empirical H2(15)O PET study using a task-based paradigm (random number generation vs counting) that probes executive processes (inhibition/suppression of habitual counting, response selection, monitoring). The paper reports voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses with coordinates and statistical parametric maps for within-group contrasts (RNG vs COUNT) for both elderly controls and Parkinson’s disease patients, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Results are provided as tables of coordinates and figures, and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related task-based fMRI study that directly assesses executive control/vigilance and inhibition over emotional distraction in Major Depressive Disorder. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects group analyses (t maps, ANOVAs) and within-group task contrasts (targets, sad vs neutral distractors, Target-after-Sad vs Target-after-Neutral) for both patient and control groups. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI executive-function activation reporting (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI (I5) using an auditory oddball paradigm that indexes selective attention/vigilance and context updating (falls within executive domain 'vigilance' per I6). The fMRI analysis includes whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts (target vs non-target) with a reported whole-brain threshold (p<0.0001) and coordinates/tables (I7, I10). A within-group task contrast (target > non-target) is explicitly reported (I8). Participant groups are non-clinical but any participant group is acceptable (I9). The paper provides full methods, results and discussion (full text appears complete). None of the exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROI/SVC only (E3), not only connectivity/resting-state (E4), and report within-group activations rather than only between-group contrasts (E5); it is empirical human neuroimaging data (not E6). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that directly investigates cognitive processes underlying decision making and explicitly reports involvement of executive functions (DLPFC, ACC, parietal regions) during an information-integration task. It used a whole-brain, voxelwise analysis (SPM2) with group-level (second-level random-effects) within-group contrasts (A vs B, A vs C) and reports coordinates and corrected statistics. Participants are a within-group sample (healthy elderly). The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports structural MRI volumetry, neuropsychological testing, and a serotonergic (D-fenfluramine) challenge in personality-disordered offenders and controls. It does not report any task-based functional neuroimaging (no fMRI or PET task activations), no voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps, and no within-group task contrasts. Therefore it does not meet the requirements for inclusion in a meta-analysis of task-evoked executive-function activations. Exclusion criteria met: none of the listed exclusion criteria (E3–E6) strictly apply. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (no fMRI/PET task-based study), I6 (no task falling within executive function domains reported as a task-based neuroimaging paradigm), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), I8 (no within-group task contrast), I9 (no within-group task contrast reported for any group), I10 (no whole-brain results reported in coordinates/figures/tables). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (overt verbal fluency) reporting whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and within-group contrasts. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, with voxelwise statistics (SPM5) and FDR correction across the brain and coordinates/figures reported. Participant groups include healthy controls and schizophrenia patients. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.
